# Lumiose UI

> `@lumiose/ui`: accessible, unstyled UI primitives built on native elements (`<dialog>`, popover, invoker commands, CSS anchor positioning), server-rendered without hydration. Style them with your own CSS or the optional default theme.

These docs ship in `@lumiose/ui` and match the installed version: `node_modules/@lumiose/ui/docs`.
In a project that depends on it, `lumiose docs ui` prints the index and `lumiose docs dialog` a
component's page; the Lumiose MCP server's `ui_components` tool lists every component's parts,
props, events and styling hooks. The Lumiose docs: `node_modules/lumiose/docs/llms.txt`.

<!-- source: README.md -->

# UI components

> `@lumiose/ui`: accessible, unstyled UI primitives built on native elements (`<dialog>`, popover, invoker commands, CSS anchor positioning), server-rendered without hydration. Style them with your own CSS or the optional default theme.

**Status:** in development. `@lumiose/ui` keeps its own 0.x versions, apart from the version all
other Lumiose packages share, and is not on npm yet: today it is used from this repository's
workspace. The goal for its 1.0 is parity with [Base UI](https://base-ui.com)'s components; the
table below lists them as they land.

These pages ship in the package, in `node_modules/@lumiose/ui/docs`, so they match the installed
version, and the Lumiose site renders them with a live demo of each example at
[itsjavi.com/lumiose/ui](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/ui/). Start with [Installation](installation.md)
and [Theming](theming.md). For coding agents, `llms.txt` indexes them and `llms-full.txt` holds them all;
`lumiose docs ui` and `lumiose docs dialog` print them; the MCP server's `ui_components` tool lists
every component's parts, props, events and styling hooks; and `lumiose agents init` adds a UI
section to `AGENTS.md` and the `lumiose-ui` skill. Every component page has the same sections:
Anatomy, API, Example, Styling, Keyboard and focus, Without JavaScript, Browser support and Related.

## Approach

- **Native first.** A component renders the element the platform already has for the job: a
  `<dialog>` opened by an invoker command, a popover, a `<button>`. Those work in server HTML
  before any script loads, and keep the browser's own keyboard handling and focus management.
- **Custom elements only where the platform falls short.** Keyboard navigation in a menu or the
  filtering of a combobox need script: those components render a light-DOM custom element with a
  `lu-` tag (`lu-menu`, `lu-combobox`) that upgrades the server HTML in place. A page is meant to
  load only the definitions of the elements it renders, and no island runtime for them (in
  development, with those components).
- **Small scripts for native gaps.** Where a native element falls short of Base UI's behaviour, a
  small script closes the gap, such as Dialog's right-click and touch handling. The component
  still works without it; a page that renders the component loads it once, without the island
  runtime.
- **Parts.** Each component is a set of parts named as in Base UI (`Dialog.Root`,
  `Dialog.Trigger`, `Dialog.Popup`, …). Every part that renders an element takes that element's
  props (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, events) and passes them through.
- **Signals.** A component's state is a prop and a callback: `open` with `onOpenChange`, `checked`
  with `onCheckedChange`, `value` with `onValueChange`. Pass a signal's value and write it back in
  the callback to keep both in sync, or leave both out and the element keeps its own state. Custom
  elements report changes with lowercase DOM events, like native ones: `openchange`,
  `checkedchange` and `change`.
- **Keyboard contracts.** Every component follows its WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern, and
  its end-to-end tests check the keyboard paths.
- **WCAG 2.2 AA.** Every component meets it: the components own semantics, keyboard and
  behaviour, and the default theme owns the visual criteria (contrast, non-text contrast, focus
  visible, target size). Each component's end-to-end tests run axe with the WCAG A and AA rules,
  closed and open, in light and dark, and check reflow at 320 CSS pixels and text spacing.

This is the approach of [Timeless](https://timeless.build), ported to Lumiose.

## Styling

`@lumiose/ui` is **unstyled**: its stylesheets hold only what a component needs to work (display,
positioning and anchoring, the top layer, the CSS variables a component sets), in the `lu.core`
cascade layer. A look is opt-in: the default theme, or your own CSS. [Installation](installation.md)
shows the imports, and [Theming](theming.md) the layers, the theme's classes and custom properties,
and how to style the parts yourself.

### The default theme

`@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css` is a ready look for demos, prototypes and getting started: neutral
surfaces, a blue primary, light and dark. Its classes (`lu-button`, `lu-dialog`, …) and its `--lu-`
custom properties, named as in shadcn/ui, are listed in [Theming](theming.md#the-default-theme).

## Components

| Component                             | Status                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Dialog, alert dialog](dialog.md)     | Available: native `<dialog>`, works without JavaScript                                    |
| [Popover](popover.md)                 | Available: native popover, works without JavaScript                                       |
| [Tooltip](tooltip.md)                 | Available: native hint popover, opened by its script                                      |
| [Menu](menu.md)                       | Available: popover menu, opens without JavaScript                                         |
| [Combobox](combobox.md)               | Available: `<lu-combobox>`, a form control that filters its options                       |
| [Select](select.md)                   | Available: native `<select>`, customizable where supported, no script                     |
| [Tabs](tabs.md)                       | Available: server HTML with the full state, `<lu-tabs>` adds the keys                     |
| [Field](field.md)                     | Available: label, description, errors; native validation in the field                     |
| [Fieldset](fieldset.md)               | Available: native `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`, no script                                  |
| [Form](form.md)                       | Available: native `<form>`, a form action's errors in its fields                          |
| [Input](input.md)                     | Available: native `<input>`, no script                                                    |
| [Checkbox](checkbox.md)               | Available: native checkbox, indeterminate and read-only                                   |
| [Checkbox Group](checkbox-group.md)   | Available: checkboxes with one value and a parent checkbox                                |
| [Radio](radio-group.md)               | Available: native radios in a radiogroup fieldset                                         |
| [Switch](switch.md)                   | Available: native checkbox with the switch role                                           |
| [Collapsible](collapsible.md)         | Available: native `<details>`, works without JavaScript                                   |
| [Accordion](accordion.md)             | Available: native `<details>` items, `<lu-accordion>` adds the keys                       |
| [Toast](toast.md)                     | Available: server-rendered or from a manager, `<lu-toast-viewport>` times and closes them |
| [Button](button.md)                   | Available: native `<button>`, focusable when disabled                                     |
| [Toggle](toggle.md)                   | Available: `<button aria-pressed>`, pressed by the component in an island                 |
| [Toggle Group](toggle-group.md)       | Available: `<lu-toggle-group>` presses its toggles and moves focus                        |
| [Progress](progress.md)               | Available: native `<progress>`, indeterminate when unknown, no script                     |
| [Meter](meter.md)                     | Available: native `<meter>`, no script                                                    |
| [Slider](slider.md)                   | Available: native range inputs, `<lu-slider>` adds ranges and Page Up and Page Down       |
| [Number Field](number-field.md)       | Available: native number input, or a formatted spinbutton; press-and-hold buttons         |
| [Autocomplete](autocomplete.md)       | Available: free text with suggestions, on Combobox's `<lu-combobox>`                      |
| [OTP Field](otp-field.md)             | Available: one native input under visual slots; autofill, paste, validation natively      |
| [Preview Card](preview-card.md)       | Available: a link whose hover or focus opens a card; the link works without JavaScript    |
| [Toolbar](toolbar.md)                 | Available: `<lu-toolbar>`, one tab stop across buttons, links, inputs and toggles         |
| [Scroll Area](scroll-area.md)         | Available: native scrolling, custom scrollbars from `<lu-scroll-area>`                    |
| [Context Menu](context-menu.md)       | Available: Menu at the pointer, opened by its script (right-click, long press, keys)      |
| [Drawer](drawer.md)                   | Available: a Dialog against an edge, works without JavaScript; its script adds the swipe  |
| [Separator](separator.md)             | Available: native `<hr>`, horizontal or vertical, no script                               |
| [Avatar](avatar.md)                   | Available: an image over its fallback, `<lu-avatar>` follows its loading status           |
| [Menubar](menubar.md)                 | Available: Menus in a `role="menubar"`, `<lu-menubar>` moves between them                 |
| [Navigation Menu](navigation-menu.md) | Available: a `<nav>` whose triggers open panels of links, works without JavaScript        |

## Right to left

There is no direction provider: every component reads the direction from the page, the `dir`
attribute on `<html>` or on any container around it, when it acts (TASK-385). Right to left:

- **Arrow keys** that move along a row swap: Tabs, Toggle Group, Toolbar, Menubar, Navigation
  Menu, Accordion's and Menu's submenu keys, a Radio group (the browser's), Slider and Number
  Field's scrub area (leftward goes up).
- **Placement** follows logical sides and alignment: `inline-start` and `inline-end` sides, and
  `align="start"` or `"end"`, mirror; `left` and `right` sides stay physical, as in Base UI.
- **Sliders and scrollbars** run from the right: a Slider's track and Indicator, a Scroll Area's
  horizontal thumb, a Progress or Meter bar (the indeterminate segment slides leftward).
- **Swipes** are physical: a Toast or a Drawer swiped right goes right in either direction.
- **The theme** uses logical properties (`inset-inline-*`, `margin-inline-*`, `border-inline-*`),
  so it mirrors with no extra rule. A numeric OTP Field keeps its slots left to right, as digits
  read in right-to-left scripts too.

The theme avoids `:dir()`: Lightning CSS, which minifies production CSS, lowers it to a list of
`:lang()` selectors that misses a `dir` attribute. It uses `[dir="rtl"]` around the component
instead, or logical properties.

## Size

`@lumiose/ui` is opt-in, so its size is reported apart from the runtime's caps:
`pnpm --filter @lumiose/ui size` prints, per component, the JavaScript a server-rendered page loads
for its custom elements, the JavaScript an island that uses it loads, and its CSS (minified, gzip
and brotli).

## Related

- [Web components](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/guides/web-components/): custom elements in Lumiose pages and islands.
- [Islands](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/islands/): where components run in the browser.
- [JSX](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/jsx/): `class`, events and `on:`.

<!-- source: installation.md -->

# Installation

> Add `@lumiose/ui` to a Lumiose app and import its stylesheets, and the default theme if you want its look. The components then render in server HTML, without an island, and a page loads only the small scripts of the components it renders.

**Status:** `@lumiose/ui` is not on npm yet. In this repository's workspace, an app adds it as
`"@lumiose/ui": "workspace:*"` in its `dependencies`.

## Add the package

`@lumiose/ui` needs a Lumiose app: it ships its components as TSX, which the app's build compiles
with the app's own code, and `lumiose` is its peer dependency. Once it is on npm:

```sh
pnpm add @lumiose/ui
```

A new app can start with it: `create-lumiose --ui` adds the dependency, imports the stylesheets in
the root layout and adds the UI agent files (the `lumiose-ui` skill and a UI part in `AGENTS.md`).
In an app that already depends on it, `lumiose agents init` adds those agent files.

## Import the stylesheets

Import them once, in the root layout (`src/routes/layout.stsx`), so every page has them:

```ts
import "@lumiose/ui/styles.css"; // what every component needs (or "@lumiose/ui/dialog.css", …)
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

They sit in cascade layers, so your own CSS overrides them without specificity games
([Theming](theming.md#cascade-layers)).

## Use a component

Import a component from `@lumiose/ui` (or its own entry, `@lumiose/ui/popover`) and compose its
parts. In a page or a server component it renders as server HTML that works before any script
loads; with the default theme, the `lu-` classes give it its look:

```tsx check
import { Popover } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function Help() {
  return (
    <Popover.Root>
      <Popover.Trigger class="lu-button">Help</Popover.Trigger>
      <Popover.Popup class="lu-popover">
        <Popover.Title>Help</Popover.Title>
        <Popover.Description>
          Server HTML: this popover opens without JavaScript.
        </Popover.Description>
      </Popover.Popup>
    </Popover.Root>
  );
}
```

To keep a component's state in a signal (`bind:open`, `bind:value`), render it inside an
[island](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/islands/). Each component's page lists its parts,
props, keyboard contract and what works without JavaScript.

## Related

- [UI components](README.md): the approach and the components.
- [Theming](theming.md): the default theme's classes and `--lu-` properties, and your own CSS.
- [Getting started](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/getting-started/): a new Lumiose app.

<!-- source: theming.md -->

# Theming

> `@lumiose/ui` is unstyled: its stylesheets hold only what the components need to work. The optional default theme gives them a look, light and dark, through `--lu-` custom properties you can change; or style the parts with your own CSS.

## Cascade layers

The components' stylesheets hold only what a component needs to work (display, positioning and
anchoring, the top layer, the CSS variables a component sets), in the `lu.core` cascade layer. The
default theme sits in `lu.theme`, above it:

```ts
import "@lumiose/ui/styles.css"; // what every component needs (or "@lumiose/ui/dialog.css", …)
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

Both stylesheets declare the layers `lu.core, lu.theme`, in that order. CSS outside layers always
wins over layered CSS, so your own stylesheets override the package's without specificity games.
If your app orders its own layers, put `lu` first: `@layer lu, reset, components;`.

## The default theme

`@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css` is a ready look for demos, prototypes and getting started: neutral
surfaces, a blue primary, light and dark. It styles a few classes, which you put on the parts
through their `class` prop:

| Class                | On                                             | Variants                                                                                    |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lu-button`          | `Button`, any `<button>` part                  | `data-variant="primary"`, `data-variant="destructive"`                                      |
| `lu-dialog`          | `Dialog.Popup`                                 | Styles the backdrop, the title, the description and a `<footer>` inside                     |
| `lu-popover`         | `Popover.Popup`                                | Styles the title, the description and a `<footer>` inside                                   |
| `lu-tooltip`         | `Tooltip.Popup`                                |                                                                                             |
| `lu-tabs`            | `Tabs.Root`                                    | Styles the list, the tabs (the selected one underlined) and the panels                      |
| `lu-menu`            | every `Menu.Popup`                             | Styles the items, their checkbox and radio marks, separators and labels                     |
| `lu-combobox`        | `Combobox.Root`, `Autocomplete.Root`           | Lays out the field (label, chips, input, buttons) and styles the popup                      |
| `lu-select`          | `Select.Root`                                  | Makes it a customizable select and styles the control and the picker                        |
| `lu-field`           | `Field.Root`                                   | Stacks the label, control, description and errors; errors in red                            |
| `lu-input`           | `Input`, `Field.Control`                       | A text field with a focus ring and a red border when invalid                                |
| `lu-fieldset`        | `Fieldset.Root`, `CheckboxGroup`, `RadioGroup` | The legend and the items in a column                                                        |
| `lu-checkbox`        | `Checkbox.Root`                                | An 18px box in a 24px target, a ✓ or a dash                                                 |
| `lu-radio`           | `Radio.Root`                                   | An 18px circle in a 24px target, a thick ring when checked                                  |
| `lu-switch`          | `Switch.Root`                                  | A track and a thumb on the side that tells on from off                                      |
| `lu-collapsible`     | `Collapsible.Root`                             | Styles the trigger (a chevron) and animates the panel's height                              |
| `lu-accordion`       | `Accordion.Root`                               | Items between borders; styles the triggers and animates the panels                          |
| `lu-toast-viewport`  | `Toast.Viewport`                               | A column at the window's bottom end                                                         |
| `lu-toast`           | every `Toast.Root`                             | Styles the title, description and close button; `data-type="error"`                         |
| `lu-toggle`          | `Toggle`                                       | Pressed: a filled surface and a bar along the bottom                                        |
| `lu-toggle-group`    | `ToggleGroup`                                  | The toggles in a row, or a column when vertical                                             |
| `lu-progress`        | `Progress.Root`                                | The label and value above a bar; a sliding segment when indeterminate                       |
| `lu-meter`           | `Meter.Root`                                   | The label and value above a bar                                                             |
| `lu-slider`          | `Slider.Root`                                  | The label and value above the track, the indicator and 24px thumbs                          |
| `lu-number-field`    | `NumberField.Root`                             | The label above one bordered group: the input between its buttons                           |
| `lu-otp-field`       | `OTPField.Root`                                | A box per character, the caret's box ringed while focused                                   |
| `lu-preview-card`    | `PreviewCard.Popup`                            | A surface like a popover's, with a fade                                                     |
| `lu-toolbar`         | `Toolbar.Root`                                 | A bordered row (or column), separators across it, links as tall as buttons                  |
| `lu-scroll-area`     | `ScrollArea.Root`                              | A bordered box; 10px scrollbars shown on hover, scroll or focus                             |
| `lu-drawer`          | `Drawer.Popup`                                 | A surface against its edge (a handle on a bottom sheet), title, description, footer; slides |
| `lu-separator`       | `Separator`                                    | A 1px line in `--lu-border`, horizontal or vertical                                         |
| `lu-avatar`          | `Avatar.Root`                                  | A 40px circle on a muted surface, the image covering it, the initials centred               |
| `lu-menubar`         | `Menubar`                                      | A bordered bar of the triggers, the open one filled; `lu-menu` on each popup                |
| `lu-navigation-menu` | `NavigationMenu.Root`                          | The list in a row, the current page underlined, contents as surfaces that slide in          |

Its colours and radius are custom properties with shadcn/ui's names and a `--lu-` prefix, so a
shadcn palette carries over:

| Property                                          | Used for                            |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `--lu-background`, `--lu-foreground`              | Page-level surfaces and text        |
| `--lu-card`, `--lu-card-foreground`               | Cards                               |
| `--lu-popover`, `--lu-popover-foreground`         | Dialogs, popovers, menus            |
| `--lu-primary`, `--lu-primary-foreground`         | Primary actions                     |
| `--lu-secondary`, `--lu-secondary-foreground`     | Secondary actions                   |
| `--lu-muted`, `--lu-muted-foreground`             | Subdued surfaces and text           |
| `--lu-accent`, `--lu-accent-foreground`           | Hover and highlighted items         |
| `--lu-destructive`, `--lu-destructive-foreground` | Destructive actions                 |
| `--lu-border`, `--lu-input`, `--lu-ring`          | Borders, field borders, focus rings |
| `--lu-radius`                                     | Corner radius                       |

The theme sets `color-scheme: light dark` on `:root` and every colour with `light-dark()`, so it
follows the system. Set `color-scheme: light` (or `dark`) on `:root` or on any element to force
one, and redefine a property outside layers to change it:

```css
:root {
  --lu-primary: #7c3aed;
  --lu-radius: 0.375rem;
}
```

The theme meets WCAG 2.2 AA in light and dark: each `-foreground` colour reaches 4.5:1 on its
surface, and `--lu-input` (the borders of fields and controls) and `--lu-ring` (the focus ring)
reach 3:1 on the surfaces they sit on. `--lu-border` is for decoration, such as a dialog's edge:
it is too light to outline a control. Keep those ratios when you change the colours.

## Your own CSS

Style the parts through:

- **Class props.** Every part takes `class` (and `style`), like the element it renders. No part
  carries a class or attribute of its own.
- **State.** Components expose state the way the platform does, so selectors read it directly:
  `dialog[open]`, `:modal`, `::backdrop`, `:popover-open`, `[aria-expanded]`, `[aria-checked]`,
  `[aria-selected]`, and `data-highlighted` on the active option of a list.

Each component's page has an example stylesheet to start from.

## Related

- [UI components](README.md): the approach and the components.
- [Installation](installation.md): adding the package and importing its stylesheets.
- [Styles](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/styles/): scoped CSS and global stylesheets in Lumiose.

<!-- source: accordion.md -->

# Accordion

> A stack of items whose triggers show and hide their panels, after the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern: each item is a native `<details>`, one open at a time through the browser's exclusive group (`name`) or several, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript and find-in-page opens the item it lands in. `<lu-accordion>`, a 1 kB light-DOM element, adds the arrow keys and Base UI's animation hooks. `bind:value` (or `value` and `onValueChange`) keeps a signal in sync.

```ts
import { Accordion } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/accordion"
import "@lumiose/ui/accordion.css"; // the root is a block; disabled triggers ignore the pointer
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Accordion.Root>
  <Accordion.Item>
    <Accordion.Header>
      <Accordion.Trigger />
    </Accordion.Header>
    <Accordion.Panel />
  </Accordion.Item>
</Accordion.Root>
```

| Part      | Renders                                                                                                            |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Root`    | `<lu-accordion>`, around the items.                                                                                |
| `Item`    | `<details name="…">`, right inside `Root`, `open` while its panel shows; no `name` when several may be open.       |
| `Header`  | `<h3>` around the trigger's label: inside the `<summary>`, where HTML allows a heading.                            |
| `Trigger` | `<summary aria-controls="…">`, the first child of `Item`: it opens and closes the panel.                           |
| `Panel`   | `<div role="region" aria-labelledby="…">`, labelled by its trigger; the browser hides it while the item is closed. |

HTML puts a heading inside a `<summary>`, not a `<summary>` inside a heading, so `Header` renders
its `<h3>` inside the trigger's `<summary>`: the trigger names the heading, and the browser
exposes the `<summary>` as a button with its expanded state. Set `aria-level` on `Header` for
another heading level.

## API

### Accordion.Root

| Prop            | Type                         | Default      |                                                                                                                   |
| --------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string[]`                   |              | The values of the open items: opens and closes them when it changes. Server HTML starts as it says.               |
| `defaultValue`  | `string[]`                   | `[]`         | The items open at first, when there is no `value`.                                                                |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string[]) => void`  |              | Called after an item opens or closes, with the values of the open items.                                          |
| `bind:value`    | `Signal<string[]>`           |              | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                                                        |
| `multiple`      | `boolean`                    | `false`      | Several items may be open at once. By default opening one closes the other, and only the first value starts open. |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`                    | `false`      | Every item is disabled.                                                                                           |
| `orientation`   | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` | `"vertical"` | The direction the arrow keys follow: Up and Down, or Left and Right.                                              |
| `loopFocus`     | `boolean`                    | `true`       | The arrow keys go from the last trigger to the first and back.                                                    |

Without `value`, `onValueChange` or `bind:value` the items keep their own state.

### Accordion.Item

| Prop           | Type                      | Default          |                                                           |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`        | `string`                  | an id of its own | Identifies the item in the root's `value`.                |
| `disabled`     | `boolean`                 | `false`          | Its trigger takes no focus and does not toggle the panel. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |                  | Called after the item opens or closes.                    |

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through. `id`, `name`, `aria-controls` and `aria-labelledby` stay
the parts' own, since they connect the parts.

- **`Trigger`**: a disabled trigger gets `aria-disabled="true"` and `tabindex="-1"`.
- **`Panel`**: the client script sets `--accordion-panel-height` and `--accordion-panel-width` on
  it while it opens and closes, and `data-starting-style` and `data-ending-style`
  ([Styling](#styling)).

## Example

A FAQ in a server-rendered page, with no island, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { Accordion } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function ShippingFaq() {
  return (
    <Accordion.Root class="lu-accordion" defaultValue={["shipping"]}>
      <Accordion.Item value="shipping">
        <Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Trigger>When will my order ship?</Accordion.Trigger>
        </Accordion.Header>
        <Accordion.Panel>Within two working days.</Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
      <Accordion.Item value="returns">
        <Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Trigger>Can I return it?</Accordion.Trigger>
        </Accordion.Header>
        <Accordion.Panel>Yes, within 30 days, for free.</Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
      <Accordion.Item value="gifts" disabled>
        <Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Trigger>Gift cards</Accordion.Trigger>
        </Accordion.Header>
        <Accordion.Panel>Coming soon.</Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
    </Accordion.Root>
  );
}
```

In an island, several items open, bound to a signal: `bind:value={open}` is short for
`value={open()}` plus `onValueChange={(next) => open.set(next)}`.

```tsx check
import { Accordion } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function SettingsSections() {
  const open = signal(["profile"]);
  return (
    <>
      <Accordion.Root class="lu-accordion" multiple bind:value={open}>
        <Accordion.Item value="profile">
          <Accordion.Header>
            <Accordion.Trigger>Profile</Accordion.Trigger>
          </Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Panel>Your name and photo.</Accordion.Panel>
        </Accordion.Item>
        <Accordion.Item value="security">
          <Accordion.Header>
            <Accordion.Trigger>Security</Accordion.Trigger>
          </Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Panel>Password and recovery keys.</Accordion.Panel>
        </Accordion.Item>
      </Accordion.Root>
      <p>Open: {open().join(", ") || "none"}</p>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-accordion` on `Root`: items between borders, triggers as rows
with a chevron that turns while the item is open, and panels whose height animates.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class`, `[open]` on the items and
`[aria-disabled]` on the triggers. The client script gives each panel what Base UI's does, for an
open and close animation: `--accordion-panel-height` (the content's height in pixels while it
moves, `auto` once open), `data-starting-style` for the frame an opening starts from and
`data-ending-style` while it closes. The browser hides a panel as soon as its item closes, so keep
it visible while it closes with a transition on `::details-content`:

```css
.accordion > details > .panel {
  overflow: hidden;
  block-size: var(--accordion-panel-height, auto);
  transition: block-size 200ms ease-out;
}
.accordion > details > .panel:is([data-starting-style], [data-ending-style]) {
  block-size: 0;
}
.accordion > details::details-content {
  transition: content-visibility 200ms allow-discrete;
}
```

Opening an item closes the open one, and both animate. `@lumiose/ui/accordion.css`, in the
`lu.core` layer, makes `<lu-accordion>` a block, keeps a trigger's heading on the line of the
`<summary>`'s marker (`display: inline`), and makes a disabled trigger ignore the pointer.

## Keyboard and focus

The [WAI-ARIA accordion pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/accordion/), with its
optional keys, as in Base UI:

| Key            | Does                                                                                                                      |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter, Space   | On a trigger: opens or closes its item.                                                                                   |
| Tab, Shift+Tab | Move through the triggers and the open panels' content.                                                                   |
| Down, Up       | Move focus to the next or the previous trigger; Right and Left when `orientation="horizontal"`, swapped in right-to-left. |
| Home, End      | Move focus to the first or the last trigger.                                                                              |

- **Disabled triggers** are out of the tab order, and the arrow keys skip them.
- **Looping**: from the last trigger, Down goes to the first, unless `loopFocus={false}`.

## Without JavaScript, and the element's script

Opening and closing, one open item at a time (the `name` group), find-in-page and links into a
closed item are HTML features: an accordion in a server-rendered page works before any script
loads, and with none. Disabled triggers ignore the pointer through CSS. `value`, `onValueChange`
and `bind:value` need the component to run in an island.

A page that renders an `Accordion` loads a 1 kB (brotli) module once, without the Lumiose runtime;
islands bundle it. It defines `<lu-accordion>`, which adds the arrow keys, Home and End, and sets
the panels' animation hooks (shared with [Collapsible](collapsible.md)); a disabled trigger does
not toggle, also from the keyboard.

## Browser support

- **`<details name>`** (one open item at a time): Chrome 120, Firefox 130, Safari 17.2. Older
  browsers let several items open.
- **Find-in-page and links into a closed item** open it: Chrome 97, Firefox 139. Safari has not
  shipped it yet (WebKit bug 304174): there, find-in-page skips a closed item.
- **`::details-content`**, which the closing transition needs: Chrome 131, Firefox 143, Safari
  18.4. Elsewhere a panel disappears at once when its item closes.

## Related

- [Collapsible](collapsible.md): one panel and its trigger.
- [Tabs](tabs.md): one panel at a time, from a tab list.
- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling and the other components.

<!-- source: autocomplete.md -->

# Autocomplete

> A text input with suggestions, for text that may be anything (a search, a tag, an address): the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with list autocomplete, after Base UI's Autocomplete. Unlike a [Combobox](combobox.md), the text is the value: the input has the name and submits what is typed, and choosing a suggestion only fills it in. It runs on the Combobox's element (`<lu-combobox free>`, 4.1 kB) and parts, on server-rendered pages and in islands; `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync. Filtering, inline completion, groups, an empty state and a status.

```ts
import { Autocomplete } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/autocomplete"
import "@lumiose/ui/autocomplete.css"; // Combobox's CSS: places the popup, hides filtered options
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Autocomplete.Root>
  <Autocomplete.Label />
  <Autocomplete.Input />
  <Autocomplete.Clear />
  <Autocomplete.Trigger />
  <Autocomplete.Popup>
    <Autocomplete.List>
      <Autocomplete.Item />
      <Autocomplete.Group>
        <Autocomplete.GroupLabel />
        <Autocomplete.Item />
      </Autocomplete.Group>
    </Autocomplete.List>
    <Autocomplete.Empty />
    <Autocomplete.Status />
  </Autocomplete.Popup>
</Autocomplete.Root>
```

| Part                  | Renders                                                                             |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`                | `<lu-combobox free>`: the element, with no box; `inline` with inline completion     |
| `Label`               | `<label for>` the input                                                             |
| `Input`               | `<input role="combobox" aria-autocomplete name value>`: the form control            |
| `Clear`, `Trigger`    | `<button tabindex="-1">`: empty the text, or open and close the suggestions         |
| `Popup`, `List`       | `<div popover>` around the `<div role="listbox">`, or the listbox as the popup      |
| `Item`                | `<div role="option" data-value>`: a suggestion; its `value` is the text it fills in |
| `Group`, `GroupLabel` | `<div role="group">` named by its `<div role="presentation">`                       |
| `Empty`, `Status`     | `<div role="status">`: shown when nothing matches, or a message you update          |

The parts are [Combobox](combobox.md)'s, under this Root: their props and styling hooks are the
same.

## API

### Autocomplete.Root

| Prop                                | Type                                     | Default      |                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`                             | `string`                                 |              | Puts this text in the input when it changes. Pair it with `onValueChange`.      |
| `defaultValue`                      | `string`                                 |              | The text at first; a form reset goes back to it.                                |
| `onValueChange`                     | `(value: string) => void`                |              | Called as the text changes: typing, choosing a suggestion, clearing.            |
| `bind:value`                        | `Signal<string>`                         |              | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                      |
| `open`, `onOpenChange`, `bind:open` | `boolean`, `(open: boolean) => void`     |              | Open or close the suggestions, and hear about it, as in Combobox.               |
| `mode`                              | `"list" \| "both" \| "inline" \| "none"` | `"list"`     | How the suggestions complete the text (below).                                  |
| `filter`                            | `"contains" \| "startsWith"`             | `"contains"` | How `"list"` and `"both"` filter the suggestions, ignoring case and accents.    |
| `openOnInputClick`                  | `boolean`                                | `false`      | A click on the input opens the suggestions; otherwise typing and Arrow Down do. |
| `name`                              | `string`                                 |              | The name the text is submitted under (the input's).                             |
| `required`, `disabled`              | `boolean`                                | `false`      | As on a native input.                                                           |

The modes follow Base UI's:

- **`"list"`**: typing filters the suggestions; the input keeps what is typed while the arrows move
  through them.
- **`"both"`**: filtered, and the arrows show the highlighted suggestion in the input, its
  completed part selected; Escape takes it back, Tab or a click elsewhere keeps it.
- **`"inline"`**: the arrows show the highlighted suggestion in the input, unfiltered.
- **`"none"`**: neither: the page filters the suggestions itself (results from a server).

### The other parts

As in [Combobox](combobox.md#the-other-parts). An `Item`'s `value` is the text it fills in (and its
`label`, when the shown text differs, what typing matches). Inside a [Field](field.md), the input
takes the field's id, name, description and error, and the field shows its validation.

**Differences from Base UI's Autocomplete.** The suggestions are markup, not an `items` array, and
filtering compares their text (`mode="none"` hands it to you, as Base UI's `filter={null}`). No
`autoHighlight`, `keepHighlight`, `submitOnItemClick` or `limit`: Enter on a highlighted suggestion
fills it in, and Enter with none highlighted submits the form. No `Portal`, `Positioner`,
`Backdrop`, `Arrow`, `Value`, `Icon`, `Row`, `Collection` or `Separator`.

## Example

A search with suggestions, in an island:

```tsx check
import { Autocomplete } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

const TOPICS = ["accessibility", "animation", "forms", "islands", "routing", "signals"];

export function TopicSearch() {
  const query = signal("");
  return (
    <>
      <Autocomplete.Root name="q" bind:value={query} class="lu-combobox">
        <Autocomplete.Label>Search the docs</Autocomplete.Label>
        <Autocomplete.Input placeholder="Any topic" />
        <Autocomplete.Popup>
          <Autocomplete.List>
            {TOPICS.map((topic) => (
              <Autocomplete.Item value={topic}>{topic}</Autocomplete.Item>
            ))}
          </Autocomplete.List>
          <Autocomplete.Empty>No suggestions: press Enter to search.</Autocomplete.Empty>
        </Autocomplete.Popup>
      </Autocomplete.Root>
      <p>{query() ? `Searching for “${query()}”` : "Type to search."}</p>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-combobox` on `Root`, as for a Combobox: the label, the input
with its buttons, and the popup with the highlighted suggestion marked.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class` and their state: `[aria-expanded]` on the
input, `:popover-open` on the popup, `[data-highlighted]` and `[aria-disabled]` on the
suggestions, `[hidden]` on filtered ones.

`@lumiose/ui/autocomplete.css` is Combobox's stylesheet: it places the popup next to the input and
keeps filtered suggestions hidden.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key                   | Does                                                                                             |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Typing                | Filters the suggestions (with `"list"` and `"both"`) and opens them; an empty input closes them. |
| Arrow Down / Arrow Up | Opens the suggestions, then moves the highlight (with `"both"` and `"inline"`, into the input).  |
| Enter                 | Fills in the highlighted suggestion; with none highlighted, submits the form.                    |
| Escape                | Closes the suggestions and keeps the typed text (taking back an inline completion).              |
| Tab                   | Closes the suggestions and moves on, keeping the text.                                           |

Focus stays in the input: the highlight moves through `aria-activedescendant`.

## Without JavaScript, and the element's script

The input is a native text field with the name: typing, `required`, submission and reset work with
no script; the suggestions need it. `<lu-combobox>`'s script (4.1 kB brotli, shared with Combobox)
filters and opens them, moves the highlight, fills in a choice (firing `input` and `change` on the
input) and runs inline completion.

## Browser support

As [Combobox](combobox.md#browser-support): popover, and CSS anchor positioning where available
(the script places the popup elsewhere).

## Related

- [Combobox](combobox.md): a value picked from the options, when the text must match one.
- [Field](field.md): a label, a description and errors for an autocomplete.
- [Input](input.md): a text field without suggestions.

<!-- source: avatar.md -->

# Avatar

> A person's picture with a fallback, such as their initials, after Base UI's Avatar: the image loads in the server HTML and shows once it has loaded, the fallback shows until then, after an optional delay, and when the image fails. Both sit in one cell, so neither moves the other. A 0.5 kB script follows the image's loading status; without JavaScript the image covers the fallback when it loads.

```ts
import { Avatar } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/avatar"
import "@lumiose/ui/avatar.css"; // stacks the image over the fallback; hides each in turn
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Avatar.Root>
  <Avatar.Image />
  <Avatar.Fallback />
</Avatar.Root>
```

| Part       | Renders                                                                                        |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`     | `<lu-avatar>`, an inline grid with one cell, `data-loaded` once the image has loaded.          |
| `Image`    | `<img data-loading>`: `data-loading` while it loads, `data-error` when it failed, both hidden. |
| `Fallback` | `<span data-fallback>`, hidden once the image has loaded.                                      |

The image is the root's `<img>` child; anything else inside, such as a status badge, is yours to
place.

## API

### Avatar.Image

| Prop                    | Type                                                 | Default |                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onLoadingStatusChange` | `(status: "loading" \| "loaded" \| "error") => void` |         | Called when the loading status changes; `"error"` also when there is no `src`. An island hears the status the image had when it hydrated. |

Every native `<img>` prop passes through: `src`, `srcset`, `sizes`, `alt`, `width`, `height`,
`loading`, `decoding`, `fetchpriority`. A new `src` or `srcset` starts over at `"loading"`.

### Avatar.Fallback

| Prop    | Type     | Default |                                                                                                           |
| ------- | -------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `delay` | `number` | `0`     | How long to wait before showing the fallback, in milliseconds: an image that loads sooner never shows it. |

### The other parts

`Root` and `Fallback` take the props of the element they render (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`,
`data-*`, event handlers) and pass them through. The root element has a `status` property
(`"loading"`, `"loaded"`, `"error"`, or `undefined` without an image), and the image dispatches
`loadingstatuschange` (`event.detail.status`) for `on:loadingstatuschange`.

**Differences from Base UI's Avatar.** The image is always in the page, as with Base UI's
`keepMounted`: it starts loading with the server HTML, supports `loading="lazy"`, and shows without
JavaScript. A missing `src` is `"error"`, not `"idle"`. No `render`.

## Example

Two people in a server-rendered page, with no island: an image that loads, and one that fails and
leaves the initials. The default theme draws the circles.

```tsx check
import { Avatar } from "@lumiose/ui";

// A portrait drawn inline, so the example runs anywhere.
const portrait = `data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent(
  `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="80" height="80" viewBox="0 0 80 80">
    <rect width="80" height="80" fill="#c7d2fe"/>
    <circle cx="40" cy="31" r="14" fill="#4338ca"/>
    <path d="M12 80a28 28 0 0 1 56 0z" fill="#4338ca"/>
  </svg>`,
)}`;

export function Reviewers() {
  return (
    <ul aria-label="Reviewers" style={{ display: "flex", gap: "0.5rem", "list-style": "none" }}>
      <li>
        <Avatar.Root class="lu-avatar">
          <Avatar.Image src={portrait} alt="Ada Lovelace" />
          <Avatar.Fallback role="img" aria-label="Ada Lovelace" delay={600}>
            AL
          </Avatar.Fallback>
        </Avatar.Root>
      </li>
      <li>
        <Avatar.Root class="lu-avatar">
          <Avatar.Image src="/avatars/missing.jpg" alt="Grace Hopper" />
          <Avatar.Fallback role="img" aria-label="Grace Hopper">
            GH
          </Avatar.Fallback>
        </Avatar.Root>
      </li>
    </ul>
  );
}
```

In an island, the loading status in a signal, as the picture breaks and comes back:

```tsx check
import { Avatar, type AvatarLoadingStatus } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

const portrait = `data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent(
  `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="80" height="80" viewBox="0 0 80 80">
    <rect width="80" height="80" fill="#fde68a"/>
    <circle cx="40" cy="31" r="14" fill="#b45309"/>
    <path d="M12 80a28 28 0 0 1 56 0z" fill="#b45309"/>
  </svg>`,
)}`;

export function ProfilePicture() {
  const broken = signal(false);
  const status = signal<AvatarLoadingStatus>("loading");
  return (
    <>
      <Avatar.Root class="lu-avatar">
        <Avatar.Image
          src={broken() ? "/avatars/missing.jpg" : portrait}
          alt=""
          onLoadingStatusChange={(next) => status.set(next)}
        />
        <Avatar.Fallback aria-hidden="true">AL</Avatar.Fallback>
      </Avatar.Root>
      <p>Ada Lovelace (picture: {status()})</p>
      <button type="button" class="lu-button" onClick={() => broken.set(!broken())}>
        {broken() ? "Fix the picture" : "Break the picture"}
      </button>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-avatar` on `Root`: a 40px circle on a muted surface, the image
covering it, the fallback's initials centred.

**With your own CSS**, give the root a size, so the image loading or failing never changes the
layout, and style the parts through `class`, `[data-loaded]`, `[data-loading]`, `[data-error]` and
`[data-fallback]`:

```css
.avatar {
  place-items: center;
  inline-size: 3rem;
  block-size: 3rem;
  overflow: hidden;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: #f4f4f5;
}
.avatar > img {
  inline-size: 100%;
  block-size: 100%;
  object-fit: cover;
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/avatar.css`, in the `lu.core` layer, puts the parts in one grid cell, the image above
the fallback, and hides them in turn with `visibility` (so a `loading="lazy"` image still loads):
the image while it loads, where scripting is enabled, and when it failed; the fallback once the
image has loaded. The fallback's `delay` is a zero-length `lu-avatar-delay` animation: an animation
of your own on the fallback replaces it, so list both (`animation: lu-avatar-delay 0s
var(--lu-avatar-delay, 0s) backwards, my-fade 200ms`).

## Keyboard and focus

An avatar takes no focus and has no keys. Name it once:

- **Next to the person's name**, it repeats it: `alt=""` on the image and `aria-hidden="true"` on
  the fallback.
- **Alone**, name both parts, since only one shows at a time: the image's `alt`, and on the
  fallback `role="img"` with an `aria-label`, so the initials are not read letter by letter.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

The image and the fallback are in the server HTML. Without JavaScript both show, the image above:
it covers the fallback once it loads, and the browser's broken-image box replaces it when it fails.
`onLoadingStatusChange` needs the component to run in an island.

A page that renders an `Avatar` loads a 0.5 kB (brotli) script, without the Lumiose runtime;
islands bundle it. `<lu-avatar>` reads the image's state when it connects (a cached image shows
at once), then follows its `load` and `error` events and changes to its `src` and `srcset`. An
image that is complete without a size (an SVG without intrinsic dimensions, or a broken image) is
told apart with `decode()`.

## Browser support

- **The `scripting` media query**, which keeps a loading image hidden only where scripts run:
  Chrome and Edge 120, Firefox 113, Safari 17. Elsewhere a loading image shows as it arrives.
- **CSS grid and `visibility`**: every browser.

## Related

- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling and the other components.
- [Theming](theming.md): the default theme's classes and custom properties.

<!-- source: button.md -->

# Button

> A native `<button>`, after Base UI's Button. It is `type="button"` unless you say otherwise, so it submits a form only when asked to. Disabled it leaves the tab order; with `focusableWhenDisabled` it stays focusable as `aria-disabled="true"` (a loading state keeps focus where it was) and a tiny script cancels its clicks.

```ts
import { Button } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/button"
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Button>Save</Button>
```

| Part     | Renders                                                                       |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Button` | `<button type="button">`; `aria-disabled="true"` with `focusableWhenDisabled` |

## API

### Button

| Prop                    | Type      | Default    |                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | --------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`                  | `string`  | `"button"` | `"submit"` or `"reset"` to act on its form.                                                                |
| `disabled`              | `boolean` | `false`    | Natively disabled: out of the tab order, its clicks ignored.                                               |
| `focusableWhenDisabled` | `boolean` | `false`    | With `disabled`: it stays focusable as `aria-disabled="true"`, and its clicks, Enter and Space do nothing. |

Every other native prop passes through: `name`, `value`, `form`, `command`, `commandfor`,
`popovertarget`, `id`, `class`, `aria-*`, `onClick`.

**Differences from Base UI's Button.** It is always a `<button>`: no `nativeButton` or `render`. For
a link that looks like a button, style an `<a>` with the same class.

## Example

A save button that keeps focus while it saves, in an island:

```tsx check
import { Button } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function SavingButton() {
  const saving = signal(false);
  return (
    <Button
      class="lu-button"
      data-variant="primary"
      disabled={saving()}
      focusableWhenDisabled
      onClick={() => {
        saving.set(true);
        setTimeout(() => saving.set(false), 1500);
      }}
    >
      {saving() ? "Saving…" : "Save"}
    </Button>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-button` on it (`data-variant="primary"` or
`data-variant="destructive"` for the others): a 36px tall button with a focus ring, faded when
`:disabled` or `[aria-disabled="true"]`.

**With your own CSS**, style the button and its states: `:hover`, `:focus-visible`, `:disabled`,
`[aria-disabled="true"]`.

Button ships no stylesheet: it needs none to work.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key           | Does                                                                          |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter / Space | Presses it, unless it is disabled.                                            |
| Tab           | Moves on. A disabled button is skipped, unless it is focusable when disabled. |

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

A native button: it works, submits and resets with no script. The client script (0.1 kB brotli)
only cancels the clicks, Enter and Space of an `aria-disabled` button (one without a `role` of its
own); without it such a button still acts, so a server page that disables a button until
something happens should use `disabled` alone.

## Browser support

Native `<button>`: every browser.

## Related

- [Toggle](toggle.md): a button that stays pressed.
- [Form](form.md): a form whose submit button is a Button.
- [Dialog](dialog.md): a Button with `command="show-modal"` opens a dialog without JavaScript.

<!-- source: checkbox.md -->

# Checkbox

> A native `<input type="checkbox">`, after Base UI's Checkbox: Space and a label click toggle it, the form submits its value when checked, reset and `required` work, in server HTML and without JavaScript. `indeterminate`, `readOnly`, the parent checkbox of a [Checkbox Group](checkbox-group.md) and `bind:checked` come on top, with a 0.5 kB script shared with Radio Group and Switch.

```ts
import { Checkbox } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/checkbox"
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<label>
  <Checkbox.Root /> Label
</label>
```

| Part   | Renders                                                                                                           |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root` | `<input type="checkbox">`; `data-indeterminate` in server HTML while indeterminate, `aria-readonly` if read-only. |

Name it with a wrapping `<label>`, a `<label for>`, a `Field.Label`, or `aria-label`.

## API

### Checkbox.Root

| Prop              | Type                         | Default |                                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checked`         | `boolean`                    |         | Checks or unchecks it when it changes. Pair it with `onCheckedChange`.                               |
| `defaultChecked`  | `boolean`                    | `false` | Whether it starts checked; a form reset goes back to it.                                             |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` |         | Called after the user checks or unchecks it.                                                         |
| `bind:checked`    | `Signal<boolean>`            |         | Stands in for `checked` and `onCheckedChange`.                                                       |
| `indeterminate`   | `boolean`                    | `false` | Neither checked nor unchecked (mixed for assistive technology) until the user toggles it.            |
| `value`           | `string`                     | `"on"`  | What it submits when checked, and its identity in a Checkbox Group.                                  |
| `parent`          | `boolean`                    | `false` | The "select all" checkbox of a Checkbox Group: it checks them all and follows them. Never submitted. |
| `readOnly`        | `boolean`                    | `false` | It cannot be toggled, but stays focusable and is submitted.                                          |

Every other native prop passes through: `name`, `required`, `disabled`, `form`, `id`, `class`,
`aria-*`. Inside a Field it takes the field's `id`, `name`, `aria-describedby` and
`aria-invalid`; inside a Checkbox Group, its `checked` state and `name`.

**Differences from Base UI's Checkbox.** The box is the native input, so there is no
`Checkbox.Indicator`: draw the box and its mark with `appearance: none` and `::before` (as the
default theme does). There is no `nativeButton`, `inputRef` or `uncheckedValue`: an unchecked box
submits nothing, as a native one does.

## Example

In an island, bound to a signal:

```tsx check
import { Checkbox } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function NewsletterOptIn() {
  const subscribed = signal(false);
  return (
    <p>
      <label>
        <Checkbox.Root name="newsletter" bind:checked={subscribed} class="lu-checkbox" /> Send me
        the newsletter
      </label>{" "}
      {subscribed() ? "Thanks!" : ""}
    </p>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-checkbox` on `Root`: an 18px box drawn by `::before` inside a
24px target, a ✓ when checked and a dash when indeterminate (a symbol, not only a colour), the
primary colour for both, a focus ring, a red border with `aria-invalid="true"`.

**With your own CSS**, style the input and its state: `:checked`, `:indeterminate` (and
`[data-indeterminate]` before the script runs), `:disabled`, `:focus-visible`,
`[aria-readonly="true"]`, `[aria-invalid="true"]`.

```css
.checkbox {
  appearance: none;
  inline-size: 1.25rem;
  block-size: 1.25rem;
  border: 1px solid #85858e;
  border-radius: 0.25rem;
}
.checkbox:checked {
  background: #2563eb;
}
.checkbox:checked::before {
  content: "✓" / "";
  color: #fff;
}
```

Checkbox ships no stylesheet: it needs none to work.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key   | Does                                                   |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Space | Toggles it (not when read-only).                       |
| Tab   | Moves to the next control: a checkbox is one tab stop. |

Enter does not toggle it. A click on its label toggles it too.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

A native checkbox: toggling, submission, `required`, reset and `disabled` (its own or a fieldset's)
work with no script.

A page that renders a Checkbox, Checkbox Group, Radio Group or Switch loads one 0.5 kB (brotli)
script once, without the Lumiose runtime; islands bundle it. It turns server HTML's
`data-indeterminate` into the `indeterminate` property (which has no attribute), makes read-only
inputs ignore clicks, Space and the label, and runs the parent checkbox of a group. Without it, an
indeterminate box shows unchecked (the theme still draws it mixed) and a read-only one toggles.

## Browser support

Native checkboxes, `:indeterminate` and `appearance: none` with `::before`: every supported
browser.

## Related

- [Checkbox Group](checkbox-group.md): several checkboxes with one value and a parent checkbox.
- [Switch](switch.md): on and off for a setting that applies at once.
- [Field](field.md): a label, a description and errors for a checkbox.

<!-- source: checkbox-group.md -->

# Checkbox Group

> A group of checkboxes with one value, the list of the checked ones, after Base UI's CheckboxGroup: a native `<fieldset>` whose checkboxes share a name, so the form submits each checked value and a disabled group disables them all, without JavaScript. A parent checkbox checks them all and shows checked, mixed or unchecked as they are; `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync.

```ts
import { CheckboxGroup, Checkbox, Fieldset } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/checkbox-group"
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<CheckboxGroup>
  <Fieldset.Legend />
  <Checkbox.Root parent />
  <Checkbox.Root />
</CheckboxGroup>
```

| Part            | Renders                                                                             |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CheckboxGroup` | `<fieldset>` around the checkboxes; a `Fieldset.Legend` first inside names it.      |
| `Checkbox.Root` | A [Checkbox](checkbox.md) of the group, checked when its `value` is in the group's. |

## API

### CheckboxGroup

| Prop            | Type                        | Default |                                                                                        |
| --------------- | --------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string[]`                  |         | Checks the checkboxes with these values when it changes. Pair it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue`  | `string[]`                  | `[]`    | The values checked at first.                                                           |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string[]) => void` |         | Called with the checked values after the user checks or unchecks one.                  |
| `bind:value`    | `Signal<string[]>`          |         | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                             |
| `allValues`     | `string[]`                  |         | Every checkbox's value: the parent checkbox's state in server HTML.                    |
| `name`          | `string`                    |         | The name the checkboxes submit under, unless they have their own.                      |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`                   | `false` | Disables every checkbox (a disabled fieldset).                                         |

Every other `<fieldset>` prop passes through.

**Differences from Base UI's CheckboxGroup.** It renders a `<fieldset>`, so a legend names it and
`disabled` is native. `name` is added: Base UI gives each checkbox its own. A parent checkbox
needs only `parent` here, not a controlled group, since the script runs it from the DOM. A
`required` group (one checked at least) is not offered yet.

## Example

Toppings in a server-rendered form, with a "select all" box:

```tsx check
import { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup, Fieldset } from "@lumiose/ui";

const TOPPINGS = ["Cheese", "Olives", "Peppers"];

export function ToppingsGroup() {
  return (
    <CheckboxGroup
      name="toppings"
      defaultValue={["Cheese"]}
      allValues={TOPPINGS}
      class="lu-fieldset"
    >
      <Fieldset.Legend>Toppings</Fieldset.Legend>
      <label>
        <Checkbox.Root parent class="lu-checkbox" /> All toppings
      </label>
      {TOPPINGS.map((topping) => (
        <label>
          <Checkbox.Root value={topping} class="lu-checkbox" /> {topping}
        </label>
      ))}
    </CheckboxGroup>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-fieldset` on the group and `lu-checkbox` on each checkbox
([Checkbox](checkbox.md#styling)). Style a parent checkbox with `[data-parent]` if it should look
different.

CheckboxGroup ships no stylesheet: it needs none to work.

## Keyboard and focus

Each checkbox is its own tab stop; Space toggles the focused one. Toggling the parent checks or
unchecks every enabled checkbox of the group; toggling one updates the parent (checked, mixed or
unchecked).

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

The checkboxes are native: they toggle, submit under the group's name and reset with no script.
The parent checkbox shows its server state and is never submitted, but checks nothing until the
shared checkbox script (0.5 kB brotli, [Checkbox](checkbox.md#without-javascript-and-the-client-script))
runs.

## Browser support

Every supported browser.

## Related

- [Checkbox](checkbox.md): the checkboxes, `indeterminate` and `readOnly`.
- [Fieldset](fieldset.md): the legend.
- [Radio Group](radio-group.md): one value out of several.

<!-- source: collapsible.md -->

# Collapsible

> A panel that its trigger shows and hides: a native `<details>` whose `<summary>` is the trigger, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript, keeps the browser's keyboard handling, and opens when find-in-page or a link lands inside it. A 0.7 kB script adds Base UI's animation hooks. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.

```ts
import { Collapsible } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/collapsible"
import "@lumiose/ui/collapsible.css"; // a disabled trigger ignores the pointer
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Collapsible.Root>
  <Collapsible.Trigger />
  <Collapsible.Panel />
</Collapsible.Root>
```

| Part      | Renders                                                                                     |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`    | `<details>`, `open` while the panel shows.                                                  |
| `Trigger` | `<summary aria-controls="…">`, the first child of `Root`: it opens and closes the panel.    |
| `Panel`   | `<div>`, the rest of the `<details>`: the browser hides it while the `<details>` is closed. |

The browser exposes the `<summary>` as a button with its expanded state, so the trigger has no
`aria-expanded` of its own. HTML allows one heading inside a `<summary>`, for a trigger that
titles a section (Accordion renders its headings that way).

## API

### Collapsible.Root

| Prop           | Type                      | Default |                                                                                                                         |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                 |         | Opens or closes the panel when it changes. Server HTML starts as it says.                                               |
| `defaultOpen`  | `boolean`                 | `false` | Whether the panel starts open, when there is no `open`.                                                                 |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |         | Called after the panel opens or closes, whatever did it: the trigger, find-in-page, a link, another item of its `name`. |
| `bind:open`    | `Signal<boolean>`         |         | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`.                                                                                |
| `disabled`     | `boolean`                 | `false` | The trigger takes no focus and does not toggle the panel.                                                               |

Without `open`, `onOpenChange` or `bind:open` the element keeps its own state. `Root` takes the
props of a `<details>` too: `name` makes collapsibles with the same name an exclusive group, where
opening one closes the others.

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through. `id` and `aria-controls` stay the parts' own, since
they connect the trigger and the panel.

- **`Trigger`**: a disabled trigger gets `aria-disabled="true"` and `tabindex="-1"`.
- **`Panel`**: the client script sets `--collapsible-panel-height` and `--collapsible-panel-width`
  on it while it opens and closes, and `data-starting-style` and `data-ending-style`
  ([Styling](#styling)).

## Example

A section in a server-rendered page, with no island, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { Collapsible } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function RecoveryKeys() {
  return (
    <Collapsible.Root class="lu-collapsible">
      <Collapsible.Trigger>Recovery keys</Collapsible.Trigger>
      <Collapsible.Panel>
        <p>Store these keys somewhere safe: each one lets you back in once.</p>
      </Collapsible.Panel>
    </Collapsible.Root>
  );
}
```

In an island, bound to a signal: `bind:open={open}` is short for `open={open()}` plus
`onOpenChange={(next) => open.set(next)}`.

```tsx check
import { Collapsible } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function AdvancedOptions() {
  const open = signal(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Collapsible.Root class="lu-collapsible" bind:open={open}>
        <Collapsible.Trigger>Advanced options</Collapsible.Trigger>
        <Collapsible.Panel>Proxy, timeouts and retries.</Collapsible.Panel>
      </Collapsible.Root>
      <p>{open() ? "Showing the advanced options" : "Advanced options hidden"}</p>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-collapsible` on `Root`: the trigger becomes a row with a
chevron that turns while the panel is open, and the panel's height animates.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class` and `[open]` on the root. The client script
gives the panel what Base UI's does, for an open and close animation: `--collapsible-panel-height`
(the content's height in pixels while it moves, `auto` once open), `data-starting-style` for the
frame an opening starts from and `data-ending-style` while it closes. The browser hides the panel
as soon as the `<details>` closes, so keep it visible while it closes with a transition on
`::details-content`:

```css
.collapsible > .panel {
  overflow: hidden;
  block-size: var(--collapsible-panel-height, auto);
  transition: block-size 200ms ease-out;
}
.collapsible > .panel:is([data-starting-style], [data-ending-style]) {
  block-size: 0;
}
.collapsible::details-content {
  transition: content-visibility 200ms allow-discrete;
}
```

A panel rendered open does not animate. `@lumiose/ui/collapsible.css` holds one rule, in the
`lu.core` layer: a disabled trigger (`summary[aria-disabled="true"]`) ignores the pointer.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key          | Does                                                                |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter, Space | On the trigger: opens or closes the panel.                          |
| Tab          | Moves to the trigger, then into the open panel's focusable content. |

The trigger is a `<summary>`, so the browser handles its keys and its focus. A disabled trigger is
out of the tab order.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

Opening and closing, the exclusive group of a `name`, and find-in-page are HTML features: a
Collapsible in a server-rendered page works before any script loads, and with none. A disabled
trigger ignores the pointer through CSS. `open`, `onOpenChange` and `bind:open` need the component
to run in an island.

A page that renders a `Collapsible` loads a 0.7 kB (brotli) module once, without the Lumiose
runtime; islands bundle it. It covers every Collapsible and [Accordion](accordion.md) panel on the
page:

- the animation hooks above, set on every opening and closing, whatever caused it (the trigger,
  find-in-page, a link, the `open` prop, another item of the group);
- a disabled trigger does not toggle, also from the keyboard.

## Browser support

- **`<details>` and `<summary>`**: every browser. **`name`** (exclusive groups): Chrome 120,
  Firefox 130, Safari 17.2.
- **Find-in-page and links into a closed panel** open it: Chrome 97, Firefox 139. Safari has not
  shipped it yet (WebKit bug 304174): there, find-in-page skips a closed panel.
- **`::details-content`**, which the closing transition needs: Chrome 131, Firefox 143, Safari
  18.4. Elsewhere the panel disappears at once when it closes.

## Related

- [Accordion](accordion.md): a stack of collapsible items, with arrow keys between them.
- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling and the other components.
- [Theming](theming.md): the default theme's classes and custom properties.

<!-- source: combobox.md -->

# Combobox

> A text input that filters a list of options, for picking one value or several from many: the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with list autocomplete, after Base UI's Combobox. The input shows the option's label and the form gets its value. `<lu-combobox>`, a 4.1 kB form-associated light-DOM element, runs it on server-rendered pages and in islands; `bind:value` and `bind:open` keep signals in sync. Groups, an empty state, a status, a clear button, multiple values with chips, validation and async options.

```ts
import { Combobox } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/combobox"
import "@lumiose/ui/combobox.css"; // places the popup and keeps filtered options hidden
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Combobox.Root>
  <Combobox.Label />
  <Combobox.Chips />
  <Combobox.Input />
  <Combobox.Clear />
  <Combobox.Trigger />
  <Combobox.Popup>
    <Combobox.List>
      <Combobox.Item />
      <Combobox.Group>
        <Combobox.GroupLabel />
        <Combobox.Item />
      </Combobox.Group>
    </Combobox.List>
    <Combobox.Empty />
    <Combobox.Status />
  </Combobox.Popup>
</Combobox.Root>
```

| Part         | Renders                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`       | `<lu-combobox>`, a form control with no box (`display: contents`) that holds the value and runs the parts.                                      |
| `Label`      | `<label for="…">` for the input; it also names the listbox.                                                                                     |
| `Input`      | `<input type="text" role="combobox" aria-autocomplete="list" aria-expanded="…" aria-controls="…" autocomplete="off">`, the anchor of the popup. |
| `Trigger`    | `<button type="button" tabindex="-1" command="--toggle" commandfor="…">`, which opens and closes the popup.                                     |
| `Clear`      | `<button type="button" tabindex="-1" command="--clear" commandfor="…">`, hidden while there is nothing to clear.                                |
| `Chips`      | `<div role="list">` of the selected values, with `multiple`; the script renders a `<span role="listitem">` for each, with a remove `<button>`.  |
| `Popup`      | `<div popover="manual" data-side="…" data-align="…">` around the `List`, for an empty state or a status beside it. Optional.                    |
| `List`       | `<div role="listbox">` of options; the popover itself (`popover="manual"`, `data-side`, `data-align`) when there is no `Popup`.                 |
| `Item`       | `<div role="option" data-value="…" aria-selected="…">`.                                                                                         |
| `Group`      | `<div role="group">` of options, named by its `GroupLabel`, hidden while none of its options matches.                                           |
| `GroupLabel` | `<div role="presentation">`, which names its `Group`.                                                                                           |
| `Empty`      | `<div role="status" hidden>`, shown instead of the options when none matches the text. Inside a `Popup`.                                        |
