| `Status`     | `<div role="status">` for a message whose changes are announced, such as "Searching…". Inside a `Popup`, or anywhere in the `Root`.             |

Every part goes inside `Root`. Options and groups go inside the `List`; the `Empty` and `Status`
parts go next to it in a `Popup`, never inside the listbox.

## API

### Combobox.Root

| Prop            | Type                                   | Default      |                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string`, `string[]` with `multiple`   |              | Selects the option with this value (these values) when it changes. `""` or `[]` selects nothing.                            |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`, `string[]` with `multiple`   |              | The selection at first, when `value` is left out.                                                                           |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void`                      |              | Called after the user chooses, removes or clears a value, with the new value. Typing never calls it.                        |
| `bind:value`    | `Signal<string>`, `Signal<string[]>`   |              | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                                                                  |
| `open`          | `boolean`                              |              | Opens or closes the popup when it changes, in the browser. Server HTML always starts closed.                                |
| `onOpenChange`  | `(open: boolean) => void`              |              | Called after the popup opens or closes, whatever did it.                                                                    |
| `bind:open`     | `Signal<boolean>`                      |              | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`.                                                                                    |
| `multiple`      | `boolean`                              | `false`      | Several values: choosing an option toggles it and the popup stays open. `value` is then an array.                           |
| `name`          | `string`                               |              | The name the value is submitted under; with `multiple`, each value is its own entry.                                        |
| `required`      | `boolean`                              | `false`      | The form needs a value: the browser reports an empty combobox at its input on submit.                                       |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`                              | `false`      | The input and the buttons are disabled. A disabled `<fieldset>` around it does the same.                                    |
| `filter`        | `"contains" \| "startsWith" \| "none"` | `"contains"` | How typing filters the options by their label, ignoring case and accents. `"none"` leaves filtering to you (async options). |

Without `value`, `onValueChange` or `bind:value` the combobox keeps its own state. `Root` passes
`class`, `style` and other element props to `<lu-combobox>`.

### Combobox.Item

| Prop       | Type      | Default |                                                                                        |
| ---------- | --------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`    | `string`  |         | Required: the value the combobox takes, and submits, when the option is chosen.        |
| `label`    | `string`  |         | The text the input shows and typing matches, when the option's text content is not it. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | The option cannot be chosen, and the arrow keys skip it (`aria-disabled`).             |

### Combobox.List and Combobox.Popup

| Prop          | Type                                                                       | Default    |                                                                    |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `side`        | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "inline-start" \| "inline-end"` | `"bottom"` | The input's side the popup goes on. It flips when it does not fit. |
| `align`       | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"`                                             | `"start"`  | How the popup aligns with the input along that side.               |
| `sideOffset`  | `number`                                                                   |            | The gap between the input and the popup, in CSS pixels.            |
| `alignOffset` | `number`                                                                   |            | A shift along the side, away from the aligned edge, in CSS pixels. |

The placement props go on the part that is the popover: the `Popup` when there is one, else the
`List`.

### Combobox.Chips

| Prop          | Type     | Default    |                                                                      |
| ------------- | -------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `removeLabel` | `string` | `"Remove"` | The remove buttons' name, before the value's label: "Remove Berlin". |

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through. Your props override the defaults (`tabindex`,
`autocomplete`, `hidden`); the roles, ids, ARIA references, commands and the anchor stay the parts'
own, since they connect the parts.

- **`Input`**: `placeholder`, `onInput` (for async options) and `aria-describedby` pass through.
  Its `type` and `value` are the combobox's. Inside a [Field](field.md), it takes the field's id
  (so `Field.Label` labels it), its description and error references and `aria-invalid`, and Root
  takes the field's `name` and disabled state; the field shows the combobox's validation.
- **`Trigger`** and **`Clear`**: out of the tab order, as in the APG examples; the input does
  everything from the keyboard. Name them with `aria-label` (or content).
- **`Group`**: `aria-labelledby` points at its `GroupLabel` while one renders.

**Differences from Base UI's Combobox.** No `Portal`, `Positioner`, `Backdrop`, `Arrow`, `Value`,
`Icon`, `ItemIndicator`, `Row`, `Collection` or `Separator`: the top layer and anchor positioning
replace the first ones, and the theme draws the selected mark from `[aria-selected="true"]`. The
options are markup, not an `items` array, and filtering compares their labels; `filter="none"`
hands it to you, as Base UI's `filter={null}`. The chips are rendered by the script from the
selected options' labels rather than by your components, so a server-rendered page needs no island
for them. `Label` is a part of its own (Base UI uses `Field.Label`). Arrow keys skip disabled
options, as in Zag.

## Example

A city picker in a server-rendered page, with no island, in a form:

```tsx check
import { Combobox } from "@lumiose/ui";

const CITIES = [
  { value: "ber", label: "Berlin" },
  { value: "lis", label: "Lisbon" },
  { value: "mad", label: "Madrid" },
];

export function CityField() {
  return (
    <form method="post">
      <Combobox.Root name="city" defaultValue="lis" required class="lu-combobox">
        <Combobox.Label>City</Combobox.Label>
        <Combobox.Input placeholder="Search cities" />
        <Combobox.Clear aria-label="Clear city" />
        <Combobox.Trigger aria-label="Show cities" />
        <Combobox.Popup>
          <Combobox.List>
            {CITIES.map((city) => (
              <Combobox.Item value={city.value}>{city.label}</Combobox.Item>
            ))}
          </Combobox.List>
          <Combobox.Empty>No city matches.</Combobox.Empty>
        </Combobox.Popup>
      </Combobox.Root>
      <button class="lu-button">Save</button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

In an island: several values bound to a signal, and options loaded as the user types.
`bind:value={tags}` is short for `value={tags()}` plus `onValueChange={(next) => tags.set(next)}`.

```tsx check
import { Combobox } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

const TAGS = ["accessibility", "bug", "docs", "performance", "security", "ui"];

/** Stands in for a request to your API: the tags that contain `text`, a moment later. */
function searchTags(text: string): Promise<string[]> {
  const query = text.trim().toLowerCase();
  const found = query ? TAGS.filter((tag) => tag.includes(query)) : [];
  return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(() => resolve(found), 200));
}

export function TagPicker() {
  const tags = signal<string[]>([]);
  const results = signal<string[]>([]);
  const searching = signal(false);
  const search = async (text: string) => {
    searching.set(true);
    results.set(await searchTags(text));
    searching.set(false);
  };
  return (
    <Combobox.Root multiple name="tags" filter="none" bind:value={tags} class="lu-combobox">
      <Combobox.Label>Tags</Combobox.Label>
      <Combobox.Chips />
      <Combobox.Input
        onInput={(event) => search((event.currentTarget as HTMLInputElement).value)}
      />
      <Combobox.Popup>
        <Combobox.List>
          {results().map((tag) => (
            <Combobox.Item value={tag}>{tag}</Combobox.Item>
          ))}
        </Combobox.List>
        <Combobox.Status>{searching() ? "Searching…" : ""}</Combobox.Status>
      </Combobox.Popup>
    </Combobox.Root>
  );
}
```

With `filter="none"`, the script gives new options the selection and opens the popup when results
arrive while the user types; a chosen value keeps its label after its option is gone.

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-combobox` on `Root`. It turns the root into the field's grid
(the label, the chips, then the input with the trigger and clear buttons over its inline end, with
a glyph when they are empty), and styles the popup, the options (highlighted, selected with a ✓,
disabled), the group labels, the chips and the empty and status messages. Its colours come from the
theme's `--lu-` properties ([UI components](README.md#the-default-theme)), and it sets a 4px gap
with `--lu-side-offset`.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class` and their state:

- the input: `[aria-expanded="true"]` while the popup is open, `[aria-invalid="true"]` after a
  submit found it empty, `:disabled`;
- the popup: `:popover-open`, `data-side` and `data-align`;
- options: `[data-highlighted]` on the active option (by keyboard or pointer; focus stays in the
  input), `[aria-selected="true"]`, `[aria-disabled="true"]`;
- `[role="group"]`, a group label's `[role="presentation"]`, `[role="status"]`;
- chips: `[role="listitem"]` in the `Chips` list, and its `button`;
- the buttons: `[command="--toggle"]`, `[command="--clear"]` (`[hidden]` while there is nothing to
  clear);
- the element: `lu-combobox:disabled`, `:invalid` and `:user-invalid` (it is a form control).

A starting point:

```css
.combobox [role="listbox"] {
  max-block-size: 18rem;
  overflow-y: auto;
  padding: 0.25rem;
  border: 1px solid #d4d4d8;
  border-radius: 0.5rem;
  --lu-side-offset: 4px;
}
.combobox [role="option"] {
  padding: 0.375rem 0.5rem;
  border-radius: 0.25rem;
}
.combobox [role="option"][data-highlighted] {
  background: #f4f4f5;
  outline: 2px solid #2563eb;
  outline-offset: -2px;
}
.combobox [role="option"][aria-selected="true"]::before {
  content: "✓" / "";
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/combobox.css` holds what the combobox needs to work, in the `lu.core` layer:
`lu-combobox` has no box, the options, groups and empty state the script hides stay hidden whatever
`display` your CSS gives them, and the shared placement rules anchor the popup to the input (with
CSS anchor positioning, a popup sits on its `data-side` and `data-align`, keeps the gaps of
`--lu-side-offset` and `--lu-align-offset`, and flips when it does not fit).

## Keyboard and focus

The [WAI-ARIA combobox pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/) with a listbox
popup, list autocomplete and manual selection, with Base UI's behaviour where it leaves a choice.
Focus stays in the input; the active option is `aria-activedescendant`.

| Key                  | Does                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A character          | Edits the text, filters the options and opens the popup when something matches (or there is an `Empty`). Never commits.                                                                             |
| Arrow Down, Arrow Up | Closed: opens the popup on the selected option, else the first (Arrow Up: the last). Open: the next or previous option, past the last back to the input, then around. Disabled options are skipped. |
| Alt+Arrow Down       | Opens the popup without highlighting an option.                                                                                                                                                     |
| Alt+Arrow Up         | Closes the popup.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Enter                | Chooses the highlighted option. With nothing highlighted, it does what Enter does in a form field.                                                                                                  |
| Escape               | Closes the popup without choosing and puts the selection's label back. Closed, it goes on to the page, so a dialog closes.                                                                          |
| Tab                  | Closes the popup without choosing and moves on.                                                                                                                                                     |
| Backspace            | With `multiple`, in an empty input: removes the last value.                                                                                                                                         |
| Home, End            | Move the text cursor, as in any text field.                                                                                                                                                         |

- **Choosing** an option puts its label in the input and closes the popup, or, with `multiple`,
  toggles it, clears the text and keeps the popup open. It fires `change` once per change.
- **Emptying the input** clears a single selection. Closing the popup without choosing (Escape,
  Tab, a click outside) puts the label back.
- **The pointer**: a click on the input opens the popup, hovering highlights an option, a click
  chooses it; presses in the popup and on the buttons keep focus in the input. A click outside
  closes the popup; a right-click or a second finger outside leaves it open, as in Base UI.
- **IME**: while composing, Enter and the arrows belong to the input method.

## Without JavaScript, and the element's script

The combobox needs its script: there is no native element that filters a styled list (`<datalist>`
cannot be styled or grouped, and customizable select cannot filter). Without JavaScript the server
HTML shows a labelled text field and nothing opens, and the form gets no value. For a choice that
must work without JavaScript, use [Select](select.md).

A page that renders a `Combobox` loads the script once, as a 4.1 kB (brotli) module without the
Lumiose runtime, and islands bundle it. It defines `lu-combobox`, which upgrades every combobox on
the page in place: it reads the selection the server rendered (`aria-selected="true"`), puts its
label in the input, renders the chips, and from then on owns the value, the filtering, the popup,
the keyboard and the form value. Its popup is a manual popover, dismissed by the model Menu and
Popover share: an outside press with the main button, a close request (Escape, the Android back
gesture), Tab, or focus moving elsewhere.

The element is also an API of its own, for scripts and other frameworks:

- `value`: the selected option's `data-value` (`""` for none), or an array with `multiple`;
  setting it selects without a `change` event.
- `open`: a property; setting it opens or closes the popup.
- `name`, `required`, `disabled`, `multiple`: reflect their attributes; `filter` is an attribute.
- `form`, `validity`, `validationMessage`, `willValidate`, `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`:
  as on native controls. It submits under `name`, resets with its form and follows a disabled
  `<fieldset>`.
- `change`: a bubbling event after the user chooses, removes or clears a value. The inner input's
  own `change` stays inside.
- `openchange`: an event (not bubbling, like `toggle`) with `detail.open`, after the popup opens or
  closes.
- The buttons are invoker commands: a `<button commandfor="<the element's id>" command="--toggle">`
  (or `"--clear"`) works anywhere on the page; where the browser lacks invoker commands, the
  element handles the clicks of those inside it.

## Browser support

- **Form-associated custom elements** (`ElementInternals`): Chrome and Edge 77, Firefox 98,
  Safari 16.4.
- **Popovers**: Chrome and Edge 114, Firefox 125, Safari 17. **`showPopover({ source })`**: Chrome
  137, Firefox 144, Safari 26; older browsers open the popup the same way.
- **CSS anchor positioning** places the popup: Chrome and Edge 125, Firefox 147, Safari 26 (partly;
  27 fully). Elsewhere the script places it with the same sides, alignment, offsets and flips.
- **Invoker commands**: Chrome 135, Firefox 144, Safari 26.2; elsewhere the element handles the
  buttons' clicks.
- **`CloseWatcher`**, for the Android back gesture: Chrome 126, Firefox 149. Elsewhere Escape still
  closes the popup.

## Related

- [Autocomplete](autocomplete.md): the same input and list for free text, when any text is fine
  and the options only suggest it.
- [Select](select.md): a native select, when the user picks from a short list without typing; it
  works without JavaScript.
- [Field](field.md): a label, a description and errors for a combobox.
- [Menu](menu.md): commands rather than values, and the dismissal model the combobox shares.
- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling, the default theme and the other components.
- [Islands](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/islands/): running a component in the
  browser, for `bind:value`, `bind:open` and async options.
- [JSX](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/jsx/): `bind:`, native events with `on:` and
  `ref`.

<!-- source: context-menu.md -->

# Context Menu

> A menu opened at the pointer by a right-click in its trigger area, a long press on a touch screen, or Shift+F10 and the ContextMenu key: Menu's popup and items, with Menu's keys, typeahead, submenus and dismissal. A 0.6 kB script on top of Menu's (3.9 kB together) opens it; without JavaScript the browser shows its own menu. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.

```ts
import { ContextMenu } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/context-menu"
import "@lumiose/ui/context-menu.css"; // Menu's layout, and no iOS callout over the area
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<ContextMenu.Root>
  <ContextMenu.Trigger />
  <ContextMenu.Popup>
    <ContextMenu.Item />
    <ContextMenu.LinkItem />
    <ContextMenu.CheckboxItem />
    <ContextMenu.Separator />
    <ContextMenu.Group>
      <ContextMenu.GroupLabel />
      <ContextMenu.Item />
    </ContextMenu.Group>
    <ContextMenu.RadioGroup>
      <ContextMenu.GroupLabel />
      <ContextMenu.RadioItem />
    </ContextMenu.RadioGroup>
    <ContextMenu.SubmenuRoot>
      <ContextMenu.SubmenuTrigger />
      <ContextMenu.Popup>…</ContextMenu.Popup>
    </ContextMenu.SubmenuRoot>
  </ContextMenu.Popup>
</ContextMenu.Root>
```

| Part                      | Renders                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`                    | `<lu-context-menu>`, an element with no box (`display: contents`) around the area and the menu; it opens the menu.                                               |
| `Trigger`                 | `<div>`: the area whose right-click, long press or keys open the menu.                                                                                           |
| `Popup`                   | Menu's `<lu-menu>` with its `<div role="menu" popover="auto" data-side="…" data-align="…">`, anchored to a zero-size `<span aria-hidden="true">` at the pointer. |
| `Item` … `SubmenuTrigger` | Menu's parts, as [Menu](menu.md#anatomy) renders them.                                                                                                           |

The popup has no trigger button to be named by: give it an `aria-label`. Inside a `SubmenuRoot`,
`Popup` is the submenu's, placed next to its trigger as in Menu.

## API

### ContextMenu.Root

| Prop           | Type                      | Default |                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                 |         | Opens or closes the menu when it changes, in the browser, where it last opened (the window's top start corner at first). Server HTML always starts closed. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |         | Called after the menu opens or closes, whatever did it: a right-click, a long press, a key, an item, Escape, a click outside or `open`.                    |
| `bind:open`    | `Signal<boolean>`         |         | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`.                                                                                                                   |
| `disabled`     | `boolean`                 | `false` | The area keeps the browser's own menu.                                                                                                                     |

### ContextMenu.Popup

Menu's [popup props](menu.md#menupopup), from the pointer: `side` (default `"bottom"`), `align`
(default `"start"`), `sideOffset` (default `0`: the popup's corner at the pointer) and
`alignOffset`. It flips when it does not fit.

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through.

- **`Trigger`**: for the keys, focus must be in the area: give it `tabindex={0}` (and a name, such
  as `aria-label`), or focusable content.
- **The items**: Menu's `Item`, `LinkItem`, `CheckboxItem`, `RadioGroup`, `RadioItem`, `Group`,
  `GroupLabel`, `Separator`, `SubmenuRoot` and `SubmenuTrigger`, with
  [Menu's props](menu.md#api): `disabled`, `label`, `closeOnClick`, `checked` and
  `onCheckedChange`, `value` and `onValueChange`, and `bind:`.

## Example

A file's actions in a server-rendered page, with no island, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { ContextMenu } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function FileActions() {
  return (
    <ContextMenu.Root>
      <ContextMenu.Trigger class="file" tabindex={0} aria-label="report.pdf">
        report.pdf
      </ContextMenu.Trigger>
      <ContextMenu.Popup class="lu-menu" aria-label="File actions">
        <ContextMenu.Item>Rename</ContextMenu.Item>
        <ContextMenu.Item>Duplicate</ContextMenu.Item>
        <ContextMenu.Separator />
        <ContextMenu.SubmenuRoot>
          <ContextMenu.SubmenuTrigger>Move to</ContextMenu.SubmenuTrigger>
          <ContextMenu.Popup class="lu-menu">
            <ContextMenu.Item>Archive</ContextMenu.Item>
            <ContextMenu.Item>Trash</ContextMenu.Item>
          </ContextMenu.Popup>
        </ContextMenu.SubmenuRoot>
      </ContextMenu.Popup>
    </ContextMenu.Root>
  );
}
```

In an island, with a checkbox item and a radio group bound to signals:

```tsx check
import { ContextMenu } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function GalleryOptions() {
  const grid = signal(true);
  const sort = signal("name");
  return (
    <>
      <ContextMenu.Root>
        <ContextMenu.Trigger class="gallery" tabindex={0} aria-label="Gallery">
          Right-click the gallery
        </ContextMenu.Trigger>
        <ContextMenu.Popup class="lu-menu" aria-label="View options">
          <ContextMenu.CheckboxItem bind:checked={grid}>Show the grid</ContextMenu.CheckboxItem>
          <ContextMenu.RadioGroup bind:value={sort}>
            <ContextMenu.GroupLabel>Sort by</ContextMenu.GroupLabel>
            <ContextMenu.RadioItem value="name">Name</ContextMenu.RadioItem>
            <ContextMenu.RadioItem value="date">Date</ContextMenu.RadioItem>
          </ContextMenu.RadioGroup>
        </ContextMenu.Popup>
      </ContextMenu.Root>
      <p>
        {grid() ? "Grid" : "No grid"}, sorted by {sort()}
      </p>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-menu` on each `Popup`, as on a Menu's: a surface with its
items, checkbox and radio marks, separators and group labels. The theme leaves the area to you.

**With your own CSS**, style the popup and items as a Menu's ([Menu: Styling](menu.md#styling)):
`:popover-open`, `[data-highlighted]`, `[aria-checked]`, `[aria-disabled]`, `[data-side]`. The
element sets `--lu-context-x` and `--lu-context-y` (the pointer, in pixels) on the root.

`@lumiose/ui/context-menu.css` holds Menu's rules and two of its own, in the `lu.core` layer:
`<lu-context-menu>` adds no box, and the area has `-webkit-touch-callout: none`, so iOS shows no
preview over the menu on a long press.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key                           | Does                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Shift+F10, ContextMenu        | With focus in the area: opens the menu below the focused element, on its first item. |
| Arrow keys, Home, End, typing | Menu's: move between items, open and close submenus, typeahead.                      |
| Enter, Space                  | Run the item (checkbox and radio items toggle and stay open).                        |
| Escape                        | Closes the menu (one submenu at a time).                                             |
| Tab, Shift+Tab                | Close the menu.                                                                      |

- **A right-click or a long press** opens the menu with focus on the popup: the arrows then reach
  the items. A right-click inside the open menu does nothing; another one in the area moves the
  menu there.
- **On close**, focus returns to where it was before the menu opened (the area, for the keys),
  unless a click outside landed on a control, which keeps it.
- **A long press** (500ms, one finger, moving less than 10px) is the touch alternative to the
  right-click, and the keys the keyboard one (WCAG 2.5.1). Offer the menu's commands elsewhere too
  when they matter: a context menu is hard to discover.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

Opening a menu at the pointer needs the script: without JavaScript a right-click shows the
browser's own menu, and the popup stays hidden. `open`, `onOpenChange` and `bind:open` need the
component to run in an island.

A page that renders a `ContextMenu` loads Menu's script and a 0.6 kB (brotli) one of its own,
3.9 kB together, without the Lumiose runtime; islands bundle them. The element opens the menu on a
right-click, a long press or the keys, at the pointer, through a zero-size anchor that it moves
there (CSS anchor positioning places the popup, with Menu's flips; without it, the shared
placement script does). Menu's script does the rest: keys, items, submenus, and dismissal shared
with [Popover](popover.md) and [Combobox](combobox.md).

## Browser support

- **CSS anchor positioning**: Chrome and Edge 125, Firefox 147, Safari 26. Elsewhere the script
  places the popup at the pointer.
- **Long press**: iOS fires no `contextmenu` on one, so the script times it; Android's
  `contextmenu` after a long press is ignored.
- **The ContextMenu key and Shift+F10**: Windows and Linux keyboards; on macOS, only Shift+F10
  where the keyboard has F10.

## Related

- [Menu](menu.md): the same popup and items, opened by a button.
- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling and the other components.

<!-- source: dialog.md -->

# Dialog

> A modal dialog, or an alert dialog that needs an answer: a native `<dialog>` opened and closed by invoker commands, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript, and a 0.8 kB script closes the native element's gaps where JavaScript runs. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.

```ts
import { Dialog } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/dialog"
import "@lumiose/ui/dialog.css"; // locks the page's scroll behind a modal dialog
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Dialog.Root>
  <Dialog.Trigger />
  <Dialog.Popup>
    <Dialog.Title />
    <Dialog.Description />
    <Dialog.Close />
  </Dialog.Popup>
</Dialog.Root>
```

| Part          | Renders                                                                                                                       |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`        | No element. Holds the state and the ids the other parts share.                                                                |
| `Trigger`     | `<button type="button" command="show-modal" commandfor="…" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="…">`                         |
| `Popup`       | `<dialog closedby="…">`, labelled by its `Title` and described by its `Description`; `role="alertdialog"` for an alert dialog |
| `Title`       | `<h2>`, which names the dialog.                                                                                               |
| `Description` | `<p>`, which describes it.                                                                                                    |
| `Close`       | `<button type="button" command="close" commandfor="…">`: its `value` becomes the dialog's `returnValue`.                      |

The trigger can sit anywhere inside `Root`, and a popup may have several close buttons. `Title` and
`Description` go inside `Popup`. A dialog may contain another `Dialog.Root`: the inner dialog
opens on top of the outer one.

## API

### Dialog.Root

| Prop           | Type                        | Default    |                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------- | --------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                   |            | Opens or closes the dialog when it changes, in the browser. Server HTML always starts closed: a modal dialog opens only from a trigger or script. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void`   |            | Called after the dialog opens or closes, whatever did it: the trigger, a close button, Escape, a click outside or `open`.                         |
| `bind:open`    | `Signal<boolean>`           |            | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`: the signal opens and closes the dialog, and follows it.                                                  |
| `role`         | `"dialog" \| "alertdialog"` | `"dialog"` | `"alertdialog"` for a confirmation that needs an answer: a click outside does not close it.                                                       |

Without `open`, `onOpenChange` or `bind:open` the dialog keeps its own state.

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through. Your props override the defaults (`type`,
`aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, `closedby`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`); `id`,
`command` and `commandfor` stay the parts' own, since they connect the parts.

- **`Trigger`**: `aria-expanded` follows the dialog in the browser. In server HTML it stays
  `"false"`, which is never wrong where assistive technology can reach it: while the modal dialog
  is open, the trigger is inert.
- **`Popup`**: `closedby` is `"any"` for a dialog (Escape or a click outside closes it) and
  `"closerequest"` for an alert dialog (Escape only); pass `closedby="none"` to allow neither. Native
  events work as on a `<dialog>`: `on:close` runs after any close, and
  `event.currentTarget.returnValue` holds the value of the `Close` that closed it (it is unchanged
  after Escape).
- **`Title`** and **`Description`**: the popup's `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` point at
  the ones it renders, and only those; in an island they follow parts that appear or go away. A
  dialog without a `Title` needs an `aria-label` on `Popup`.

## Example

A confirmation in a server-rendered page, with no island, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { Dialog } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function DeleteProject() {
  return (
    <Dialog.Root role="alertdialog">
      <Dialog.Trigger class="lu-button">Delete project…</Dialog.Trigger>
      <Dialog.Popup class="lu-dialog">
        <Dialog.Title>Delete project?</Dialog.Title>
        <Dialog.Description>This removes the project and its deployments.</Dialog.Description>
        <footer>
          <Dialog.Close class="lu-button" value="cancel">
            Cancel
          </Dialog.Close>
          <Dialog.Close class="lu-button" data-variant="destructive" value="delete">
            Delete
          </Dialog.Close>
        </footer>
      </Dialog.Popup>
    </Dialog.Root>
  );
}
```

In an island, bound to a signal: the button outside opens it, and the signal follows whatever
closes it. `bind:open={open}` is short for `open={open()}` plus
`onOpenChange={(next) => open.set(next)}`.

```tsx check
import { Dialog } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function EditProfile() {
  const open = signal(false);
  const saved = signal("");
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" class="lu-button" onClick={() => open.set(true)}>
        Edit profile
      </button>
      <Dialog.Root bind:open={open}>
        <Dialog.Popup
          class="lu-dialog"
          on:close={(event) => saved.set(event.currentTarget.returnValue)}
        >
          <Dialog.Title>Edit profile</Dialog.Title>
          <Dialog.Description>Your name as others see it.</Dialog.Description>
          <footer>
            <Dialog.Close class="lu-button" data-variant="primary" value="save">
              Save
            </Dialog.Close>
          </footer>
        </Dialog.Popup>
      </Dialog.Root>
      <p>{open() ? "Editing…" : `Last answer: ${saved() || "none"}`}</p>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-dialog` on `Popup` and `lu-button` on the buttons
(`data-variant="primary"` or `"destructive"` for filled ones). `lu-dialog` also styles the backdrop,
the title, the description and a `<footer>` for the buttons, and fades and zooms the dialog in and
out. Its colours come from the theme's `--lu-` properties ([UI components](README.md#the-default-theme)).

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class` and the dialog's native state: `dialog[open]`,
`:modal`, `::backdrop` and `[role="alertdialog"]`. Where the client script runs, a dialog with open
dialogs inside also gets `data-nested-dialog-open` and `--nested-dialogs` (how many are open inside
it), as in Base UI; `dialog:has(dialog[open])` matches the same dialogs without the script. A starting point, with a fade that keeps the dialog in the top layer while it
closes:

```css
.dialog {
  inline-size: min(28rem, 100vw - 2rem);
  padding: 1.25rem;
  border: 1px solid #d4d4d8;
  border-radius: 0.75rem;
  box-shadow: 0 10px 30px -10px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35);
}
.dialog::backdrop {
  background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45);
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
  .dialog,
  .dialog::backdrop {
    transition:
      opacity 150ms ease-out,
      overlay 150ms allow-discrete,
      display 150ms allow-discrete;
  }
  .dialog:not([open]),
  .dialog:not([open])::backdrop {
    opacity: 0;
  }
  @starting-style {
    .dialog[open],
    .dialog[open]::backdrop {
      opacity: 0;
    }
  }
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/dialog.css` holds one rule, in the `lu.core` layer: the page behind any modal
`<dialog>` does not scroll, and keeps its scrollbar's space so the layout does not shift
(`:root:has(dialog:modal) { overflow: hidden; scrollbar-gutter: stable }`). Leave the stylesheet out,
or override the rule, to let the page scroll.

## Keyboard and focus

The browser's modal dialog provides the
[WAI-ARIA dialog pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/):

| Key            | Does                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter, Space   | On the trigger: opens the dialog.                                                                    |
| Tab, Shift+Tab | Move between the focusable elements of the dialog. The page behind is inert: focus never reaches it. |
| Escape         | Closes the dialog on top, alert dialogs included. With nested dialogs, one Escape closes one dialog. |

- **On open**, focus moves to the element with `autofocus`, or else the first focusable element
  inside, or else the dialog. Opened by touch, the dialog focuses itself instead, so no virtual
  keyboard opens over it (an `autofocus` element still gets focus).
- **On close**, focus returns to the element that had it before: the trigger, or the button that
  set the signal. If that element is gone, focus goes to another trigger of the dialog, without
  scrolling the page.
- **A click outside** closes a dialog, not an alert dialog, and only the dialog on top. A press
  that starts inside and ends outside, such as selecting text, does not count, and neither does a
  right-click or a second finger.
- Popups opened from a dialog (a menu, a select) belong inside its `Popup`: everything outside a
  modal dialog is inert.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

The trigger, the close buttons, Escape and the click outside are HTML features: a dialog in a
server-rendered page works before any script loads, and with none. `open`, `onOpenChange`,
`bind:open` and a live `aria-expanded` need the component to run in the browser, in an island.

Where the native element falls short of Base UI's dialog, a small script closes the gap: a page
that renders a `Dialog` loads it once, as a 0.8 kB (brotli) module without the Lumiose runtime, and
islands bundle it. It covers every `<dialog>` on the page:

- a right-click or a second finger outside does not close the dialog;
- `data-nested-dialog-open` and `--nested-dialogs` on a dialog with open dialogs inside;
- a dialog opened by touch focuses itself;
- focus returns without scrolling, to the opener or, if it is gone, another trigger (WebKit, which
  does not focus a clicked button, would otherwise leave focus on the page);
- the click outside where the browser lacks `closedby` (Safari), and the invoker commands where it
  lacks them.

Until the script loads (or without JavaScript) the dialog behaves as the browser's own.

## Browser support

- **Invoker commands** (`command`, `commandfor`) open and close the dialog: Chrome and Edge 135,
  Firefox 144, Safari 26.2. In older browsers the client script stands in for them; without
  JavaScript the trigger and the close buttons do nothing there.
- **`closedby`**: Chrome 134 and Firefox 141; Safari only in Technology Preview. Elsewhere the
  client script closes the dialog on a click outside; without JavaScript only Escape does.
- **Exit animations** that keep the dialog in the top layer (`overlay`) are Chromium-only.
  Elsewhere the dialog leaves the top layer as soon as it starts closing.

## Related

- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling, the default theme and the other components.
- [Islands](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/islands/): running a component in the browser, for `open` and
  `onOpenChange`.
- [JSX](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/jsx/): native events with `on:` and `ref`.

<!-- source: drawer.md -->

# Drawer

> A panel that slides in from an edge of the window and that a swipe toward that edge closes: a Dialog (a native modal `<dialog>` opened by an invoker command, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript) against the edge its `swipeDirection` names. A 1 kB script adds the swipe, with the close buttons, Escape and a click on the backdrop as its alternatives. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.

```ts
import { Drawer } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/drawer"
import "@lumiose/ui/drawer.css"; // puts the dialog against its edge; locks the page's scroll
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Drawer.Root>
  <Drawer.Trigger />
  <Drawer.Popup>
    <Drawer.Title />
    <Drawer.Description />
    <Drawer.Content />
    <Drawer.Close />
  </Drawer.Popup>
</Drawer.Root>
```

| Part          | Renders                                                                                                             |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`        | No element. Holds the state and the ids the other parts share, as `Dialog.Root`.                                    |
| `Trigger`     | `<button type="button" command="show-modal" commandfor="…" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="…">`, as Dialog's. |
| `Popup`       | `<dialog closedby="any" data-swipe-direction="…">`, labelled by its `Title` and described by its `Description`.     |
| `Content`     | `<div>` around the drawer's content, which may scroll.                                                              |
| `Title`       | `<h2>`, which names the drawer.                                                                                     |
| `Description` | `<p>`, which describes it.                                                                                          |
| `Close`       | `<button type="button" command="close" commandfor="…">`, as Dialog's.                                               |

`Trigger`, `Title`, `Description` and `Close` are [Dialog's](dialog.md#anatomy). A drawer is
modal: the page behind it is inert, and focus stays inside.

## API

### Drawer.Root

| Prop             | Type                                  | Default  |                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`           | `boolean`                             |          | Opens or closes the drawer when it changes, in the browser. Server HTML always starts closed: a modal dialog opens only from a trigger or script. |
| `onOpenChange`   | `(open: boolean) => void`             |          | Called after the drawer opens or closes, whatever did it: the trigger, a close button, Escape, a click outside, a swipe or `open`.                |
| `bind:open`      | `Signal<boolean>`                     |          | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`.                                                                                                          |
| `swipeDirection` | `"down" \| "up" \| "left" \| "right"` | `"down"` | The direction a swipe closes the drawer in, and the window's edge it sits against: `"down"` is a bottom sheet.                                    |

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through, as Dialog's do ([Dialog: API](dialog.md#api)): `closedby`
on `Popup` (`"closerequest"` keeps a click outside from closing it), `on:close` and the close
buttons' `value`.

- **`Content`**: a swipe that starts in content that can still scroll toward the drawer's edge
  scrolls it instead, until it reaches its end. When it scrolls, make it focusable for the
  keyboard: `tabindex={0}` with `role="region"` and an `aria-label`.
- **`[data-swipe-ignore]`** on any element inside keeps swipes from starting on it, as on buttons,
  links and fields.

## Example

A bottom sheet in a server-rendered page, with no island, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { Drawer } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function FiltersSheet() {
  return (
    <Drawer.Root>
      <Drawer.Trigger class="lu-button">Filters</Drawer.Trigger>
      <Drawer.Popup class="lu-drawer">
        <Drawer.Title>Filters</Drawer.Title>
        <Drawer.Description>Swipe down, or press Done, to close.</Drawer.Description>
        <footer>
          <Drawer.Close class="lu-button" data-variant="primary">
            Done
          </Drawer.Close>
        </footer>
      </Drawer.Popup>
    </Drawer.Root>
  );
}
```

In an island, a side drawer bound to a signal: `bind:open={open}` is short for `open={open()}`
plus `onOpenChange={(next) => open.set(next)}`, and the signal follows a swipe too.

```tsx check
import { Drawer } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function NavigationDrawer() {
  const open = signal(false);
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" class="lu-button" onClick={() => open.set(true)}>
        Menu
      </button>
      <Drawer.Root bind:open={open} swipeDirection="left">
        <Drawer.Popup class="lu-drawer">
          <Drawer.Title>Menu</Drawer.Title>
          <Drawer.Description>Swipe left to close.</Drawer.Description>
          <Drawer.Close class="lu-button">Close</Drawer.Close>
        </Drawer.Popup>
      </Drawer.Root>
      <p>{open() ? "The menu is open" : "The menu is closed"}</p>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-drawer` on `Popup`: a surface against its edge, rounded on the
inside, with a handle on a bottom sheet, the title, the description and a `<footer>` styled. It
slides in and out from its edge, follows a swipe, and leaves from where the swipe let go; the
backdrop fades with it.

**With your own CSS**, style the drawer through `class`, `[data-swipe-direction]`, `dialog[open]`
and `::backdrop`, and the swipe through the script's state, named as in Base UI:

- `[data-swiping]` while a swipe runs, with `--drawer-swipe-movement-x` or
  `--drawer-swipe-movement-y` (pixels, toward the edge) and `--drawer-swipe-progress` (0 to 1,
  for the backdrop);
- `[data-swipe-dismiss]` (the direction) when a swipe closed it, until it has left.

```css
.drawer {
  translate: var(--drawer-swipe-movement-x, 0) var(--drawer-swipe-movement-y, 0);
  transition:
    translate 250ms ease-out,
    overlay 250ms allow-discrete,
    display 250ms allow-discrete;
}
.drawer[data-swiping] {
  transition: none;
}
.drawer[data-swipe-direction="down"]:not([open]) {
  translate: 0 100%;
}
@starting-style {
  .drawer[data-swipe-direction="down"][open] {
    translate: 0 100%;
  }
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/drawer.css` holds Dialog's scroll lock and, in the `lu.core` layer, puts each
`dialog[data-swipe-direction]` against its edge, across that edge's length, instead of the
browser's centred box; a swiped drawer selects no text.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key            | Does                                                                         |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter, Space   | On the trigger: opens the drawer.                                            |
| Tab, Shift+Tab | Move between the focusable elements of the drawer; the page behind is inert. |
| Escape         | Closes the drawer on top.                                                    |

- **Focus** moves into the drawer on open and returns to the trigger on close, a swipe included, as
  with [Dialog](dialog.md#keyboard-and-focus).
- **A swipe** is a dragging movement: the close buttons, Escape and a click on the backdrop close
  the drawer without one (WCAG 2.5.7). Give a drawer a visible close button.
- **The swipe** needs to travel 40% of the drawer's size toward its edge, or to be a quick flick;
  shorter, the drawer springs back. It never starts on a button, link or field.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

The trigger, the close buttons, Escape and the click outside are HTML features, as for Dialog: a
drawer in a server-rendered page works before any script loads, and with none, against its edge.
`open`, `onOpenChange` and `bind:open` need the component to run in an island.

A page that renders a `Drawer` loads Dialog's script and a 1 kB (brotli) one of its own (1.9 kB
together), without the Lumiose runtime; islands bundle them. The drawer's script handles the
swipe, with the mouse and pen through pointer events and on touch screens through touch events,
taking the gesture from scrolling only once it is a swipe.

Not in this Drawer, next to Base UI's: snap points, a swipe area that opens the drawer from the
edge, indented backgrounds, the virtual keyboard provider, detached triggers (`createHandle`), and
non-modal drawers.

## Browser support

- **`<dialog>`, invoker commands and `closedby`**: as for [Dialog](dialog.md#browser-support).
- **Exit animations** that keep the drawer in the top layer (`overlay`) are Chromium-only.
  Elsewhere it leaves the top layer as soon as it starts closing.

## Related

- [Dialog](dialog.md): the same parts, centred.
- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling and the other components.

<!-- source: field.md -->

# Field

> A form field: a label, a native control, a description and its errors, wired with `for`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`, after Base UI's Field. Validation is the browser's constraint validation (`required`, `type`, `pattern`, `minlength`…); a 1.0 kB script shows it in the field's Error parts at the right time, instead of the browser's bubble, and focuses the first invalid field on submit. A Form's server errors render in the HTML, so they work without JavaScript.

```ts
import { Field } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/field"
import "@lumiose/ui/field.css"; // makes <lu-field> a block, keeps hidden errors hidden
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Field.Root>
  <Field.Label />
  <Field.Control />
  <Field.Description />
  <Field.Error />
</Field.Root>
```

| Part          | Renders                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`        | `<lu-field>`, a block around the other parts, with `validation-mode`.                                                                        |
| `Label`       | `<label for="…">`, pointing at the control.                                                                                                  |
| `Control`     | `<input>`: [Input](input.md), with the field's `id`, `name`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`.                                          |
| `Description` | `<p>` that describes the control.                                                                                                            |
| `Error`       | `<output hidden>`: without children, the field's message (`for` the control); with children, your message. Shown while the field is invalid. |

Instead of `Field.Control`, a field can hold a [Checkbox](checkbox.md), a [Switch](switch.md), a
[Select](select.md), a [Radio Group](radio-group.md), a [Combobox](combobox.md), an
[Autocomplete](autocomplete.md), a [Number Field](number-field.md) or a [Slider](slider.md): they
take the field's wiring the same way (a Combobox and an Autocomplete through their input).

## API

### Field.Root

| Prop             | Type                                           | Default      |                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`           | `string`                                       |              | The control's `name` (unless it has its own), and the key of the field's errors in the Form's `errors`.                                     |
| `disabled`       | `boolean`                                      | `false`      | Disables the control.                                                                                                                       |
| `invalid`        | `boolean`                                      | `false`      | Marks the field invalid, as a server error does: its Error shows and the control gets `aria-invalid`, until the value changes.              |
| `validationMode` | `"onSubmit" \| "onBlur" \| "onChange"`         | `"onSubmit"` | When errors show: after a submit attempt, also when the control loses focus, or as soon as it is edited. Once shown, they follow the value. |
| `validate`       | `(value: string \| boolean) => string \| null` |              | Your own check, run on every edit in an island: return a message when the value is invalid. It becomes the control's custom validity.       |

`Root` passes `class`, `style` and other element props to `<lu-field>`. A Form's `validationMode`
applies to the fields that set none.

### Field.Error

| Prop       | Type                          | Default |                                                                                                        |
| ---------- | ----------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `match`    | `keyof ValidityState \| true` |         | Shows only for that problem (`"valueMissing"`, `"typeMismatch"`, `"tooShort"`, …), or always (`true`). |
| `children` | `JSX.Element`                 |         | Your message. Without children, the Error shows the server's message or the browser's.                 |

### Field.Control

[Input](input.md)'s props: every native `<input>` prop, plus `value`, `defaultValue`,
`onValueChange` and `bind:value`.

### The other parts

`Label` and `Description` take the props of the element they render (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`)
and pass them through; their `id` and `for` stay the field's.

**Differences from Base UI's Field.** The control is native and so is validation: there is no
`Field.Validity`, no async `validate` or `validationDebounceTime`, and no `dirty`, `touched`,
`actionsRef` or `Field.Item`. State is exposed the platform's way, `aria-invalid` on the control
and `:user-invalid`, `:invalid`, `:focus-within` in CSS, rather than Base UI's `data-dirty`,
`data-touched` and friends. `Field.Error` renders an `<output>`, not a `<div>`.

## Example

An email field in a server-rendered page, with no island:

```tsx check
import { Field } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function EmailField() {
  return (
    <form method="post">
      <Field.Root name="email" validationMode="onBlur" class="lu-field">
        <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
        <Field.Control type="email" required autocomplete="email" class="lu-input" />
        <Field.Description>We never share it.</Field.Description>
        <Field.Error match="valueMissing">Enter your email.</Field.Error>
        <Field.Error match="typeMismatch">Enter an email like ada@example.com.</Field.Error>
      </Field.Root>
      <button class="lu-button">Subscribe</button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

With a form action, a [Form](form.md)'s `errors` (the data the action passes to `fail()`) show in
the field of the same `name`, in the page the server renders back:

```tsx check
import { Field, Form } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function UsernameField(props: { errors?: { username?: string } }) {
  return (
    <Form method="post" errors={props.errors}>
      <Field.Root name="username" class="lu-field">
        <Field.Label>Username</Field.Label>
        <Field.Control required minlength={3} class="lu-input" />
        <Field.Error />
      </Field.Root>
      <button class="lu-button">Sign up</button>
    </Form>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-field` on `Root` and `lu-input` on the control: the parts
stack with a small gap, the label is medium weight, the description muted, the errors red (a
lighter red in dark, to keep 4.5:1), and an invalid control gets a red border.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class` and state:

- the control: `[aria-invalid="true"]` while an error shows, `:user-invalid` (invalid after the
  user interacted), `:invalid`, `:focus-visible`, `:disabled`;
- the field: `lu-field:has([aria-invalid="true"])`, `lu-field:focus-within`;
- the errors: `output` in the field (`[hidden]` while they do not apply).

```css
.field {
  display: grid;
  gap: 0.25rem;
}
.field [aria-invalid="true"] {
  border-color: #dc2626;
}
.field output {
  color: #b91c1c;
  font-size: 0.875rem;
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/field.css` holds what Field needs to work, in the `lu.core` layer: `lu-field` is a
block, and the errors the script hides stay hidden whatever `display` your CSS gives them.

## Keyboard and focus

The control's own keyboard. Field adds focus on a submit attempt: the first invalid control of the
form, in DOM order, takes focus, and its error is part of its accessible description, so a screen
reader reads it there.

- **On a submit attempt**, every invalid field shows its errors; the browser's bubble does not
  appear for a field with an Error part.
- **`validationMode="onBlur"`** shows a field's error when focus leaves it, except a missing value
  in a field the user has not edited yet (Base UI's rule). **`"onChange"`** shows it as the user
  types.
- **Once shown**, an error follows the value: it updates as the problem changes and goes away when
  the value is valid. A server error goes away as soon as the value changes.
- **A form reset** hides every error.

## Without JavaScript, and the field's script

The control, its `for` label and its constraints are native: the browser validates on submit and
reports the first problem in its own bubble, and the form submits when everything is valid. Server
errors from a Form render in the HTML, visible and linked with `aria-describedby` and
`aria-invalid`.

A page that renders a `Field` loads a 1.0 kB (brotli) script once, without the Lumiose runtime;
islands bundle it. It cancels the browser's `invalid` bubble for fields that have an Error part and
shows the problem there instead (the browser's message, or one your `validate` set), with the
timing above, focuses the first invalid control on a submit attempt, keeps `aria-invalid` and
`aria-describedby` current (a description rendered after the control is linked once the script
runs), and hides server errors once the value changes.

## Browser support

- **Constraint validation**, `:user-invalid` (Chrome 119, Firefox 88, Safari 16.5) and the
  `invalid` event: in every supported browser.
- **`<output for>`**: in every browser; Chromium and screen readers include an output's text in
  the control's description. Playwright's own `toHaveAccessibleDescription` leaves it out; the
  @lumiose/ui tests read Chromium's computation instead.

## Related

- [Form](form.md): server errors for the fields, by name.
- [Input](input.md): `Field.Control`.
- [Fieldset](fieldset.md): a group of fields with a legend.
- [Checkbox](checkbox.md), [Switch](switch.md), [Radio Group](radio-group.md),
  [Select](select.md), [Combobox](combobox.md), [Autocomplete](autocomplete.md),
  [Number Field](number-field.md), [Slider](slider.md): controls that take a field's wiring.
- [Data and actions](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/data-and-actions/): form actions,
  `fail()` and `actionData()`.

<!-- source: fieldset.md -->

# Fieldset

> A group of related fields with a caption: a native `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`, after Base UI's Fieldset. The browser names the group by its legend and disables every control inside a disabled fieldset, with no JavaScript and no CSS of its own. The legend also names a Checkbox Group or a Radio Group.

```ts
import { Fieldset } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/fieldset"
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Fieldset.Root>
  <Fieldset.Legend />
</Fieldset.Root>
```

| Part     | Renders                                             |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`   | `<fieldset>`, a group (`role="group"`).             |
| `Legend` | `<legend>`, which names the group; the first child. |

## API

### Fieldset.Root

| Prop       | Type      | Default |                                                                               |
| ---------- | --------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables every control inside, except those in its legend; none is submitted. |

Every other `<fieldset>` prop (`form`, `name`, `class`, `aria-*`) passes through.

### Fieldset.Legend

The `<legend>`'s props pass through. Put it first in the fieldset, or first in a
[CheckboxGroup](checkbox-group.md) or [RadioGroup](radio-group.md), which render a fieldset too.

**Differences from Base UI's Fieldset.** `Legend` is a native `<legend>` (Base UI renders a
`<div>` labelling the fieldset), so the group is named without ARIA.

## Example

```tsx check
import { Field, Fieldset } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function AddressFields() {
  return (
    <Fieldset.Root class="lu-fieldset">
      <Fieldset.Legend>Shipping address</Fieldset.Legend>
      <Field.Root name="street" class="lu-field">
        <Field.Label>Street</Field.Label>
        <Field.Control autocomplete="street-address" class="lu-input" />
      </Field.Root>
      <Field.Root name="city" class="lu-field">
        <Field.Label>City</Field.Label>
        <Field.Control autocomplete="address-level2" class="lu-input" />
      </Field.Root>
    </Fieldset.Root>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-fieldset` on `Root`: no border or padding, the legend
semi-bold, the fields in a column.

**With your own CSS**, style the `fieldset` and `legend`, and `:disabled` (`fieldset:disabled`
matches a disabled fieldset; its controls match `:disabled`). A fieldset's minimum width defaults
to its content's: set `min-inline-size: 0` to let it shrink.

Fieldset ships no stylesheet: it needs none to work.

## Keyboard and focus

The controls' own. A fieldset is not focusable; a disabled fieldset takes its controls out of the
tab order. Screen readers announce the legend when focus enters the group.

## Without JavaScript

Everything is native: the group, its name, and `disabled`, in server HTML. No script.

## Browser support

`<fieldset>`, `<legend>` and `fieldset[disabled]`: every browser.

## Related

- [Field](field.md): the fields inside.
- [Checkbox Group](checkbox-group.md) and [Radio Group](radio-group.md): groups of choices, named
  by a `Fieldset.Legend`.
- [Form](form.md).

<!-- source: form.md -->

# Form

> A native `<form>` that hands its fields the server's errors, after Base UI's Form. Pass the data a form action gives `fail()` as `errors`, and each [Field](field.md) shows the message for its `name`, in the HTML the server renders back (no JavaScript needed) or, with `submit()`, in an island. Submission, validation and the first invalid field's focus are the platform's and Field's.

```ts
import { Form } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/form"
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Form>
  <Field.Root />
</Form>
```

| Part   | Renders                               |
| ------ | ------------------------------------- |
| `Form` | `<form>`, with the props it is given. |

## API

### Form

| Prop             | Type                                   | Default      |                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `errors`         | `object`                               |              | The server's errors by field name: a message or several for each `Field.Root` `name`, such as `actionData()` after a `fail()`. |
| `validationMode` | `"onSubmit" \| "onBlur" \| "onChange"` | `"onSubmit"` | When the fields show their errors, unless a field sets its own.                                                                |

Every other `<form>` prop passes through: `method`, `action`, `onSubmit` (Lumiose's `submit`),
`novalidate`, `class`.

**Differences from Base UI's Form.** No `onFormSubmit` or `actionsRef`: the form is native and
Lumiose's form actions post it (`action="?/name"`, `onSubmit={submit}`). Base UI sets
`noValidate`; here the browser's validation stays on, so it still works without JavaScript, and
Field's script shows the problems in the fields instead of the browser's bubble.

## Example

A sign-up page whose action checks the username on the server:

```tsx check
import { Field, Form } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { actionData, fail, type ActionContext } from "lumiose";

export const actions = {
  async signup(ctx: ActionContext) {
    const form = await ctx.formData();
    if (form.get("username") === "admin") {
      return fail(400, { username: "That username is taken." });
    }
    return { welcome: String(form.get("username")) };
  },
};

export function SignupForm() {
  const result = actionData<typeof actions>();
  return (
    <Form method="post" action="?/signup" errors={result}>
      <Field.Root name="username" class="lu-field">
        <Field.Label>Username</Field.Label>
        <Field.Control required minlength={3} autocomplete="username" class="lu-input" />
        <Field.Error />
      </Field.Root>
      <button class="lu-button" data-variant="primary">
        Sign up
      </button>
    </Form>
  );
}
```

`errors={result}` works whatever else the action returns: only the keys that name a field and hold
a string or an array of strings become errors. In an island, add `onSubmit={submit}` and the
errors arrive without a page load.

## Styling

Form adds nothing to style: style the `form` and its state, `form:invalid` (a field is invalid)
and `form:has(:user-invalid)` (one the user touched is), and its fields
([Field](field.md#styling)). Form ships no stylesheet.

## Keyboard and focus

The platform's: Enter in a text field submits the form. On a submit attempt with invalid fields,
nothing is sent, the fields show their errors, and the first invalid control takes focus (Field's
script; without it, the browser focuses it and shows its bubble).

## Without JavaScript

A native form posts to its action and the page renders back with `actionData()`, so the server's
errors show in their fields with no script. The browser validates the fields before it posts.

## Browser support

Every browser. Field's script needs the `invalid` event and constraint validation, which every
supported browser has.

## Related

- [Field](field.md): the fields and their errors.
- [Fieldset](fieldset.md): groups of fields.
- [Data and actions](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/data-and-actions/): form actions,
  `fail()`, `actionData()` and `submit()`.

<!-- source: input.md -->

# Input

> A native `<input>`, after Base UI's Input: every type, constraint and autofill the browser has, plus `onValueChange` and `bind:value`. Inside a [Field](field.md) (as `Field.Control`) it takes the field's id, name and ARIA references. No script, no CSS of its own.

```ts
import { Input } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/input"
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Input />
```

| Part    | Renders                                |
| ------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `Input` | `<input>`, with the props it is given. |

## API

### Input

| Prop            | Type                      | Default |                                                                             |
| --------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string`                  |         | Sets the value when it changes. Pair it with `onValueChange`.               |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                  |         | The value at first, when `value` is left out; a form reset goes back to it. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |         | Called with the new value on every edit.                                    |
| `bind:value`    | `Signal<string>`          |         | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                  |

Every native `<input>` prop passes through: `type`, `name`, `required`, `pattern`, `minlength`,
`placeholder`, `autocomplete`, `readonly`, `disabled`, `class`, `aria-*`, events. Inside a Field,
its own `id`, `name`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid` win over the field's.

**Differences from Base UI's Input.** The same element and props; `bind:value` stands in for the
pair.

## Example

A search box in an island, bound to a signal:

```tsx check
import { Input } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

const BOOKS = ["Dune", "Emma", "Ulysses", "Middlemarch"];

export function BookSearch() {
  const query = signal("");
  const found = () => BOOKS.filter((book) => book.toLowerCase().includes(query().toLowerCase()));
  return (
    <search>
      <Input type="search" aria-label="Search books" bind:value={query} class="lu-input" />
      <p>{found().join(", ") || "No books."}</p>
    </search>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-input` on it: a bordered field, a muted placeholder, a focus
ring, a red border with `aria-invalid="true"`.

**With your own CSS**, style the `input` and its state: `:focus-visible`, `:disabled`,
`:read-only`, `:placeholder-shown`, `:user-invalid`, `[aria-invalid="true"]`.

Input ships no stylesheet: it needs none to work.

## Keyboard and focus

The browser's text-field keyboard. One tab stop.

## Without JavaScript

A native input: typing, autofill, validation and submission work with no script. `value`,
`onValueChange` and `bind:value` need the component to run in an island.

## Browser support

Every browser; input types and constraints as the browser supports them.

## Related

- [Field](field.md): label, description and errors for an Input (`Field.Control`).
- [Combobox](combobox.md): an input that filters options.
- [JSX](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/jsx/): `bind:value`.

<!-- source: menu.md -->

# Menu

> A menu of commands, links, checkbox and radio items and submenus, opened by a button: the trigger's `popovertarget` opens it and CSS anchor positioning places it, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript, and a 3.3 kB script adds the APG Menu Button keyboard contract where JavaScript runs. `bind:open`, `bind:checked` and `bind:value` keep signals in sync in islands.

```ts
import { Menu } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/menu"
import "@lumiose/ui/menu.css"; // places the popup next to its trigger and stacks the items
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Menu.Root>
  <Menu.Trigger />
  <Menu.Popup>
    <Menu.Item />
    <Menu.LinkItem />
    <Menu.CheckboxItem />
    <Menu.Separator />
    <Menu.Group>
      <Menu.GroupLabel />
      <Menu.Item />
    </Menu.Group>
    <Menu.RadioGroup>
      <Menu.GroupLabel />
      <Menu.RadioItem />
    </Menu.RadioGroup>
    <Menu.SubmenuRoot>
      <Menu.SubmenuTrigger />
      <Menu.Popup>…</Menu.Popup>
    </Menu.SubmenuRoot>
  </Menu.Popup>
</Menu.Root>
```

| Part             | Renders                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`           | `<lu-menu>`, an element with no box (`display: contents`) that holds the menu's state and adds the keyboard contract.                                |
| `Trigger`        | `<button type="button" popovertarget="…" aria-haspopup="menu">`; `aria-expanded` follows the menu once the script runs.                              |
| `Popup`          | `<div role="menu" popover="auto" tabindex="-1" data-side="…" data-align="…">`, labelled by its trigger; `popover="manual"` once the script opens it. |
| `Item`           | `<button type="button" role="menuitem">`: a command.                                                                                                 |
| `LinkItem`       | `<a role="menuitem">`: a link.                                                                                                                       |
| `CheckboxItem`   | `<button type="button" role="menuitemcheckbox" aria-checked="…">`                                                                                    |
| `Separator`      | `<div role="separator">`                                                                                                                             |
| `Group`          | `<div role="group">`, labelled by its `GroupLabel`.                                                                                                  |
| `GroupLabel`     | `<div role="presentation">`, which names its `Group` or `RadioGroup`.                                                                                |
| `RadioGroup`     | `<div role="group">` of radio items, one of them checked.                                                                                            |
| `RadioItem`      | `<button type="button" role="menuitemradio" value="…" aria-checked="…">`                                                                             |
| `SubmenuRoot`    | `<lu-menu>` for a submenu, inside a `Popup`.                                                                                                         |
| `SubmenuTrigger` | `<button type="button" role="menuitem" popovertarget="…" aria-haspopup="menu">`: an item of the parent menu.                                         |

The trigger and the popup sit inside `Root`; a submenu's trigger and popup sit inside its
`SubmenuRoot`, which sits in the parent's `Popup`, as deep as you like. Items, groups and separators
go inside a `Popup`, radio items inside a `RadioGroup`.

## API

### Menu.Root

| Prop           | Type                      | Default |                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                 |         | Opens or closes the menu when it changes, in the browser. Server HTML always starts closed: a popover opens only from its trigger or script. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |         | Called after the menu opens or closes, whatever did it: the trigger, a key, a click outside, an item that ran, `open`.                       |
| `bind:open`    | `Signal<boolean>`         |         | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`: the signal opens and closes the menu, and follows it.                                               |

Without `open`, `onOpenChange` or `bind:open` the menu keeps its own state. A menu opened from the
server HTML before its island hydrated stays open, and `onOpenChange(true)` tells the signal.
`Menu.SubmenuRoot` takes the same props, for its submenu.

### Menu.Popup

| Prop          | Type                                                                       | Default                                 |                                                                      |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `side`        | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "inline-start" \| "inline-end"` | `"bottom"`, `"inline-end"` in a submenu | The trigger's side the popup goes on. It flips when it does not fit. |
| `align`       | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"`                                             | `"start"`                               | How the popup aligns with the trigger along that side.               |
| `sideOffset`  | `number`                                                                   |                                         | The gap between the trigger and the popup, in CSS pixels.            |
| `alignOffset` | `number`                                                                   |                                         | A shift along the side, away from the aligned edge, in CSS pixels.   |

### Menu.Item

| Prop           | Type                          | Default |                                                                                                             |
