| -------------- | ----------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onClick`      | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |         | Runs the command, on a click, Enter or Space. The menu has closed and focus is back on the trigger by then. |
| `disabled`     | `boolean`                     | `false` | Unavailable (`aria-disabled`): the arrows and typeahead still reach it, but it does not run.                |
| `label`        | `string`                      |         | The text typeahead matches, when the item's text content is not it.                                         |
| `closeOnClick` | `boolean`                     | `true`  | Whether running the item closes the menu.                                                                   |

### Menu.LinkItem

| Prop           | Type      | Default |                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `href`         | `string`  |         | Where the link goes. A Ctrl, Cmd or Shift click, or a link with `download`, leaves the menu open.                                                                            |
| `label`        | `string`  |         | The text typeahead matches.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `closeOnClick` | `boolean` | `true`  | Whether following the link closes the menu. Base UI keeps it open by default; here it closes, like the other items, since a layout's menu outlives a client-side navigation. |

### Menu.CheckboxItem

| Prop              | Type                         | Default |                                                                              |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checked`         | `boolean`                    |         | Checks or unchecks the item when it changes. Pair it with `onCheckedChange`. |
| `defaultChecked`  | `boolean`                    | `false` | Whether it starts checked when `checked` is left out.                        |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` |         | Called after a click, Enter or Space checks or unchecks it.                  |
| `bind:checked`    | `Signal<boolean>`            |         | Stands in for `checked` and `onCheckedChange`.                               |
| `disabled`        | `boolean`                    | `false` | Unavailable: it can be highlighted, but it does not toggle.                  |
| `label`           | `string`                     |         | The text typeahead matches.                                                  |
| `closeOnClick`    | `boolean`                    | `false` | Whether toggling it closes the menu.                                         |

### Menu.RadioGroup

| Prop            | Type                      | Default |                                                                                        |
| --------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string`                  |         | Checks the radio item with this `value` when it changes. Pair it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                  |         | The radio item checked at first when `value` is left out.                              |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |         | Called with the `value` of the radio item a click, Enter or Space checks.              |
| `bind:value`    | `Signal<string>`          |         | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                             |

### Menu.RadioItem

| Prop           | Type      | Default |                                                            |
| -------------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`        | `string`  |         | Required: the value its group takes when it is checked.    |
| `disabled`     | `boolean` | `false` | Unavailable: it can be highlighted, but it is not checked. |
| `label`        | `string`  |         | The text typeahead matches.                                |
| `closeOnClick` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether checking it closes the menu.                       |

### Menu.SubmenuTrigger

| Prop       | Type      | Default |                                                                    |
| ---------- | --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Unavailable: it can be highlighted, but its submenu does not open. |
| `label`    | `string`  |         | The text typeahead matches in the parent menu.                     |

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through. Your props override the defaults (`type`, `tabindex`,
`aria-labelledby`, `data-side`, `data-align`); the roles, `id`, `popovertarget` and the anchor
stay the parts' own, since they connect the parts. Your `style` is kept, after the anchor's.

- **`Trigger`**: `aria-expanded` is left to the browser in server HTML, where `popovertarget`
  implies it, and set by the script once it runs. Disable it with the native `disabled`.
- **`Group`** and **`RadioGroup`**: `aria-labelledby` points at their `GroupLabel` while one
  renders; without one, give the group an `aria-label`.
- **`Separator`**: a horizontal rule between items; `aria-orientation` passes through.

**Differences from Base UI's Menu.** No `Portal`, `Positioner`, `Backdrop` or `Arrow`: the top
layer and anchor positioning replace them, and the placement props go on `Popup`. The menu is not
modal: the page keeps scrolling (the popup follows its trigger), and a press outside closes the
menu and reaches what it lands on. Items render buttons, so they run with Enter and Space without
the script. There are no indicator parts: style `[aria-checked="true"]`. Submenus open on hover
after 100 ms, which no prop changes, and the root trigger does not open on hover.

## Example

A menu in a server-rendered page, with no island, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { Menu } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function ProjectMenu() {
  return (
    <Menu.Root>
      <Menu.Trigger class="lu-button">Project</Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu">
        <Menu.LinkItem href="/settings">Settings</Menu.LinkItem>
        <Menu.LinkItem href="/members">Members</Menu.LinkItem>
        <Menu.Separator />
        <Menu.SubmenuRoot>
          <Menu.SubmenuTrigger>Export</Menu.SubmenuTrigger>
          <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu">
            <Menu.LinkItem href="/export.csv" download>
              CSV
            </Menu.LinkItem>
            <Menu.LinkItem href="/export.json" download>
              JSON
            </Menu.LinkItem>
          </Menu.Popup>
        </Menu.SubmenuRoot>
      </Menu.Popup>
    </Menu.Root>
  );
}
```

In an island, with a command, a checkbox item and a radio group bound to signals, and a status
line that follows them. `bind:checked={wrap}` is short for `checked={wrap()}` plus
`onCheckedChange={(next) => wrap.set(next)}`, and `bind:value` likewise.

```tsx check
import { Menu } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function EditorMenu() {
  const formatted = signal(0);
  const wrap = signal(true);
  const indent = signal("spaces");
  return (
    <>
      <Menu.Root>
        <Menu.Trigger class="lu-button">View</Menu.Trigger>
        <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu" align="end">
          <Menu.Item onClick={() => formatted.set(formatted() + 1)}>Format document</Menu.Item>
          <Menu.Item disabled>Fold all</Menu.Item>
          <Menu.Separator />
          <Menu.CheckboxItem bind:checked={wrap}>Wrap lines</Menu.CheckboxItem>
          <Menu.RadioGroup bind:value={indent}>
            <Menu.GroupLabel>Indent with</Menu.GroupLabel>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="spaces">Spaces</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="tabs">Tabs</Menu.RadioItem>
          </Menu.RadioGroup>
        </Menu.Popup>
      </Menu.Root>
      <p>
        Formatted {formatted()} times, lines {wrap() ? "wrap" : "do not wrap"}, indent with{" "}
        {indent()}.
      </p>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-menu` on every `Popup`, submenus included, and `lu-button` on
the trigger. `lu-menu` styles the surface, the items (highlighted, disabled, focus ring), the
checkbox and radio marks, the arrow of a submenu trigger, the separators and the group labels, and
fades the popup in and out. Its colours come from the theme's `--lu-` properties
([UI components](README.md#the-default-theme)), and it sets a 4px gap with `--lu-side-offset`.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class` and their state:

- the popup: `:popover-open`, `data-side` and `data-align` (where it was asked to go);
- the trigger and a submenu trigger: `[aria-expanded="true"]` while their menu is open;
- items: `[data-highlighted]` on the item that has focus (by keyboard or pointer),
  `:focus-visible`, `[aria-disabled="true"]`, and `[aria-checked="true"]` on checkbox and radio
  items;
- `[role="separator"]`, `[role="group"]` and a group label's `[role="presentation"]`.

A starting point:

```css
.menu {
  min-inline-size: 10rem;
  padding: 0.25rem;
  border: 1px solid #d4d4d8;
  border-radius: 0.5rem;
  box-shadow: 0 10px 30px -10px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35);
  --lu-side-offset: 4px;
}
.menu [role^="menuitem"] {
  padding: 0.375rem 0.5rem;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 0.25rem;
  background: none;
  font: inherit;
}
.menu [role^="menuitem"][data-highlighted] {
  background: #f4f4f5;
}
.menu [role^="menuitem"][aria-disabled="true"] {
  opacity: 0.5;
}
.menu [aria-checked="true"]::before {
  content: "✓" / "";
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/menu.css` holds what the menu needs to work, in the `lu.core` layer: `lu-menu` has
no box, and the popup and its groups lay the items out in a column (`display: grid`, items
`display: flex`). It imports the placement rules Menu shares with Popover and Tooltip: with CSS
anchor positioning, a popup sits on its `data-side` and `data-align`, keeps the gaps of
`--lu-side-offset` and `--lu-align-offset`, flips when it does not fit (a submenu tries the other
side, then the other alignment, then below and above its trigger) and hides while its trigger is
scrolled out of view. The `sideOffset` and `alignOffset` props set those two properties on the
popup.

## Keyboard and focus

The [WAI-ARIA Menu Button pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/), with
Base UI's behaviour where the pattern leaves a choice:

| Key                       | Does                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter, Space              | On the trigger: opens the menu on its first item. On an item: runs it, or checks it. On a submenu trigger: opens it. |
| Arrow Down, Arrow Up      | On the trigger: opens the menu on its first item, or on its last. In the menu: the next or previous item, looping.   |
| Home, End                 | The first or last item.                                                                                              |
| Arrow Right (Left in RTL) | On a submenu trigger: opens the submenu on its first item.                                                           |
| Arrow Left (Right in RTL) | In a submenu: closes it, back on its trigger.                                                                        |
| A character               | The next item whose text starts with it; characters typed within 750 ms add up, and Space among them is text.        |
| Escape                    | Closes one level: the submenu on top, or the menu. Focus goes back to its trigger.                                   |
| Tab, Shift+Tab            | Close the whole menu. Tab moves on from the trigger; Shift+Tab stays on it.                                          |

- **On open**, focus moves to the first item that can run (Arrow Up: the last one). Opened by a
  pointer, the popup itself takes focus and no item is highlighted until a key or the pointer
  picks one.
- **On close**, focus returns to the trigger without scrolling the page, after Escape, Tab, an
  item that ran or a click outside on nothing focusable; a click on a button or a field outside
  leaves focus there.
- **Running an item** closes the whole menu and returns focus before the item's `onClick` runs,
  so a handler that opens a dialog gets focus back on the trigger when it closes. Checkbox and
  radio items stay open.
- **Disabled items** (`aria-disabled`) stay in the arrow order and typeahead, as the pattern
  asks, but do not run.
- **The pointer** highlights the item under it, and leaving the items clears the highlight. A
  mouse press on the trigger opens the menu at once: releasing it on an item runs the item, and
  releasing it outside closes the menu. A submenu opens after the pointer rests 100 ms on its
  trigger, and stays open while the pointer heads for it across other items.
- **A click outside** closes the whole menu, submenus included, and a click in a menu closes the
  submenus open from it. A right-click, a middle click or a second finger outside leaves the menu
  open, as in Base UI.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

The trigger opens the popup with `popovertarget`, and Escape or a click outside closes it: a menu
in a server-rendered page opens before any script loads, and with none. Tab then moves through the
items in order, and links work; commands, which run JavaScript, need it anyway. `open`,
`onOpenChange` and the `bind:` props need the component to run in the browser, in an island.

The keyboard contract comes from a small script: a page that renders a `Menu` loads it once, as a
3.3 kB (brotli) module without the Lumiose runtime, and islands bundle it. It defines `lu-menu`,
which upgrades every menu on the page in place, and adds what the native popover lacks: focus on
open and its return on close, the arrows, Home, End and typeahead, Escape one level at a time, Tab,
submenus, checkbox and radio items, disabled items, `data-highlighted`, and the pointer behaviour
above. It also takes over dismissal, with the model Menu shares with [Popover](popover.md) and
[Combobox](combobox.md): the popup becomes a manual popover when the script opens it, and the
script closes it on a click outside (main button only), on Escape, on a close request such as the
Android back gesture, and when another popup opens outside it. Until it loads (or without JavaScript) the menu behaves as a
native `popover="auto"` of buttons, which any click outside closes.

The element is also an API of its own, for scripts and other frameworks:

- `open`: a property; setting it to `true` or `false` opens or closes the menu.
- `openchange`: an event (not bubbling, like `toggle`) with `detail.open`, after the menu opens or
  closes.
- `checkedchange`: a bubbling event that checkbox and radio items fire with `detail.checked` when
  a click, Enter or Space checks or unchecks them.

## Browser support

- **Popovers and `popovertarget`**: Chrome and Edge 114, Firefox 125, Safari 17.
- **CSS anchor positioning** places the popup: Chrome and Edge 125, Firefox 147, Safari 26
  (partly; 27 fully). Elsewhere the client script places the popup with the same sides,
  alignment, offsets and flips; without JavaScript it shows where the browser shows any popover,
  in the middle of the viewport, and still works.
- **`showPopover({ source })`**, which ties a popup the script opens to its trigger: Chrome 137,
  Firefox 144, Safari 26. Older browsers open it the same way.
- **`CloseWatcher`**, for the Android back gesture: Chrome 126, Firefox 149. Elsewhere Escape
  still closes the menu.
- **Exit animations** that keep the popup in the top layer while it fades (`overlay`) are
  Chromium-only.

## Related

- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling, the default theme and the other components.
- [Dialog](dialog.md): a menu item can open one; focus returns to the menu's trigger when it
  closes.
- [Islands](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/islands/): running a component in the
  browser, for `open`, `onOpenChange` and the `bind:` props.
- [JSX](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/jsx/): `bind:`, native events with `on:` and
  `ref`.

<!-- source: menubar.md -->

# Menubar

> A bar of menus, such as an app's File, Edit and View, after Base UI's Menubar and the WAI-ARIA menubar pattern: `Menu.Root`s inside `<lu-menubar role="menubar">`, whose triggers are the bar's items. Menu's popups, items, submenus and dismissal; the bar is one tab stop, the arrow keys move between its items and between open menus, and once a menu is open, hovering another item opens its menu instead. A 0.6 kB script on top of Menu's (4.0 kB together); without JavaScript each trigger opens its menu.

```ts
import { Menu, Menubar } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/menu" and "@lumiose/ui/menubar"
import "@lumiose/ui/menubar.css"; // Menu's layout, and the bar's row (or column)
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Menubar>
  <Menu.Root>
    <Menu.Trigger />
    <Menu.Popup>
      <Menu.Item />
      <Menu.SubmenuRoot>
        <Menu.SubmenuTrigger />
        <Menu.Popup>…</Menu.Popup>
      </Menu.SubmenuRoot>
    </Menu.Popup>
  </Menu.Root>
  <Menu.Root>…</Menu.Root>
</Menubar>
```

| Part                       | Renders                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Menubar`                  | `<lu-menubar role="menubar" aria-orientation="…" data-orientation="…">`: a row of the menus (a column when vertical). |
| `Menu.Root` inside it      | Menu's `<lu-menu>`, with `role="none"`.                                                                               |
| `Menu.Trigger` inside it   | Menu's `<button popovertarget="…">`, with `role="menuitem"`: an item of the bar.                                      |
| `Menu.Popup` and the items | As in [Menu](menu.md#anatomy).                                                                                        |

A menubar's items are the triggers of its menus, each inside its `<lu-menu role="none">`, as in
the APG example. Give the bar an `aria-label`.

## API

### Menubar

| Prop          | Type                         | Default        |                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Which way the items run. Vertical: Arrow Up and Down move between them, the arrow that points at a popup opens it, and popups go at the inline end. |
| `loopFocus`   | `boolean`                    | `true`         | Whether the arrows wrap from the last item to the first and back.                                                                                   |

Every other prop passes through to `<lu-menubar>`: `class`, `style`, `aria-label`, `data-*`.

### The menus

Each `Menu.Root` keeps [Menu's props](menu.md#api): `open`, `onOpenChange` and `bind:open` per
menu, and its items' `bind:checked` and `bind:value`. `disabled` on a `Menu.Trigger` takes the menu
out of the bar: no focus, no opening.

**Differences from Base UI's Menubar.** No `modal` (the page stays scrollable and usable while a
menu is open) and no `disabled` on the bar: disable each trigger instead. No `render`.

## Example

An editor's menus in a server-rendered page, with no island, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { Menu, Menubar } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function EditorMenus() {
  return (
    <Menubar aria-label="Editor" class="lu-menubar">
      <Menu.Root>
        <Menu.Trigger>File</Menu.Trigger>
        <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu">
          <Menu.Item>New file</Menu.Item>
          <Menu.Item>Open…</Menu.Item>
          <Menu.SubmenuRoot>
            <Menu.SubmenuTrigger>Share</Menu.SubmenuTrigger>
            <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu">
              <Menu.Item>Email</Menu.Item>
              <Menu.Item>Copy link</Menu.Item>
            </Menu.Popup>
          </Menu.SubmenuRoot>
        </Menu.Popup>
      </Menu.Root>
      <Menu.Root>
        <Menu.Trigger>Edit</Menu.Trigger>
        <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu">
          <Menu.Item>Undo</Menu.Item>
          <Menu.Item>Redo</Menu.Item>
        </Menu.Popup>
      </Menu.Root>
      <Menu.Root>
        <Menu.Trigger>View</Menu.Trigger>
        <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu">
          <Menu.RadioGroup defaultValue="100">
            <Menu.GroupLabel>Zoom</Menu.GroupLabel>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="75">75%</Menu.RadioItem>
            <Menu.RadioItem value="100">100%</Menu.RadioItem>
          </Menu.RadioGroup>
        </Menu.Popup>
      </Menu.Root>
    </Menubar>
  );
}
```

In an island, a checkbox item bound to a signal and an item that writes a status line:

```tsx check
import { Menu, Menubar } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function DocumentMenus() {
  const wrap = signal(false);
  const status = signal("Not saved yet");
  return (
    <>
      <Menubar aria-label="Document" class="lu-menubar">
        <Menu.Root>
          <Menu.Trigger>File</Menu.Trigger>
          <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu">
            <Menu.Item onClick={() => status.set("Saved")}>Save</Menu.Item>
          </Menu.Popup>
        </Menu.Root>
        <Menu.Root>
          <Menu.Trigger>Edit</Menu.Trigger>
          <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu">
            <Menu.CheckboxItem bind:checked={wrap}>Word wrap</Menu.CheckboxItem>
          </Menu.Popup>
        </Menu.Root>
      </Menubar>
      <p>
        {status()}; word wrap is {wrap() ? "on" : "off"}
      </p>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-menubar` on `Menubar` and `lu-menu` on each `Menu.Popup`: a
bordered bar of the triggers, the one whose menu is open filled, with a focus ring.

**With your own CSS**, style the bar through `class` and `[data-orientation]`, the items as
`lu-menubar > lu-menu > [role="menuitem"]` with `[aria-expanded="true"]` for the open one, and
`[data-has-submenu-open]` on the bar while a menu is open. The popups and items are
[Menu's](menu.md#styling).

`@lumiose/ui/menubar.css` holds Menu's rules and, in the `lu.core` layer, makes `<lu-menubar>` a
flex row (a column when vertical); each `<lu-menu>` adds no box.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key                            | Does                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab, Shift+Tab                 | Enter and leave the bar, which is one tab stop: the item focused last.                                                           |
| Arrow Right, Arrow Left        | On an item: the next or previous item (Down and Up when vertical; swapped right to left). An open menu follows to the next item. |
| Home, End                      | The first or last item.                                                                                                          |
| A letter                       | The next item whose label starts with it.                                                                                        |
| Arrow Down, Enter, Space       | Open the item's menu on its first item (Arrow Up: the last one). Vertical: the arrow that points at the popup opens it.          |
| Arrow Right, Arrow Left (menu) | On an item that opens no submenu: close the menu and open the next or previous one. Vertical: the arrow pointing back closes it. |
| Escape                         | Closes the menu (a submenu first) and returns to its item.                                                                       |

- **The pointer**: a click opens or closes a menu; once one is open, hovering another item opens
  its menu instead. Inside a menu, Menu's rules apply: hover highlights, submenus open on hover.
- **Focus** returns to the item when its menu closes, as in Menu. Disabled triggers are skipped.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

Each trigger opens its menu through `popovertarget`, and the browser light-dismisses it: without
JavaScript every trigger is a tab stop, and the menus open with Enter, Space or a click.

A page that renders a `Menubar` loads Menu's script and a 0.6 kB (brotli) one of its own, 4.0 kB
together, without the Lumiose runtime; islands bundle them. The menubar's script makes the bar one
tab stop once the page has loaded, and adds the arrow keys between items and menus and the hover
switching. Each menu stays Menu's: its keys, items, submenus and dismissal.

## Browser support

As for [Menu](menu.md#browser-support): popovers everywhere current, CSS anchor positioning in
Chrome, Edge, Firefox 147 and Safari 26 (elsewhere the script places the popups).

## Related

- [Menu](menu.md): one menu, opened by a button.
- [Navigation Menu](navigation-menu.md): site navigation with panels of links.
- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling and the other components.

<!-- source: meter.md -->

# Meter

> A measurement within a known range (storage used, a password's strength, a rating), after Base UI's Meter: a native `<meter>` (with its value, range and `aria-valuetext`), labelled, with the value as text (a percentage of the range by default, or your `Intl.NumberFormat` options). No script.

```ts
import { Meter } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/meter"
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Meter.Root value={72}>
  <Meter.Label />
  <Meter.Value />
  <Meter.Track />
</Meter.Root>
```

| Part    | Renders                                         |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`  | `<div>` with `--lu-value` (`0%` to `100%`)      |
| `Label` | `<label for>` the track                         |
| `Value` | `<span>` with the formatted value               |
| `Track` | `<meter value min max aria-valuetext>`: the bar |

## API

### Meter.Root

| Prop               | Type                                                | Default             |                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`            | `number`                                            |                     | The measurement, from `min` to `max`. Required.                                     |
| `min`              | `number`                                            | `0`                 | The bottom of the range.                                                            |
| `max`              | `number`                                            | `100`               | The top of the range.                                                               |
| `format`           | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`                          | a percentage        | How the value is written. With it, the value itself is formatted, not a percentage. |
| `locale`           | `Intl.LocalesArgument`                              | the browser's       | The locale of the formatted value (the server's in server HTML).                    |
| `getAriaValueText` | `(formattedValue: string, value: number) => string` | the formatted value | The text assistive technology reads.                                                |

Every other prop passes through to the `<div>`: `id`, `class`, `style`.

### Meter.Label, Meter.Track and Meter.Value

`Label` takes `<label>` props. `Track` takes `<meter>` props, among them the native `low`, `high`
and `optimum`, which tell browsers which band a value is in (`aria-label` when there is no
`Label`). `Value` takes `<span>` props, and its `children` may be a function
`(formattedValue, value) => JSX.Element`.

**Differences from Base UI's Meter.** The `<meter>` element is the track and the indicator: there is
no `Meter.Indicator`. Root has no `role`; the `<meter>` has it (`meter`).

## Example

```tsx check
import { Meter } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function StorageMeter() {
  return (
    <Meter.Root
      value={7.2}
      max={10}
      getAriaValueText={(_, gb) => `${gb} of 10 GB`}
      class="lu-meter"
    >
      <Meter.Label>Storage used</Meter.Label>
      <Meter.Value>{(_, gb) => `${gb} GB of 10`}</Meter.Value>
      <Meter.Track low={6} high={9} optimum={0} />
    </Meter.Root>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-meter` on `Root`: the label and the value on a row above a 10px
bar, its edge in `--lu-input` (3:1, so the whole range shows) and its value in the primary colour
(a lighter blue in dark mode), whatever band it is in.

**With your own CSS**, style the bar with `appearance: none` and its pseudo-elements:
`::-webkit-meter-bar`, `::-webkit-meter-optimum-value`, `::-webkit-meter-suboptimum-value`,
`::-webkit-meter-even-less-good-value`, `::-moz-meter-bar` (and `:-moz-meter-optimum` and the
others). Or draw your own bar from `--lu-value` on `Root`.

Meter ships no stylesheet: it needs none to work.

## Keyboard and focus

A meter is not interactive: it takes no focus and no keys.

## Without JavaScript

Fully: the server renders the `<meter>` with its value, range, label and text.

## Browser support

Native `<meter>`: every browser. Its pseudo-elements differ between engines, hence the two sets
above. `role="meter"` reaches screen readers in recent versions; older ones read a progress bar.

## Related

- [Progress](progress.md): a task's progress, which can be indeterminate.
- [Slider](slider.md): a value the user picks within a range.

<!-- source: navigation-menu.md -->

# Navigation Menu

> A site's navigation whose items open panels of links, after Base UI's NavigationMenu and the WAI-ARIA disclosure navigation pattern: a `<nav>` landmark around a list, each trigger opening its content through `popovertarget` (a native popover placed under it by CSS anchor positioning), so the links work and the panels open on a click, one at a time, in server HTML with no JavaScript. A 2.1 kB script adds hover intent, the arrow keys, closing when focus leaves and the direction a panel comes in from. `bind:value` (or `value` and `onValueChange`) keeps the open item in a signal.

```ts
import { NavigationMenu } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/navigation-menu"
import "@lumiose/ui/navigation-menu.css"; // places each content next to its trigger
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<NavigationMenu.Root>
  <NavigationMenu.List>
    <NavigationMenu.Item>
      <NavigationMenu.Trigger>
        <NavigationMenu.Icon />
      </NavigationMenu.Trigger>
      <NavigationMenu.Content>
        <NavigationMenu.Link />
      </NavigationMenu.Content>
    </NavigationMenu.Item>
    <NavigationMenu.Item>
      <NavigationMenu.Link />
    </NavigationMenu.Item>
  </NavigationMenu.List>
</NavigationMenu.Root>
```

| Part      | Renders                                                                                                        |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`    | `<nav data-orientation="…">` inside `<lu-navigation-menu>`, an element with no box; `role="none"` when nested. |
| `List`    | `<ul>` of the items.                                                                                           |
| `Item`    | `<li data-value="…">`: a trigger with its content, or a link.                                                  |
| `Trigger` | `<button type="button" popovertarget="…">`; `aria-expanded` follows its content where the script runs.         |
| `Icon`    | `<span aria-hidden="true">` inside the trigger, such as a chevron.                                             |
| `Content` | `<div popover="auto" data-side="…" data-align="…">` of links, anchored to its trigger.                         |
| `Link`    | `<a>`; `aria-current="page"` and `data-active` when `active`.                                                  |

Give `Root` an `aria-label` ("Main") when the page has more than one `<nav>`. A `Root` inside a
`Content` is a nested menu, part of its parent's landmark: its `<nav>` has `role="none"`.

## API

### NavigationMenu.Root

| Prop            | Type                              | Default        |                                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string \| null`                  |                | The `value` of the item whose content is open, or `null`; opens or closes them when it changes, in the browser.     |
| `defaultValue`  | `string \| null`                  | `null`         | The item open at first, in the browser, when `value` is left out.                                                   |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string \| null) => void` |                | Called after a content opens (its item's `value`) or the open one closes (`null`), whatever did it.                 |
| `bind:value`    | `Signal<string \| null>`          |                | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                                                          |
| `delay`         | `number`                          | `50`           | How long the pointer rests on a trigger before its content opens, in milliseconds.                                  |
| `closeDelay`    | `number`                          | `50`           | How long after the pointer leaves an item its content closes, in milliseconds (300 while it heads for the content). |
| `orientation`   | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"`      | `"horizontal"` | Which way the items run: vertical moves with Arrow Up and Down and places contents at the inline end.               |

Server HTML always starts closed: a popover only opens from its trigger or script.

### NavigationMenu.Item

| Prop    | Type     | Default        |                                         |
| ------- | -------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `value` | `string` | a generated id | The value `Root`'s `value` names it by. |

### NavigationMenu.Content

| Prop          | Type                                                                       | Default                                   |                                                 |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `side`        | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "inline-start" \| "inline-end"` | `"bottom"` (`"inline-end"` when vertical) | The trigger's side it goes on; it flips to fit. |
| `align`       | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"`                                             | `"center"` (`"start"` when vertical)      | How it aligns with the trigger along that side. |
| `sideOffset`  | `number`                                                                   |                                           | The gap to the trigger, in CSS pixels.          |
| `alignOffset` | `number`                                                                   |                                           | A shift along the side, in CSS pixels.          |

### NavigationMenu.Link

| Prop           | Type      | Default |                                                      |
| -------------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `active`       | `boolean` | `false` | The link to the current page: `aria-current="page"`. |
| `closeOnClick` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether following it closes the open content.        |

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers) and passes them through: `href` and `target` on a `Link`, `disabled` on a `Trigger`.

**Differences from Base UI's NavigationMenu.** Each `Content` is its own popover in the top layer,
anchored to its trigger: there is no shared `Viewport`, `Popup`, `Positioner`, `Portal`,
`Backdrop` or `Arrow`, and so no `--popup-width` and `--popup-height` to animate one box between
contents. `data-activation-direction` lets a content slide in from where the previous one was. No
`actionsRef`, `onOpenChangeComplete`, `keepMounted` or `render`.

## Example

A site's main navigation in a server-rendered page, with no island, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { NavigationMenu } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function MainNavigation() {
  return (
    <NavigationMenu.Root aria-label="Main" class="lu-navigation-menu">
      <NavigationMenu.List>
        <NavigationMenu.Item>
          <NavigationMenu.Trigger>
            Products <NavigationMenu.Icon>▾</NavigationMenu.Icon>
          </NavigationMenu.Trigger>
          <NavigationMenu.Content>
            <ul>
              <li>
                <NavigationMenu.Link href="#analytics">Analytics</NavigationMenu.Link>
              </li>
              <li>
                <NavigationMenu.Link href="#automation">Automation</NavigationMenu.Link>
              </li>
            </ul>
          </NavigationMenu.Content>
        </NavigationMenu.Item>
        <NavigationMenu.Item>
          <NavigationMenu.Trigger>
            Learn <NavigationMenu.Icon>▾</NavigationMenu.Icon>
          </NavigationMenu.Trigger>
          <NavigationMenu.Content>
            <ul>
              <li>
                <NavigationMenu.Link href="#guides">Guides</NavigationMenu.Link>
              </li>
              <li>
                <NavigationMenu.Link href="#blog">Blog</NavigationMenu.Link>
              </li>
            </ul>
          </NavigationMenu.Content>
        </NavigationMenu.Item>
        <NavigationMenu.Item>
          <NavigationMenu.Link href="#pricing" active>
            Pricing
          </NavigationMenu.Link>
        </NavigationMenu.Item>
      </NavigationMenu.List>
    </NavigationMenu.Root>
  );
}
```

In an island, the open item in a signal:

```tsx check
import { NavigationMenu } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function SiteNavigation() {
  const open = signal<string | null>(null);
  return (
    <>
      <NavigationMenu.Root aria-label="Site" bind:value={open} class="lu-navigation-menu">
        <NavigationMenu.List>
          <NavigationMenu.Item value="docs">
            <NavigationMenu.Trigger>Docs</NavigationMenu.Trigger>
            <NavigationMenu.Content>
              <NavigationMenu.Link href="#start">Getting started</NavigationMenu.Link>
            </NavigationMenu.Content>
          </NavigationMenu.Item>
          <NavigationMenu.Item value="community">
            <NavigationMenu.Trigger>Community</NavigationMenu.Trigger>
            <NavigationMenu.Content>
              <NavigationMenu.Link href="#forum">Forum</NavigationMenu.Link>
            </NavigationMenu.Content>
          </NavigationMenu.Item>
        </NavigationMenu.List>
      </NavigationMenu.Root>
      <p>Open: {open() ?? "none"}</p>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-navigation-menu` on `Root`: the list in a row (a column when
vertical), the triggers and links as 36px targets, the current page underlined, an open trigger
filled with its icon turned, and each content a surface of links that fades and slides in.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class`, the triggers' `[aria-expanded="true"]`,
links' `[aria-current="page"]`, and the contents' `:popover-open`, `[data-side]` and
`[data-activation-direction]` (`left`, `right`, `up` or `down`: where the content's trigger is from
the trigger of the content that was open before; absent when none was):

```css
.panel {
  transition:
    opacity 150ms,
    translate 150ms,
    overlay 150ms allow-discrete,
    display 150ms allow-discrete;
}
.panel:not(:popover-open) {
  opacity: 0;
}
@starting-style {
  .panel[data-activation-direction="right"]:popover-open {
    translate: 1rem 0;
  }
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/navigation-menu.css`, in the `lu.core` layer, holds the shared placement rules that put
each content next to its trigger, with the same flips as Popover and Menu, and gives
`<lu-navigation-menu>` no box.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key                     | Does                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab, Shift+Tab          | Every trigger and link is a tab stop; from an open trigger, Tab goes into its content.                      |
| Enter, Space            | On a trigger: opens or closes its content.                                                                  |
| Arrow Right, Arrow Left | Between the top-level triggers and links (Down and Up when vertical; swapped right to left).                |
| Home, End               | The first or last top-level trigger or link.                                                                |
| Arrow Down              | On a trigger: opens its content on its first link (Arrow Right when vertical). In a content: the next link. |
| Arrow Up                | In a content: the previous link.                                                                            |
| Escape                  | Closes the open content and returns to its trigger.                                                         |

- **The pointer**: resting on a trigger opens its content after `delay`, at once while another one
  is open; leaving the item closes it after `closeDelay`, unless a click kept it open. A click
  toggles a content; a click outside closes it.
- **Focus** leaving an open item for elsewhere on the page closes its content. It is a navigation
  landmark, not a menu: links keep their roles and the browser's link behaviour.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

The `<nav>`, its links and the triggers are HTML: each trigger opens its content with
`popovertarget`, one at a time (an auto popover closes the others), and Escape or a click outside
closes it. `value`, `onValueChange` and `bind:value` need the component to run in an island.

A page that renders a `NavigationMenu` loads a 2.1 kB (brotli) script, without the Lumiose runtime;
islands bundle it. `<lu-navigation-menu>` takes over the trigger's click (so a click keeps a content
opened by hover open), opens contents on hover, adds the arrow keys, closes a content when focus
leaves its item, keeps `aria-expanded` and `data-activation-direction` current, and places the
contents where CSS anchor positioning is missing.

## Browser support

- **Popovers and `popovertarget`**: every current browser.
- **CSS anchor positioning**: Chrome and Edge 125, Firefox 147, Safari 26. Elsewhere the script
  places the contents next to their triggers.
- **Exit animations** that keep a content in the top layer (`overlay`) are Chromium-only.

## Related

- [Menubar](menubar.md): a bar of application menus, with the menu roles.
- [Popover](popover.md): one popup anchored to its trigger.
- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling and the other components.

<!-- source: number-field.md -->

# Number Field

> A number input with buttons to step it, after Base UI's NumberField and the APG spinbutton. Without `format` it is a native `<input type="number">`, which steps, validates and submits without JavaScript; with `format` (`Intl.NumberFormat` options: a currency, a percentage, grouping) it shows the formatted number, reads what is typed back in the same locale, and a hidden input submits the number. `<lu-number-field>`'s 2.2 kB script adds Page Up and Page Down, Home and End, press-and-hold buttons, a scrub area, the wheel when asked, and commit-time clamping. `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync.

```ts
import { NumberField } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/number-field"
import "@lumiose/ui/number-field.css"; // or "@lumiose/ui/styles.css" for every component
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<NumberField.Root>
  <NumberField.ScrubArea />
  <NumberField.Group>
    <NumberField.Decrement />
    <NumberField.Input />
    <NumberField.Increment />
  </NumberField.Group>
</NumberField.Root>
```

| Part        | Renders                                                                                                                           |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`      | `<lu-number-field>` with the range and format as attributes, and an `<input type="hidden">` that submits the number with `format` |
| `ScrubArea` | `<span data-scrub>`: dragging across it steps the number (usually around the label)                                               |
| `Group`     | `<div>` around the input and the buttons                                                                                          |
| `Input`     | `<input type="number" inputmode="decimal" min max step>`, or with `format` `<input type="text" role="spinbutton" aria-value…>`    |
| `Increment` | `<button type="button" tabindex="-1" aria-label="Increase" aria-controls="…">`, disabled at `max`                                 |
| `Decrement` | `<button type="button" tabindex="-1" aria-label="Decrease" aria-controls="…">`, disabled at `min`                                 |

Name the field with a [Field](field.md) (`Field.Label`), a `<label for>` the Root's `id`, or an
`aria-label` on the `Input`.

## API

### NumberField.Root

| Prop                               | Type                              | Default       |                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`                            | `number \| null`                  |               | Shows this number (`null`: empty) when it changes. Pair it with `onValueChange`.                   |
| `defaultValue`                     | `number \| null`                  | `null`        | The number at first; a form reset goes back to it.                                                 |
| `onValueChange`                    | `(value: number \| null) => void` |               | Called as the number changes: typing, a key, a button, the wheel, a drag.                          |
| `onValueCommitted`                 | `(value: number \| null) => void` |               | Called when a change is done: the input left, a key pressed, a button or a drag released.          |
| `bind:value`                       | `Signal<number \| null>`          |               | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                                         |
| `min`, `max`                       | `number`                          |               | The range. A typed number outside it becomes its end when committed.                               |
| `step`                             | `number`                          | `1`           | The step of the arrow keys, the buttons, the wheel and a drag.                                     |
| `largeStep`                        | `number`                          | `10`          | The step of Page Up, Page Down and Shift with an arrow key.                                        |
| `format`                           | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`        |               | How the number is shown; with it, the input is a text field and a hidden input submits the number. |
| `locale`                           | `string`                          | the browser's | The locale of the formatted number (the server's in server HTML).                                  |
| `allowWheelScrub`                  | `boolean`                         | `false`       | The wheel steps the number while the input has focus and the pointer is over it.                   |
| `allowOutOfRange`                  | `boolean`                         | `false`       | Typed numbers outside the range stay as typed, for the browser's validation to report.             |
| `name`, `form`                     | `string`                          |               | The name the number is submitted under, and the id of its form when it is outside it.              |
| `id`                               | `string`                          | generated     | The input's id, for a `<label for>`.                                                               |
| `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly` | `boolean`                         | `false`       | As on a native input; read-only and disabled fields' buttons are disabled.                         |

### NumberField.ScrubArea

| Prop               | Type                         | Default        |                                                              |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `direction`        | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | The drag that changes the number: right goes up, or up does. |
| `pixelSensitivity` | `number`                     | `2`            | How many pixels of drag make one step.                       |

### The other parts

`Group` takes `<div>` props. `Input` takes `<input>` props except the range's own (`type`, `value`,
`min`, `max`, `step`, `name`, `required`, `readonly`, `id`: the Root's). `Increment` and
`Decrement` take `<button>` props; give them an `aria-label` in the page's language. Inside a
[Field](field.md), the input takes the field's id, name, description and error.

**Native or formatted.** A native number input cannot show grouping, a currency or a percentage,
and reads a typed number in the browser's own way, so a formatted field is a text field with the
spinbutton role, and the number it submits sits in a hidden input. The native input is the default
because it needs no JavaScript: typing, the arrow keys, `min`, `max` and `step` validation and the
form value are the browser's.

**Differences from Base UI's NumberField.** No `smallStep` (Alt with an arrow key) or
`snapOnStep`: a native field validates its value against `step` itself. No `ScrubAreaCursor`
(Base UI's pointer-locked cursor), no `inputRef`, no `render`. `locale` is a string, written to the
element for its script.

## Example

```tsx check
import { NumberField } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function PriceField() {
  const price = signal<number | null>(19.9);
  return (
    <NumberField.Root
      id="price"
      name="price"
      bind:value={price}
      min={0}
      step={0.5}
      format={{ style: "currency", currency: "EUR" }}
      class="lu-number-field"
    >
      <NumberField.ScrubArea>
        <label for="price">Price</label>
      </NumberField.ScrubArea>
      <NumberField.Group>
        <NumberField.Decrement aria-label="Lower the price">−</NumberField.Decrement>
        <NumberField.Input />
        <NumberField.Increment aria-label="Raise the price">+</NumberField.Increment>
      </NumberField.Group>
    </NumberField.Root>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-number-field` on `Root`: the label above one bordered group,
the input centred between two 36px buttons that dim at the ends of the range, and a focus ring
around the whole group.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class`, the input's `:focus-visible`, the buttons'
`:disabled` and `[data-action="increment"]` / `[data-action="decrement"]`, the scrub area's
`[data-scrub]`, and `lu-number-field[data-scrubbing]` while a drag is on.

`@lumiose/ui/number-field.css` (0.2 kB brotli) hides the native spinners once the script runs
(`:defined`) and hides the buttons until then, keeps held buttons from selecting text, and gives a
scrub area its resize cursor and `touch-action: none`.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key                     | Does                                                                      |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Arrow Up / Arrow Down   | One step up or down.                                                      |
| Shift + Arrow Up / Down | `largeStep` up or down.                                                   |
| Page Up / Page Down     | `largeStep` up or down.                                                   |
| Home / End              | `min` or `max`, when set.                                                 |
| Enter                   | Commits the typed number (clamped, formatted); a form submits.            |
| Tab                     | Moves on: one tab stop, the input (the buttons are not in the tab order). |

Right to left, dragging the scrub area toward the left steps up, as a slider runs. A press on a
button steps once and keeps focus where it is; holding it steps again every 60 ms
after 400 ms. A click from a keyboard or a screen reader on a button steps once. Every drag (the
scrub area) has the arrow keys as its alternative (WCAG 2.5.7). The wheel steps the number only
with `allowWheelScrub`, while the input has focus and the pointer is over it (Chromium's own
stepping of a focused number input is turned off otherwise).

## Without JavaScript, and the element's script

Without `format`, the native number input works and submits with no script; the buttons, which
need it, stay hidden and the native spinners show. With `format`, the text input submits its text
as typed until the script moves the name to the hidden input, so a form that must work without
JavaScript should leave `format` out.

`<lu-number-field>`'s script (2.2 kB brotli) adds the large step, Home and End, the buttons, the
scrub area and the wheel, clamps and formats on commit, keeps the hidden input, `aria-valuenow`
and `aria-valuetext` current, and follows a form reset.

## Browser support

Native number inputs and `Intl.NumberFormat` (with `formatToParts`): every supported browser.
Scrubbing uses pointer capture, without pointer lock.

## Related

- [Field](field.md): a label, a description and errors for a number field.
- [Slider](slider.md): a number picked by dragging along a range.
- [Input](input.md): any other text.

<!-- source: otp-field.md -->

# OTP Field

> A one-time code input, after Base UI's OTPField: one native `<input>` shown as one slot per character. SMS autofill (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`), paste, Backspace, the arrow keys, `maxlength`, `pattern`, `required` and the form's value are the platform's, without JavaScript too, and assistive technology meets one labelled text field. `<lu-otp-field>`'s 1.2 kB script lays the input over the slots, keeps the code to the allowed characters, and reports completion. `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync.

```ts
import { OTPField } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/otp-field"
import "@lumiose/ui/otp-field.css"; // or "@lumiose/ui/styles.css" for every component
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<OTPField.Root length={6}>
  <OTPField.Input />
  <OTPField.Slot />
  <OTPField.Slot />
  <OTPField.Separator />
  <OTPField.Slot />
</OTPField.Root>
```

| Part        | Renders                                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`      | `<lu-otp-field length validation-type>`, with `data-complete`, `data-filled` and `data-focused` from its script         |
| `Input`     | `<input type="text" autocomplete="one-time-code" inputmode maxlength minlength pattern name>`: the field and its value  |
| `Slot`      | `<div aria-hidden="true" data-slot>`: the next character (a dot with `mask`), `data-filled`, `data-active` at the caret |
| `Separator` | `<div aria-hidden="true" data-orientation>`: a dash or a gap between slots                                              |

Name the field with a [Field](field.md) (`Field.Label`), a `<label for>` the Root's `id`, or an
`aria-label` on the `Input`.

## API

### OTPField.Root

| Prop                               | Type                                               | Default           |                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `length`                           | `number`                                           |                   | How many characters the code has. Required.                                         |
| `value`                            | `string`                                           |                   | Shows this code when it changes. Pair it with `onValueChange`.                      |
| `defaultValue`                     | `string`                                           | `""`              | The code at first; a form reset goes back to it.                                    |
| `onValueChange`                    | `(value: string) => void`                          |                   | Called as the code changes: typing, a paste, autofill, Backspace.                   |
| `bind:value`                       | `Signal<string>`                                   |                   | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                          |
| `onValueComplete`                  | `(value: string) => void`                          |                   | Called when the last character is entered.                                          |
| `onValueInvalid`                   | `(value: string) => void`                          |                   | Called with what was entered when it held characters the field does not allow.      |
| `validationType`                   | `"numeric" \| "alpha" \| "alphanumeric" \| "none"` | `"numeric"`       | The characters the code may hold; spaces are always dropped.                        |
| `inputMode`                        | `"numeric" \| "text" \| "tel" \| "none"`           | from the type     | The virtual keyboard: numeric for digits, text otherwise.                           |
| `mask`                             | `boolean`                                          | `false`           | The slots show dots.                                                                |
| `autoComplete`                     | `string`                                           | `"one-time-code"` | The input's `autocomplete`.                                                         |
| `autoSubmit`                       | `boolean`                                          | `false`           | Submits the form when the last character is entered.                                |
| `name`, `form`                     | `string`                                           |                   | The name the code is submitted under, and the id of its form when it is outside it. |
| `id`                               | `string`                                           | generated         | The input's id, for a `<label for>`.                                                |
| `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly` | `boolean`                                          | `false`           | As on a native input.                                                               |

### The other parts

`Input` takes `<input>` props except the code's own (`type`, `value`, `name`, `maxlength`,
`pattern`, `inputmode`, `autocomplete`, …: the Root's); `placeholder` and `aria-label` pass
through. `Slot` and `Separator` take `<div>` props. Inside a [Field](field.md), the input takes the
field's id, name, description and error.

**One input, not one per character.** Base UI renders an input per slot. Here one input holds the
code: autofill of an SMS code works natively (it fills one field), a paste or Backspace needs no
script, the browser validates the whole code (`pattern`, `minlength`) and submits it, and a screen
reader meets one field named once instead of six. The slots are a picture of that input, drawn by
the script; the input lies over them, transparent, so a press on a slot moves the caret there.

**Differences from Base UI's OTPField.** `Slot` replaces the per-character `Input`s; the
`Separator` is visual (`aria-hidden`). No `normalizeValue` (a function cannot reach a server
page's script), no `inputRef`, no `render`.

## Example

```tsx check
import { OTPField } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function VerifyCode() {
  const code = signal("");
  return (
    <form method="post">
      <label for="code">Verification code</label>
      <OTPField.Root
        id="code"
        name="code"
        length={6}
        required
        bind:value={code}
        class="lu-otp-field"
      >
        <OTPField.Input />
        <OTPField.Slot />
        <OTPField.Slot />
        <OTPField.Slot />
        <OTPField.Separator />
        <OTPField.Slot />
        <OTPField.Slot />
        <OTPField.Slot />
      </OTPField.Root>
      <button type="submit" class="lu-button" disabled={code().length < 6}>
        Verify
      </button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-otp-field` on `Root`: a 2.5rem box per character (they shrink
on narrow screens), the caret's box ringed while the field has focus with a blinking caret in it
(still where motion is reduced), and a short dash for a separator.

**With your own CSS**, style the slots through `[data-slot]`, `[data-filled]` and `[data-active]`,
the separator through `[data-orientation]`, and the root through `[data-complete]`,
`[data-focused]` and `:has(input:disabled)`.

`@lumiose/ui/otp-field.css` (0.2 kB brotli) lays the input over the slots once the script runs
(`:defined`), its text, caret and selection transparent, and until then shows the input as a plain
field and hides the slots.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key                | Does                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A character        | Fills the caret's slot; in a full field, types over it. Refused characters do nothing. |
| Backspace / Delete | Deletes the character before or after the caret, as in any text field.                 |
| Arrow Left / Right | Moves the caret, and the ringed slot, one slot.                                        |
| Home / End         | The first slot, or after the last character.                                           |
| Tab                | Moves on: one tab stop.                                                                |

A paste fills every slot from the caret, its spaces and dashes dropped, even past what
`maxlength` would cut.

## Without JavaScript, and the element's script

The input is a native text field: autofill, typing, paste, `pattern` and `required` validation and
submission work with no script, and the slots stay hidden. `<lu-otp-field>`'s script (1.2 kB
brotli) shows the slots, cleans the value as it changes (firing `valueinvalid` for refused input),
fires `valuecomplete`, auto-submits, and follows a form reset.

A numeric code (`validationType="numeric"`, the default) renders `dir="ltr"` on the Root: its
slots run left to right in a right-to-left page too, as digits read there. Other codes follow the
page; pass `dir` to choose.

## Browser support

`autocomplete="one-time-code"`: Safari (iOS, macOS) and Chrome on Android offer received codes;
elsewhere the field is a plain one. `pattern` with `\p{…}` classes needs the `v` flag that every
current browser uses for `pattern`.

## Related

- [Field](field.md): a label, a description and errors for the code.
- [Input](input.md): a text field without slots.
- [Form](form.md): submitting the code to a form action.

<!-- source: popover.md -->

# Popover

> A popup anchored to its trigger: a native `popover` opened and closed by the trigger's `popovertarget`, placed with CSS anchor positioning, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript. A 2.3 kB script moves focus into it and back, dismisses it as Base UI does (not on a right-click), keeps `aria-expanded` current and places it in browsers without anchor positioning. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands. A trigger can open it on hover (`openOnHover`), and a `modal` popover is a modal `<dialog>` that makes the page behind it inert.

```ts
import { Popover } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/popover"
import "@lumiose/ui/popover.css"; // places the popup next to its trigger
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Popover.Root>
  <Popover.Trigger />
  <Popover.Popup>
    <Popover.Title />
    <Popover.Description />
    <Popover.Close />
  </Popover.Popup>
</Popover.Root>
```

| Part          | Renders                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`        | No element. Holds the state and the ids the other parts share.                                                                                                              |
| `Trigger`     | `<button type="button" popovertarget="…" aria-haspopup="dialog">`, with an `anchor-name` in its `style`.                                                                    |
| `Popup`       | `<div popover="auto" role="dialog" data-side="…" data-align="…">`, labelled by its `Title` and described by its `Description`; `popover="manual"` once the script opens it. |
| `Title`       | `<h2>`, which names the popup.                                                                                                                                              |
| `Description` | `<p>`, which describes it.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Close`       | `<button type="button" popovertarget="…" popovertargetaction="hide">`.                                                                                                      |

With `modal`, the `Trigger` is a `<button command="show-modal" commandfor="…">`, the `Popup` a
`<dialog closedby="any" data-side="…" data-align="…">` and the `Close` a
`<button command="close" commandfor="…">`.

The popup is a non-modal dialog, as in Base UI: the page around it stays usable (unless `modal`). A popover may
contain another `Popover.Root`: the inner popup opens on top, and closing the outer one closes
both.

## API

### Popover.Root

| Prop           | Type                      | Default |                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                 |         | Opens or closes the popover when it changes, in the browser. Server HTML always starts closed: a popover opens only from its trigger or script. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |         | Called after the popover opens or closes, whatever did it: the trigger, a close button, Escape, a click outside, another popover or `open`.     |
| `bind:open`    | `Signal<boolean>`         |         | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`.                                                                                                        |
| `modal`        | `boolean`                 | `false` | A modal popover: the page behind it is inert and does not scroll, focus stays inside, and a press outside or Escape closes it.                  |

### Popover.Trigger

| Prop          | Type      | Default |                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------- | --------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `openOnHover` | `boolean` | `false` | A mouse or pen resting on the trigger opens the popover too, and it closes once the pointer has left the trigger and the popup. Not for a modal popover. |
| `delay`       | `number`  | `300`   | With `openOnHover`: how long the pointer rests on the trigger before the popover opens, in ms.                                                           |
| `closeDelay`  | `number`  | `0`     | With `openOnHover`: how long the popover stays open after the pointer leaves, in ms (at least 100 ms to cross the gap to the popup).                     |

A hover opens the popover without moving focus, and a click on the trigger then keeps it open
until it is dismissed. Touch and the keyboard open it with a click (a tap, Enter or Space), as
without `openOnHover`.

### Popover.Popup

| Prop          | Type                                                                       | Default    |                                                                                                |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `side`        | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "inline-start" \| "inline-end"` | `"bottom"` | The trigger's side the popup goes on. `inline-start` and `inline-end` follow `dir`.            |
| `align`       | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"`                                             | `"center"` | How the popup lines up with the trigger along that side.                                       |
| `sideOffset`  | `number`                                                                   | `0`        | The gap between the trigger and the popup, in CSS pixels.                                      |
| `alignOffset` | `number`                                                                   | `0`        | A shift along the side, in CSS pixels: away from the aligned edge, or right/down when centred. |

The popup flips to the opposite side when it does not fit, and goes below (or above) the trigger
when a `left` or `right` popup fits on neither side. It hides while its trigger is scrolled out
of view.

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through. Your props override the defaults (`type`,
`aria-haspopup`, `role`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`); `id`, `popover` and
`popovertarget` stay the parts' own. A `style` you pass keeps the anchor name.

- **`Trigger`**: `aria-expanded` comes from the browser for `popovertarget`, and from the client
  script once it runs.
- **`Popup`**: native events work as on any popover: `on:toggle` and `on:beforetoggle`. A popup
  without a `Title` needs an `aria-label`.

## Example

```tsx check
import { Popover } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function Notifications() {
  return (
    <Popover.Root>
      <Popover.Trigger class="lu-button">Notifications</Popover.Trigger>
      <Popover.Popup class="lu-popover" align="start">
        <Popover.Title>Notifications</Popover.Title>
        <Popover.Description>You are all caught up.</Popover.Description>
        <footer>
          <Popover.Close class="lu-button">Close</Popover.Close>
        </footer>
      </Popover.Popup>
    </Popover.Root>
  );
}
```

In an island, bound to a signal: `bind:open={open}` is short for `open={open()}` plus
`onOpenChange={(next) => open.set(next)}`. A popover opened by the signal still anchors to its
trigger and treats it as its invoker.

```tsx check
import { Popover } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function Filters() {
  const open = signal(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Popover.Root bind:open={open}>
        <Popover.Trigger class="lu-button">Filters</Popover.Trigger>
        <Popover.Popup class="lu-popover" side="right" sideOffset={8}>
          <Popover.Title>Filters</Popover.Title>
        </Popover.Popup>
      </Popover.Root>
      <p>{open() ? "Choosing filters…" : "All items"}</p>
    </>
  );
}
```

A profile card that opens on hover, and a modal popover with a form:

```tsx check
import { Popover } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function HoverAndModal() {
  return (
    <>
      <Popover.Root>
        <Popover.Trigger class="lu-button" openOnHover delay={200}>
          Ada Lovelace
        </Popover.Trigger>
        <Popover.Popup class="lu-popover" sideOffset={8}>
          <Popover.Title>Ada Lovelace</Popover.Title>
          <Popover.Description>Wrote the first published program.</Popover.Description>
        </Popover.Popup>
      </Popover.Root>
      <Popover.Root modal>
        <Popover.Trigger class="lu-button">Rename</Popover.Trigger>
        <Popover.Popup class="lu-popover" align="start" sideOffset={8}>
          <Popover.Title>Rename the file</Popover.Title>
          <label>
            Name <input class="lu-input" value="report.pdf" />
          </label>
          <footer>
            <Popover.Close class="lu-button">Done</Popover.Close>
          </footer>
        </Popover.Popup>
      </Popover.Root>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-popover` on `Popup`: a surface with the title, the
description and a `<footer>` styled, a 4px gap to the trigger, and a fade. Its colours come from the
theme's `--lu-` properties ([UI components](README.md#the-default-theme)).

**With your own CSS**, style the popup through `class` and its state: `:popover-open` (`[open]`
for a modal popover, whose `::backdrop` is transparent until you style it),
`[data-side]` and `[data-align]` (the requested placement; a flip does not change them), and the
trigger through `[aria-expanded]`. Two custom properties set the offsets, and the props override
them: `--lu-side-offset` and `--lu-align-offset`.

```css
.popover {
  --lu-side-offset: 6px;
  padding: 0.75rem;
  border: 1px solid #d4d4d8;
  border-radius: 0.5rem;
  box-shadow: 0 10px 30px -10px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35);
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/popover.css` holds the placement, in the `lu.core` layer: for each `data-side` and
`data-align`, the CSS anchor positioning that puts the popup next to its trigger, with flips and
`position-visibility: anchors-visible`. Tooltip shares it.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key          | Does                                                                                                                             |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter, Space | On the trigger: opens or closes the popover.                                                                                     |
| Tab          | Moves through the popup, then on to the element after the trigger. When the trigger is the last element, focus leaves the popup. |
| Shift+Tab    | From the start of the popup, back to the trigger. The popover stays open.                                                        |
| Escape       | Closes the popover on top. With nested popovers, or a popover in a dialog, one Escape closes one layer.                          |

- **On open**, focus moves to the first focusable element in the popup, or to the popup itself
  when it has none. Opened by touch, the popup focuses itself, so no virtual keyboard opens.
- **On close**, focus returns to the trigger without scrolling, unless a click outside landed on
  another control, which keeps it. Escape and the close buttons return it too.
- **A click outside** closes the popover; a right-click or a second finger does not. A press inside a nested popover does not close its
  parent, and opening another popover closes the first.
- Popovers opened from a dialog belong inside its `Popup`: everything outside a modal dialog is
  inert.
- **Opened on hover**, the popover leaves focus where it is; it stays open while the pointer is on
  the trigger or the popup, and Escape closes it without moving the pointer (WCAG 1.4.13).
- **A modal popover** keeps Tab inside it (the page behind it is inert), and Escape, a press
  outside or a close button closes it; focus returns to the trigger.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

The trigger, the close buttons, Escape, the click outside and the placement are HTML and CSS
features: a popover in a server-rendered page works before any script loads, and with none. So
does a modal popover, through invoker commands and `closedby` (where a browser lacks them,
[Dialog](dialog.md)'s script, which a modal popover loads, stands in). Opening on hover needs the
script.
`open`, `onOpenChange` and `bind:open` need the component to run in an island.

A page that renders a `Popover` loads a 2.3 kB (brotli) module once, without the Lumiose runtime;
islands bundle it. It covers every Popover on the page:

- focus on open (the first focusable element, or the popup) and its return on close;
