- dismissal, shared with [Menu](menu.md) and [Combobox](combobox.md): a trigger's click makes the
  popup a manual popover, which the script closes on a click outside (main button only, so a
  right-click or a second finger does not close it, as in Base UI), on Escape and other close
  requests (the Android back gesture), and when another popover opens outside it. Until the
  script loads, the browser's light dismiss closes it on any press outside;
- `aria-expanded` on the triggers;
- the placement in browsers without CSS anchor positioning, which it keeps current on scroll and
  resize;
- opening on hover: the delays, the grace to cross the gap to the popup, and keeping it open after
  a click on the trigger.

## Browser support

- **Popover and `popovertarget`**: every current browser (Baseline 2024).
- **Invoker commands and `closedby`** (a modal popover): Chrome 135, Firefox 144, Safari 26.2 for
  commands; Chrome 134 and Firefox 141 for `closedby`. Elsewhere Dialog's script stands in.
- **CSS anchor positioning**: Chrome and Edge 125, Firefox 147, Safari 26. Elsewhere the client
  script places the popup; without JavaScript there it opens in the middle of the viewport.
- Safari and Firefox do not follow a trigger moved by a CSS `transform`.

## Related

- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling, the default theme and the other components.
- [Tooltip](tooltip.md): a short tip on hover or focus, with the same placement props.
- [Dialog](dialog.md): a modal popup.

<!-- source: preview-card.md -->

# Preview Card

> A card that previews a link's destination while the pointer or keyboard focus rests on the link, after Base UI's PreviewCard. The trigger is the link itself, which works as a link without JavaScript; the card is a manual popover placed with [Popover](popover.md)'s placement and opened with its hover timing by a 2.0 kB script. It is hoverable, persistent and dismissible (WCAG 1.4.13). `bind:open` keeps a signal in sync.

```ts
import { PreviewCard } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/preview-card"
import "@lumiose/ui/preview-card.css"; // places the card next to its link
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<PreviewCard.Root>
  <p>
    … <PreviewCard.Trigger href="…" /> …
  </p>
  <PreviewCard.Popup />
</PreviewCard.Root>
```

| Part      | Renders                                                                                                    |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`    | No element. Holds the ids the other parts share.                                                           |
| `Trigger` | `<a href data-preview-card="…">`, with an `anchor-name` in its `style`; `data-popup-open` while it is open |
| `Popup`   | `<div popover="manual" data-side data-align>`, placed next to the link                                     |

The card is a `<div>`: put it after the paragraph that holds the link, not inside it (a `<p>`
cannot hold a `<div>`), with the Root around both.

## API

### PreviewCard.Root

| Prop           | Type                      | Default |                                                           |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                 |         | Opens or closes the card when it changes, in the browser. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |         | Called after the card opens or closes, whatever did it.   |
| `bind:open`    | `Signal<boolean>`         |         | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`.                  |

### PreviewCard.Trigger

| Prop         | Type     | Default |                                                                                |
| ------------ | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `delay`      | `number` | `600`   | How long the pointer or focus rests on the link before the card opens, in ms.  |
| `closeDelay` | `number` | `300`   | How long the card stays after the pointer leaves the link and the card, in ms. |

Every other `<a>` prop passes through: `href`, `target`, `class`, `aria-*`.

### PreviewCard.Popup

`side`, `align`, `sideOffset` and `alignOffset`, as on [Popover.Popup](popover.md#popoverpopup);
every other `<div>` prop passes through.

**Differences from Base UI's PreviewCard.** No `Portal`, `Positioner`, `Backdrop`, `Arrow` or
`Viewport`: the top layer and CSS anchor positioning replace them, and the placement props are on
`Popup`. No detached triggers (`handle`, `payload`) or `actionsRef`.

## Example

```tsx check
import { PreviewCard } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function SignalsLink() {
  return (
    <PreviewCard.Root>
      <p>
        Lumiose components update through{" "}
        <PreviewCard.Trigger href="/docs/concepts/signals">signals</PreviewCard.Trigger>.
      </p>
      <PreviewCard.Popup class="lu-preview-card">
        <strong>Signals</strong>
        <p>Values that update whatever reads them.</p>
      </PreviewCard.Popup>
    </PreviewCard.Root>
  );
}
```

A card is a visual enhancement, as Base UI says: what it shows should also be on the linked page.

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-preview-card` on `Popup`: a surface like a popover's, 8px from
the link, with a fade (none where motion is reduced).

**With your own CSS**, style the card through `class`, `:popover-open`, `[data-side]` and
`[data-align]`, and the link through `[data-popup-open]`. `--lu-side-offset` and
`--lu-align-offset` set the offsets.

`@lumiose/ui/preview-card.css` is the placement Popover and Tooltip share (placement.css).

## Keyboard and focus

| Key    | Does                                                                                                        |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab    | Onto the link: the card opens after the delay, focus stays on the link. Again: into the open card, then on. |
| Escape | Closes the card, without moving focus or the pointer.                                                       |
| Enter  | Follows the link.                                                                                           |

- **Hover** opens the card after the delay; it stays while the pointer is on the link or the card
  (it may cross the gap between them) and closes after the close delay once it left both.
- **Focus** opens it too; it closes when focus leaves the link and the card. The open card follows
  its link in the focus order (the link is its invoker).
- **Touch** follows the link: no card opens on a tap.
- **A press outside** closes it, as Escape does (the dismissal model of Popover and Menu).

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

The link is a plain link and the card never opens. A page that renders a `PreviewCard` loads a
2.0 kB (brotli) module once (with the hover timing it shares with Popover): hover and focus with
their delays, dismissal, `data-popup-open`, and the placement in browsers without CSS anchor
positioning.

## Browser support

Popover and CSS anchor positioning as in [Popover](popover.md#browser-support): the script places
the card where anchor positioning is missing.

## Related

- [Popover](popover.md): a popup a click opens, or a hover with `openOnHover`.
- [Tooltip](tooltip.md): a short text tip on hover or focus.

<!-- source: progress.md -->

# Progress

> A task's progress, after Base UI's Progress: a native `<progress>` (the progress bar for assistive technology, with its value and `aria-valuetext`), labelled, with the value as text (a percentage by default, or your `Intl.NumberFormat` options). With no value it is indeterminate. No script.

```ts
import { Progress } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/progress"
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Progress.Root value={30}>
  <Progress.Label />
  <Progress.Value />
  <Progress.Track />
</Progress.Root>
```

| Part    | Renders                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Root`  | `<div>` with `--lu-value` (`0%` to `100%`; unset while indeterminate)          |
| `Label` | `<label for>` the track                                                        |
| `Value` | `<span>` with the formatted value (empty while indeterminate)                  |
| `Track` | `<progress value max aria-valuetext>`: the bar; no `value` while indeterminate |

## API

### Progress.Root

| Prop               | Type                                                | Default             |                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`            | `number \| null`                                    |                     | The progress, from `min` to `max`; `null` while unknown (indeterminate). Required.  |
| `min`              | `number`                                            | `0`                 | The start.                                                                          |
| `max`              | `number`                                            | `100`               | The end: done.                                                                      |
| `format`           | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`                          | a percentage        | How the value is written. With it, the value itself is formatted, not a percentage. |
| `locale`           | `Intl.LocalesArgument`                              | the browser's       | The locale of the formatted value (the server's in server HTML).                    |
| `getAriaValueText` | `(formattedValue: string, value: number) => string` | the formatted value | The text assistive technology reads.                                                |

Every other prop passes through to the `<div>`: `id`, `class`, `style`.

### Progress.Label, Progress.Track and Progress.Value

`Label` takes `<label>` props. `Track` takes `<progress>` props (`aria-label` when there is no
`Label`). `Value` takes `<span>` props, and its `children` may be a function
`(formattedValue, value) => JSX.Element` that writes the value your way.

**Differences from Base UI's Progress.** The `<progress>` element is the track and the indicator:
there is no `Progress.Indicator` (style the element's value pseudo-elements, or use `--lu-value`).
Root has no `role`; the `<progress>` has it.

## Example

An upload, in an island:

```tsx check
import { Progress } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function UploadProgress() {
  const done = signal<number | null>(null);
  return (
    <p>
      <button
        type="button"
        class="lu-button"
        onClick={() => done.set(Math.min(100, (done() ?? 0) + 20))}
      >
        Upload a part
      </button>
      <Progress.Root value={done()} class="lu-progress">
        <Progress.Label>Uploading</Progress.Label>
        <Progress.Value />
        <Progress.Track />
      </Progress.Root>
    </p>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-progress` on `Root`: the label and the value on a row above a
10px bar, its edge in `--lu-input` (3:1 against the page, so the whole range shows) and its value in
the primary colour (a lighter blue in dark mode). Indeterminate, a segment slides along it; it
stands still where motion is reduced.

**With your own CSS**, style the bar with `appearance: none` and its pseudo-elements:
`::-webkit-progress-bar`, `::-webkit-progress-value`, `::-moz-progress-bar`, and
`progress:indeterminate`. Or draw your own bar from `--lu-value` on `Root`.

Progress ships no stylesheet: it needs none to work.

## Keyboard and focus

A progress bar is not interactive: it takes no focus and no keys.

## Without JavaScript

Fully: the server renders the `<progress>` with its value, the label and the text. It changes when
the component renders again (in an island, from a signal).

Right to left, the native bar fills from the right, and the default theme's indeterminate
segment slides leftward.

## Browser support

Native `<progress>`: every browser. Its pseudo-elements differ between engines, hence the two sets
above.

## Related

- [Meter](meter.md): a measurement within a range, not a task's progress.
- [Toast](toast.md): tell the user when the task is done.

<!-- source: radio-group.md -->

# Radio

> A group of radios with one value, after Base UI's RadioGroup and Radio: native radios in a `<fieldset role="radiogroup">`. The browser gives the group one tab stop, arrow keys that move and select (skipping disabled radios), `required`, submission and reset, in server HTML and without JavaScript; a legend names the group. `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync.

```ts
import { Radio, RadioGroup, Fieldset } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/radio-group"
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<RadioGroup>
  <Fieldset.Legend />
  <Radio.Root />
</RadioGroup>
```

| Part         | Renders                                                                                  |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RadioGroup` | `<fieldset role="radiogroup">`; a `Fieldset.Legend` first inside names it.               |
| `Radio.Root` | `<input type="radio">` with the group's `name`, checked when its `value` is the group's. |

Put each radio in a `<label>` (or name it with `aria-label`).

## API

### RadioGroup

| Prop            | Type                      | Default         |                                                                                 |
| --------------- | ------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string`                  |                 | Checks the radio with this value when it changes. Pair it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                  |                 | The radio checked at first; none when left out.                                 |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |                 | Called with the value of the radio the user checks.                             |
| `bind:value`    | `Signal<string>`          |                 | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                      |
| `name`          | `string`                  | a generated one | The name the radios share and submit under (a Field's `name` inside a Field).   |
| `required`      | `boolean`                 | `false`         | A radio must be checked to submit the form (`aria-required` on the group).      |
| `readOnly`      | `boolean`                 | `false`         | The radios cannot be checked, but stay focusable and are submitted.             |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`                 | `false`         | Disables every radio (a disabled fieldset).                                     |

Every other `<fieldset>` prop passes through. Inside a Field, the group takes the field's
`aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`, and its radios the field's name.

### Radio.Root

| Prop       | Type      | Default |                                                         |
| ---------- | --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`    | `string`  |         | Required: the value the group takes when it is checked. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | It cannot be checked; the arrow keys skip it.           |

Every other native prop passes through (`id`, `class`, `aria-*`).

**Differences from Base UI's RadioGroup and Radio.** The radios are native inputs in a fieldset, so
there is no `Radio.Indicator` (style `:checked` with `appearance: none`) and no `nativeButton` or
`inputRef`.

## Example

In an island, bound to a signal:

```tsx check
import { Fieldset, Radio, RadioGroup } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function ShippingChoice() {
  const speed = signal("standard");
  return (
    <div>
      <RadioGroup name="shipping" bind:value={speed} class="lu-fieldset">
        <Fieldset.Legend>Shipping</Fieldset.Legend>
        <label>
          <Radio.Root value="standard" class="lu-radio" /> Standard
        </label>
        <label>
          <Radio.Root value="express" class="lu-radio" /> Express
        </label>
        <label>
          <Radio.Root value="drone" disabled class="lu-radio" /> Drone (soon)
        </label>
      </RadioGroup>
      <p>Arrives {speed() === "express" ? "tomorrow" : "in three days"}.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-fieldset` on the group and `lu-radio` on each radio: an 18px
circle in a 24px target, a thick primary ring when checked (a shape, not only a colour), a focus
ring.

**With your own CSS**, style the inputs and their state: `:checked`, `:disabled`,
`:focus-visible`; the group: `[role="radiogroup"]`, `[aria-invalid="true"]`.

Radio Group ships no stylesheet: it needs none to work.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key                     | Does                                                            |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab                     | Into the group, on the checked radio (or the first); out of it. |
| Arrow Down, Arrow Right | Checks the next enabled radio, around at the end.               |
| Arrow Up, Arrow Left    | Checks the previous enabled radio.                              |
| Space                   | Checks the focused radio.                                       |

Enter does not check a radio. Read-only radios move focus but do not change.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

Native radios: the roving tab stop, the arrow keys, `required`, submission and reset work with no
script. The shared checkbox script (0.5 kB brotli,
[Checkbox](checkbox.md#without-javascript-and-the-client-script)) adds read-only.

## Browser support

Native radios and `role="radiogroup"` on a fieldset: every supported browser.

## Related

- [Checkbox Group](checkbox-group.md): several values.
- [Select](select.md): one value from a longer list.
- [Field](field.md): a description and errors for the group.
- [Fieldset](fieldset.md): the legend.

<!-- source: scroll-area.md -->

# Scroll Area

> A scrolling region with custom scrollbars laid over native scrolling, after Base UI's ScrollArea. The viewport scrolls natively (the wheel, touch, the keyboard, find-in-page), is focusable while it overflows, and traps nothing; without JavaScript its native scrollbars show. `<lu-scroll-area>`'s 1.4 kB script hides them and draws its own, which show on hover, while scrolling and while focused, take a thumb drag and a track press, and expose the overflow as data attributes and CSS variables.

```ts
import { ScrollArea } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/scroll-area"
import "@lumiose/ui/scroll-area.css"; // or "@lumiose/ui/styles.css" for every component
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<ScrollArea.Root>
  <ScrollArea.Viewport>
    <ScrollArea.Content />
  </ScrollArea.Viewport>
  <ScrollArea.Scrollbar>
    <ScrollArea.Thumb />
  </ScrollArea.Scrollbar>
  <ScrollArea.Scrollbar orientation="horizontal">
    <ScrollArea.Thumb />
  </ScrollArea.Scrollbar>
  <ScrollArea.Corner />
</ScrollArea.Root>
```

| Part        | Renders                                                                                             |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`      | `<lu-scroll-area>`: give it a size (a height or a max height); the viewport fills it                |
| `Viewport`  | `<div tabindex="0" data-viewport>`: scrolls natively; `tabindex="-1"` while nothing overflows       |
| `Content`   | `<div>`, at least as wide as what it holds                                                          |
| `Scrollbar` | `<div aria-hidden="true" data-scrollbar data-orientation>` over an edge; hidden while its axis fits |
| `Thumb`     | `<div data-thumb>`, sized and moved by the script                                                   |
| `Corner`    | `<div data-corner hidden>`, where the scrollbars meet, shown while both axes overflow               |

## API

### ScrollArea.Root

| Prop                    | Type     | Default |                                                                                       |
| ----------------------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `overflowEdgeThreshold` | `number` | `0`     | How many px of content past an edge before `data-overflow-*-start` or `-end` applies. |

### ScrollArea.Scrollbar

| Prop          | Type                         | Default      |                                                             |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` | `"vertical"` | The edge and axis: the inline end, or the bottom.           |
| `keepMounted` | `boolean`                    | `false`      | Keeps the scrollbar shown while its axis does not overflow. |

### The other parts

Each part passes the props of its element through. Give the `Viewport` an `aria-label` and
`role="region"` when it holds a section people should find; the scrollbars are `aria-hidden`
pointer conveniences, since the viewport itself scrolls from the keyboard.

**Data attributes and CSS variables.** On Root and Viewport: `data-has-overflow-x`,
`data-has-overflow-y`, `data-overflow-x-start`, `-x-end`, `-y-start`, `-y-end`, `data-scrolling`
(Root). On the Viewport: `--lu-scroll-area-overflow-x-start` (and `-x-end`, `-y-start`, `-y-end`),
the px of content past each edge, for fades. On the Scrollbars: `data-orientation`,
`data-hovering`, `data-scrolling`, and `--lu-scroll-area-thumb-height` (or `-width`). On Root:
`--lu-scroll-area-corner-width` and `-height`.

**What CSS can do alone.** `scrollbar-color`, `scrollbar-width` and `scrollbar-gutter` recolour
and thin the native scrollbar in every current browser, with no script; they cannot shape it, lay
it over the content, or show it only on hover. Style the native scrollbar that way for pages
without JavaScript; the custom scrollbars take over once the script runs.

**Differences from Base UI's ScrollArea.** The custom properties are `--lu-scroll-area-*` (Base
UI's `--scroll-area-*`); the viewport is focusable while it overflows; no `render`.

## Example

```tsx check
import { ScrollArea } from "@lumiose/ui";

const RELEASES = ["1.4.0", "1.3.2", "1.3.1", "1.3.0", "1.2.0", "1.1.0", "1.0.0"];

export function ReleaseList() {
  return (
    <ScrollArea.Root class="lu-scroll-area" style={{ "block-size": "8rem" }}>
      <ScrollArea.Viewport role="region" aria-label="Releases">
        <ScrollArea.Content>
          <ul>
            {RELEASES.map((release) => (
              <li>{release}</li>
            ))}
          </ul>
        </ScrollArea.Content>
      </ScrollArea.Viewport>
      <ScrollArea.Scrollbar>
        <ScrollArea.Thumb />
      </ScrollArea.Scrollbar>
    </ScrollArea.Root>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-scroll-area` on `Root`: a bordered box, padded content, 10px
scrollbars whose rounded thumbs (`--lu-muted-foreground`, 3:1) show while the pointer is over the
area, while it scrolls and while it has focus, and an inward focus ring on the viewport.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class`, `[data-scrollbar]`, `[data-thumb]`,
`[data-orientation]`, `[data-hovering]`, `[data-scrolling]` and the overflow attributes and
custom properties above; a fade at an edge reads `--lu-scroll-area-overflow-y-end`.

`@lumiose/ui/scroll-area.css` (0.3 kB brotli) fills the root with the viewport, hides the native
scrollbar once the script runs (`:defined`) and the custom ones until then, places the scrollbars
over the edges leaving room for the corner, and sizes the thumbs from the custom properties.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key                         | Does                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab                         | Onto the viewport while it overflows, then on: no trap. |
| Arrow keys                  | Scroll a line.                                          |
| Page Up / Page Down / Space | Scroll a page.                                          |
| Home / End                  | The top or the bottom.                                  |

The keys are the browser's own scrolling of the focused viewport. A focusable child (a link) takes
focus first, and the viewport scrolls it into view.

## Without JavaScript, and the element's script

The viewport scrolls with its native scrollbars, from the keyboard too. `<lu-scroll-area>`'s script
(1.4 kB brotli) hides them and runs the custom ones: thumbs sized and moved on every scroll and
resize (a ResizeObserver follows content that grows), dragging and track presses, hover and
scrolling states, the overflow attributes and variables, the corner, right to left.

## Browser support

`scrollbar-width: none` and `::-webkit-scrollbar`, ResizeObserver and pointer capture: every
supported browser.

## Related

- [Dialog](dialog.md): a modal whose long content scrolls in a Scroll Area.
- [Combobox](combobox.md) and [Select](select.md): lists that scroll on their own.

<!-- source: select.md -->

# Select

> A native `<select>` for picking one value from a list: it works with no JavaScript, submits with its form and keeps the platform's keyboard, typeahead and mobile pickers. Where the browser has customizable select (`appearance: base-select`, Chrome 135, Safari 27), `Select.Trigger` and `Select.Value` shape the button, the picker is styleable and options may hold more than text; elsewhere it is the classic select. No script; `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync in islands.

```ts
import { Select } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/select"
import "@lumiose/ui/select.css"; // makes a select with a Trigger a customizable select
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Select.Root>
  <Select.Trigger>
    <Select.Value />
  </Select.Trigger>
  <Select.Item />
  <Select.Separator />
  <Select.Group>
    <Select.Item />
  </Select.Group>
</Select.Root>
```

| Part        | Renders                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`      | `<select>`, the control (`role="combobox"`), with the props it is given.                                |
| `Trigger`   | `<button type="button">`, customizable select's button. Optional; it must be the first child of `Root`. |
| `Value`     | `<selectedcontent>`, where the browser copies the selected option's content. Inside the `Trigger`.      |
| `Item`      | `<option value="…">`.                                                                                   |
| `Group`     | `<optgroup label="…">` of options.                                                                      |
| `Separator` | `<hr>` between options or groups.                                                                       |

The picker, the popup of options, is the select's own `::picker(select)`: there is no part for it.
Browsers without customizable select drop the `Trigger` and show their own control and picker, with
the options' text.

## API

### Select.Root

| Prop            | Type                      | Default          |                                                                                   |
| --------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string`                  |                  | Selects the option with this value when it changes. Pair it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                  | the first option | The option selected at first, when `value` is left out.                           |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |                  | Called after the user selects another option, with its value.                     |
| `bind:value`    | `Signal<string>`          |                  | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                        |
| `name`          | `string`                  |                  | The name the value is submitted under.                                            |
| `required`      | `boolean`                 | `false`          | The form needs a value: an option whose value is `""` counts as none.             |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`                 | `false`          | The select cannot be used.                                                        |

Every other `<select>` prop passes through: `id`, `autocomplete`, `form`, `class`, `aria-*`, event
handlers. Name it with a `<label for>` pointing at its `id`, or `aria-label`, or put it in a
[Field](field.md) with a `Field.Label`: it takes the field's id, name and ARIA references.

### Select.Item

| Prop       | Type      | Default |                                                                   |
| ---------- | --------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`    | `string`  |         | Required: the value the select takes, and submits, when selected. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | The option cannot be selected; the arrow keys skip it.            |

### Select.Group

| Prop    | Type     | Default |                                                    |
| ------- | -------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` | `string` |         | Required: the group's name, shown above its items. |

### The other parts

`Trigger`, `Value` and `Separator` take the props of the element they render (`class`, `style`,
`aria-*`, `data-*`) and pass them through.

**Differences from Base UI's Select.** Select is the native control, chosen over the listbox
pattern because it works without JavaScript, carries forms, autofill, validation and the mobile
pickers, and ships no script. So it has no `open`, `onOpenChange` or `modal` (the platform fires no
event when the picker opens; style `:open` instead), no `Label` (use `<label for>`), no `multiple`
(use [Combobox](combobox.md) with `multiple`), no `alignItemWithTrigger` (the picker opens below the
control and flips), no `Portal`, `Positioner`, `Popup`, `List`, `Icon`, `ItemText`,
`ItemIndicator`, `GroupLabel`, `Arrow` or scroll arrows (the picker, `::picker-icon` and
`option::checkmark` are the platform's), and Enter does not open it (Space and the arrows do, as on
any select).

## Example

A select in a server-rendered page, with no island, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { Select } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function PlanField() {
  return (
    <form method="post">
      <label for="plan">Plan</label>
      <Select.Root id="plan" name="plan" defaultValue="pro" class="lu-select">
        <Select.Trigger>
          <Select.Value />
        </Select.Trigger>
        <Select.Item value="free">Free</Select.Item>
        <Select.Item value="pro">Pro</Select.Item>
        <Select.Separator />
        <Select.Group label="Teams">
          <Select.Item value="team">Team</Select.Item>
          <Select.Item value="enterprise" disabled>
            Enterprise
          </Select.Item>
        </Select.Group>
      </Select.Root>
      <button class="lu-button">Save</button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

In an island, bound to a signal. `bind:value={theme}` is short for `value={theme()}` plus
`onValueChange={(next) => theme.set(next)}`.

```tsx check
import { Select } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function ThemePicker() {
  const theme = signal("system");
  return (
    <Select.Root aria-label="Theme" bind:value={theme} class="lu-select">
      <Select.Trigger>
        <Select.Value />
      </Select.Trigger>
      <Select.Item value="light">Light</Select.Item>
      <Select.Item value="dark">Dark</Select.Item>
      <Select.Item value="system">System</Select.Item>
    </Select.Root>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-select` on `Root`. It makes the select a customizable select
and styles the control, the picker, the options (hover and keyboard focus, disabled), the groups and
the separators; in browsers without customizable select it styles the closed control. Its colours
come from the theme's `--lu-` properties ([UI components](README.md#the-default-theme)).

**With your own CSS**, opt in to customizable select and style the select's parts and states:

- the control: the `select` itself, `:open` while its picker is open, `:focus-visible`,
  `:disabled`, `:invalid` and `:user-invalid`, and `::picker-icon`;
- the picker: `::picker(select)`, placed with anchor positioning (`position-area`,
  `position-try-fallbacks` work on it);
- options: `option`, `option:checked`, `option:hover`, `option:focus-visible`, `option:disabled`,
  and `option::checkmark`;
- `optgroup`, `hr`, and inside the `Trigger`, `selectedcontent`.

A starting point:

```css
.select,
.select::picker(select) {
  appearance: base-select;
}
.select {
  padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem;
  border: 1px solid #85858e;
  border-radius: 0.5rem;
}
.select::picker(select) {
  padding: 0.25rem;
  border: 1px solid #e4e4e7;
  border-radius: 0.5rem;
}
.select option:focus-visible {
  background: #f4f4f5;
  outline: 2px solid #2563eb;
  outline-offset: -2px;
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/select.css` holds what Select needs to work, in the `lu.core` layer: a select whose
first child is a `Trigger` gets `appearance: base-select` (and so does its picker), since only a
customizable select renders the trigger, `Value` and options with more than text. A select with no
`Trigger` keeps the browser's look until your CSS or the theme opts in.

## Keyboard and focus

The platform's: the select is one tab stop with `role="combobox"`, and the browser runs the
keyboard. In Chromium's customizable select:

| Key                         | Does                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Space, Arrow Down, Arrow Up | On the control: opens the picker, with focus on the selected option.                                    |
| Alt+Arrow Down, F4          | On the control: opens the picker.                                                                       |
| Arrow Down, Arrow Up        | In the picker: the next or previous option; disabled options are skipped.                               |
| Home, End                   | In the picker: the first or last option.                                                                |
| A character                 | In the picker: typeahead, the next option whose text starts with it.                                    |
| Enter, Space                | In the picker: selects the focused option and closes the picker.                                        |
| Escape                      | Closes the picker without selecting, focus back on the control; closed, it goes on, so a dialog closes. |
| Tab                         | In the picker: closes it, focus back on the control; from there Tab moves on.                           |

A click on a `<label for>` focuses the select without opening it. A click on the control opens the
picker; a click on an option selects it; a click outside closes the picker. Other browsers keep
their own select keyboard and pickers, which differ by platform.

## Without JavaScript

Select needs none: it is a native control, in server HTML and with JavaScript off, on every
browser. It submits under its `name`, is validated (`required`), resets with its form, takes the
browser's autofill and is disabled by a disabled `<fieldset>`. `value`, `onValueChange` and
`bind:value` need the component to run in the browser, in an island; there `value` sets the
control's value when it changes, and its `change` event calls `onValueChange`.

## Browser support

- **Customizable select** (`appearance: base-select`, `::picker(select)`, `<selectedcontent>`, a
  `<button>` and rich content inside `<select>`): Chrome and Edge 135, Safari 27. Firefox has none
  yet: it shows its classic select, styled by the theme when closed, with the options' text.
- In browsers without customizable select, the HTML parser drops the `Trigger` and tags inside
  options from server HTML, so an island's select falls back to rendering on the client there
  ([LUM4006](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/errors/LUM4006/)); keep options to text if that
  matters to you.
- **`:open`** comes with customizable select; Safari 27's support is unverified here (the
  end-to-end tests run in Chromium).

## Related

- [Combobox](combobox.md): when the list is long enough to filter, for several values, or for
  async options.
- [Menu](menu.md): commands rather than a value.
- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling, the default theme and the other components.
- [Islands](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/islands/): running a component in the
  browser, for `bind:value`.

<!-- source: separator.md -->

# Separator

> A native `<hr>` between groups of content, after Base UI's Separator: announced as a separator, horizontal by default, or vertical between the items of a row with `aria-orientation="vertical"`. No script.

```ts
import { Separator } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/separator"
import "@lumiose/ui/separator.css"; // a vertical separator's margins and height in a row
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Separator />
```

| Part        | Renders                                                                              |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Separator` | `<hr data-orientation="…">`, with `aria-orientation="vertical"` when it is vertical. |

An `<hr>` is a separator for assistive technology with no role to add. It is flow content: it
cannot go inside a `<p>`, a `<span>` or a `<button>`, where the browser would move it out of the
element.

## API

### Separator

| Prop          | Type                         | Default        |                                                                           |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Which way it runs: `"vertical"` between the items of a row (a toolbar's). |

Every other native prop passes through: `class`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`.

**Differences from Base UI's Separator.** It is always an `<hr>`, not a `<div role="separator">`:
no `render`. A horizontal one leaves out `aria-orientation="horizontal"`, an `<hr>`'s default.

## Example

Links in a row, split into groups, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { Separator } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function FooterLinks() {
  return (
    <nav aria-label="Footer" style={{ display: "flex", gap: "0.75rem", "align-items": "center" }}>
      <a href="#docs">Docs</a>
      <a href="#blog">Blog</a>
      <Separator orientation="vertical" class="lu-separator" />
      <a href="#privacy">Privacy</a>
      <a href="#terms">Terms</a>
    </nav>
  );
}
```

Between sections of a page or a card, a horizontal one:

```tsx check
import { Separator } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function AccountCard() {
  return (
    <section aria-label="Account">
      <p>Signed in as ada@example.com</p>
      <Separator class="lu-separator" />
      <p>Plan: Free</p>
    </section>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-separator` on it: a 1px line in `--lu-border`, with a margin
above and below when horizontal, and as tall as its row when vertical.

**With your own CSS**, style it through `class` and `[data-orientation]`. Reset the borders an
`<hr>` has by default, and draw the line with a background:

```css
.separator {
  border: 0;
  background: #e4e4e7;
}
.separator[data-orientation="horizontal"] {
  block-size: 1px;
  margin: 1rem 0;
}
.separator[data-orientation="vertical"] {
  inline-size: 1px;
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/separator.css`, in the `lu.core` layer, gives a vertical separator no margins (an
`<hr>`'s automatic ones would push the row's items apart) and the full height of its row, even one
that centres its items (`align-self: stretch`).

## Keyboard and focus

A separator takes no focus and has no keys: it only structures the content around it.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

A native `<hr>` with attributes: it needs no script, on the server or in an island.

## Browser support

Native `<hr>` and `aria-orientation`: every browser.

## Related

- [Menu](menu.md): `Menu.Separator` between a menu's items.
- [Select](select.md): separators between a select's options.
- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling and the other components.

<!-- source: slider.md -->

# Slider

> A value picked within a range by dragging or with the keys, or a range with two thumbs, after Base UI's Slider. Each thumb is a native `<input type="range">`, so it drags, takes the arrow keys, Home and End, follows the text direction and submits with its form, in server HTML and without JavaScript. `<lu-slider>` adds Page Up and Page Down, keeps a range's thumbs in order, moves the nearest thumb on a press on the track and keeps the value text current. `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync.

```ts
import { Slider } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/slider"
import "@lumiose/ui/slider.css"; // or "@lumiose/ui/styles.css" for every component
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Slider.Root>
  <Slider.Label />
  <Slider.Value />
  <Slider.Control>
    <Slider.Track>
      <Slider.Indicator />
    </Slider.Track>
    <Slider.Thumb />
  </Slider.Control>
</Slider.Root>
```

| Part        | Renders                                                                            |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`      | `<lu-slider data-orientation>` with `--lu-slider-start` and `--lu-slider-end`      |
| `Label`     | `<label for>` the first thumb; thumbs without an `aria-label` are labelled by it   |
| `Value`     | `<output for>` the thumbs, with the formatted values (`20 – 80`)                   |
| `Control`   | `<div>`: the track and the thumbs stacked in one place; presses on it move a thumb |
| `Track`     | `<div>`: the rail                                                                  |
| `Indicator` | `<div>`: the selected part, from `--lu-slider-start` to `--lu-slider-end`          |
| `Thumb`     | `<input type="range" min max step value name>`, one per value, in order            |

## API

### Slider.Root

| Prop                     | Type                           | Default        |                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------ | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`                  | `number \| number[]`           |                | Moves the thumbs when it changes (an array: one value per thumb). Pair it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue`           | `number \| number[]`           | `min`          | The value at first; a form reset goes back to it.                                               |
| `onValueChange`          | `(value) => void`              |                | Called with the new value as a thumb moves.                                                     |
| `onValueCommitted`       | `(value) => void`              |                | Called when a move ends: a release, a key press.                                                |
| `bind:value`             | `Signal<number \| number[]>`   |                | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                                      |
| `min`                    | `number`                       | `0`            | The smallest value.                                                                             |
| `max`                    | `number`                       | `100`          | The largest value.                                                                              |
| `step`                   | `number`                       | `1`            | The step of the arrow keys; values snap to it.                                                  |
| `largeStep`              | `number`                       | `10`           | The step of Page Up, Page Down and Shift with an arrow key.                                     |
| `minStepsBetweenValues`  | `number`                       | `0`            | With several thumbs: how many steps apart they stay.                                            |
| `thumbCollisionBehavior` | `"push"` \| `"none"`           | `"push"`       | With several thumbs: a thumb moved into another pushes it along, or stops at it.                |
| `orientation`            | `"horizontal"` \| `"vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Vertical sliders run bottom to top.                                                             |
| `disabled`               | `boolean`                      | `false`        | Disables every thumb.                                                                           |
| `name`                   | `string`                       |                | The thumbs submit their values under it, one entry each.                                        |
| `form`                   | `string`                       |                | The id of a form the thumbs belong to, when they are outside it.                                |
| `format`                 | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`     | plain numbers  | How the values are written; with it, each thumb's `aria-valuetext` is its formatted value.      |
| `locale`                 | `string`                       | the browser's  | The locale of the formatted values (the server's in server HTML).                               |

The value's type follows `value`, `defaultValue` or `bind:value`: a number for one thumb, a
`number[]` for a range. Every other prop passes through to `<lu-slider>`: `id`, `class`, `style`.

### The other parts

`Label` takes `<label>` props. `Value` takes `<output>` props, and its `children` may be a function
`(formattedValues, values) => JSX.Element` (then it has no `for`, and you render its text). `Control`,
`Track` and `Indicator` take `<div>` props. `Thumb` takes `<input>` props except the range's own
(`aria-label`, `aria-valuetext`, `disabled`, `id`, `class`). Give each thumb of a range an
`aria-label` with the label's text in it ("Minimum price" under "Price"), so speech users can say
what they see (WCAG 2.5.3). Inside a Field, the first thumb takes the field's id, name,
description and error.

**Differences from Base UI's Slider.** Thumbs are the range inputs themselves, so there is no hidden
input, no `inputRef`, no `getAriaLabel` (use `aria-label` on each Thumb) and no
`thumbAlignment` (native thumbs stay inside the track, as Base UI's `"edge"`).
`thumbCollisionBehavior="swap"` is not supported. `format` is `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` and
`locale` a string, both written to the element for its script.

## Example

A price range, in an island:

```tsx check
import { Slider } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function PriceRange() {
  const price = signal([20, 80]);
  return (
    <Slider.Root
      name="price"
      bind:value={price}
      minStepsBetweenValues={5}
      format={{ style: "currency", currency: "EUR", maximumFractionDigits: 0 }}
      class="lu-slider"
    >
      <Slider.Label>Price</Slider.Label>
      <Slider.Value />
      <Slider.Control>
        <Slider.Track>
          <Slider.Indicator />
        </Slider.Track>
        <Slider.Thumb aria-label="Minimum price" />
        <Slider.Thumb aria-label="Maximum price" />
      </Slider.Control>
    </Slider.Root>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-slider` on `Root`: the label and the value on a row above a 24px
tall control, an 8px track edged in `--lu-input` (3:1), the selected part in the primary colour,
and 24px round thumbs with a focus ring around the thumb. Vertical sliders are 10rem tall.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class`, the thumbs' pseudo-elements
(`::-webkit-slider-thumb`, `::-moz-range-thumb`), `[data-orientation="vertical"]`, `:disabled`,
`:focus-visible`, and the Indicator through `--lu-slider-start` and `--lu-slider-end`. Over a Track,
the thumbs' own tracks are transparent (`appearance: none`).

`@lumiose/ui/slider.css` (0.3 kB brotli) stacks the track and thumbs, spans the Indicator, writes
vertical thumbs bottom to top and lets only the thumbs of a range take the pointer.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key                     | Does                                                                         |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab                     | Moves between the thumbs, then on: one tab stop per thumb.                   |
| Arrow Right / Arrow Up  | One step up (Arrow Left goes up right to left).                              |
| Arrow Left / Arrow Down | One step down (Arrow Right goes down right to left).                         |
| Page Up / Page Down     | `largeStep` up or down.                                                      |
| Shift + an arrow        | `largeStep` in that direction.                                               |
| Home / End              | The minimum or the maximum (a range's thumb stops at, or pushes, the other). |

Every drag has these keys as its alternative (WCAG 2.5.7). A press on a range's track moves the
nearest thumb there and focuses it; a press on a single slider's track moves its thumb.

## Without JavaScript, and the element's script

The thumbs are native range inputs: dragging, the arrows, Home, End, right to left, vertical,
submission, `disabled` and reset work with no script, and the server HTML has the Indicator's
custom properties and the value text. `<lu-slider>`'s script (1.5 kB brotli) adds Page Up and Page
Down, keeps a range's thumbs in order and apart, moves the nearest thumb on a press on its track,
and keeps the Indicator, `aria-valuetext` and the Value text current (also after a form reset).
Without it, a range's thumbs can cross, and the Value text and the Indicator stay where the server
put them.

## Browser support

Native range inputs: every browser. Vertical sliders use `writing-mode: vertical-lr` on the thumbs
(Chrome 124, Safari 17.4, Firefox 120 and later).

## Related

- [Field](field.md): a label, description and error for a slider.
- [Meter](meter.md): show a value in a range, without picking it.
- [Input](input.md): `type="number"` for an exact value.

<!-- source: switch.md -->

# Switch

> On or off, for a setting: a native `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">`, after Base UI's Switch. Space and a label click toggle it, the form submits its value when on, `required` and reset work, in server HTML and without JavaScript, and assistive technology announces a switch. `bind:checked` keeps a signal in sync.

```ts
import { Switch } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/switch"
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<label>
  <Switch.Root /> Label
</label>
```

| Part   | Renders                                                                |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root` | `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">`; `aria-readonly` if read-only. |

## API

### Switch.Root

| Prop              | Type                         | Default |                                                                     |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checked`         | `boolean`                    |         | Turns it on or off when it changes. Pair it with `onCheckedChange`. |
| `defaultChecked`  | `boolean`                    | `false` | Whether it starts on; a form reset goes back to it.                 |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` |         | Called after the user turns it on or off.                           |
| `bind:checked`    | `Signal<boolean>`            |         | Stands in for `checked` and `onCheckedChange`.                      |
| `value`           | `string`                     | `"on"`  | What it submits when on.                                            |
| `readOnly`        | `boolean`                    | `false` | It cannot be toggled, but stays focusable and is submitted.         |

Every other native prop passes through: `name`, `required`, `disabled`, `form`, `id`, `class`,
`aria-*`. Inside a Field it takes the field's wiring.

**Differences from Base UI's Switch.** The switch is the native input, so there is no
`Switch.Thumb`: draw the track and thumb with `appearance: none` and `::before`. No `nativeButton`,
`inputRef` or `uncheckedValue` (an off switch submits nothing). `<input switch>` exists only in
Safari, so `role="switch"` stays on a checkbox everywhere.

## Example

In an island, bound to a signal:

```tsx check
import { Switch } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function AirplaneMode() {
  const on = signal(false);
  return (
    <p>
      <label>
        <Switch.Root name="airplane" bind:checked={on} class="lu-switch" /> Airplane mode
      </label>{" "}
      {on() ? "Radios off." : ""}
    </p>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-switch` on `Root`: a 40 by 24px track (`--lu-input` when off,
the primary colour when on) and a white thumb on the side that tells on from off, a focus ring.

**With your own CSS**, style the input and its state: `:checked`, `:disabled`, `:focus-visible`,
`[aria-readonly="true"]`, `[aria-invalid="true"]`.

Switch ships no stylesheet: it needs none to work.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key   | Does                                     |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Space | Turns it on or off (not when read-only). |
| Tab   | Moves on: one tab stop.                  |

Enter does not toggle it. A click on its label does.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

A native checkbox with the switch role: toggling, submission, `required`, reset and `disabled`
work with no script. The shared checkbox script (0.5 kB brotli,
[Checkbox](checkbox.md#without-javascript-and-the-client-script)) adds read-only.

## Browser support

`role="switch"` on a checkbox: every supported browser and screen reader.

## Related

- [Checkbox](checkbox.md): a choice to confirm, submitted with a form.
- [Field](field.md): a description and errors for a switch.

<!-- source: tabs.md -->

# Tabs

> A tab list and the panel of the selected tab, after the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: the server HTML holds the whole state (roles, `aria-selected`, the roving tab stop, the hidden panels), and `<lu-tabs>`, a 0.8 kB light-DOM element, adds the arrow keys and the selection. Manual or automatic activation, horizontal or vertical, right-to-left aware; `bind:value` (or `value` and `onValueChange`) keeps a signal in sync.

```ts
import { Tabs } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/tabs"
import "@lumiose/ui/tabs.css"; // makes <lu-tabs> a block
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Tabs.Root>
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Tab />
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Panel />
</Tabs.Root>
```

| Part    | Renders                                                                                                                   |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`  | `<lu-tabs>`, the element that handles the keys and the selection.                                                         |
| `List`  | `<div role="tablist">`, with `aria-orientation="vertical"` when vertical. Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. |
| `Tab`   | `<button type="button" role="tab" value="…" aria-selected="…" aria-controls="…" tabindex="…">`.                           |
| `Panel` | `<div role="tabpanel" tabindex="0" aria-labelledby="…">`, `hidden` unless its tab is selected.                            |

A `Tab` and a `Panel` with the same `value` belong together. Every panel stays in the page, hidden
when its tab is not selected, so the browser can switch them before any script loads.

## API

### Tabs.Root

| Prop            | Type                         | Default               |                                                  |
| --------------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`         | `string`                     |                       | Selects the tab with this value when it changes. |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                     | the first enabled tab | The tab selected at first, without `value`.      |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void`    |                       | Called after the user selects another tab.       |
| `bind:value`    | `Signal<string>`             |                       | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.       |
| `orientation`   | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"`        | Which arrow keys move between the tabs.          |

`Root` also takes the props of an element (`class`, `style`, `data-*`, events) and passes them to
`<lu-tabs>`.

### Tabs.List

| Prop              | Type      | Default |                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `activateOnFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Selects a tab as soon as it receives focus (automatic activation), as Zag does by default. |
| `loopFocus`       | `boolean` | `true`  | The arrow keys go from the last tab to the first and back.                                 |

The element reads them from the list's attributes: `data-activate-on-focus` and
`data-loop-focus="false"`.

### Tabs.Tab and Tabs.Panel

| Prop       | On    | Type      |                                                               |
| ---------- | ----- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`    | both  | `string`  | Pairs a tab with its panel. Required.                         |
| `disabled` | `Tab` | `boolean` | The tab takes focus but cannot be selected (`aria-disabled`). |

Each takes the props of the element it renders. `role`, `id`, `value`, `aria-selected`,
`aria-controls`, `aria-labelledby`, `tabindex` on tabs and `hidden` stay the parts' own.

- **Disabled tabs.** A selected tab that becomes disabled gives its selection to the first enabled
  tab. With every tab disabled, none is selected and the first tab is the tab stop.
- **The element.** `<lu-tabs>`' `value` property reads and sets the selection, and it fires
  `valuechange` (not bubbling) when the user changes it, so `bind:value` works on the element too.

## Example

```tsx check
import { Tabs } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function AccountSettings() {
  return (
    <Tabs.Root class="lu-tabs" defaultValue="account">
      <Tabs.List aria-label="Account settings">
        <Tabs.Tab value="account">Account</Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Tab value="password">Password</Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Tab value="billing" disabled>
          Billing
        </Tabs.Tab>
      </Tabs.List>
      <Tabs.Panel value="account">Your name and email.</Tabs.Panel>
      <Tabs.Panel value="password">Change your password.</Tabs.Panel>
      <Tabs.Panel value="billing">Invoices and payment methods.</Tabs.Panel>
    </Tabs.Root>
  );
}
```

In an island, bound to a signal: `bind:value={tab}` is short for `value={tab()}` plus
`onValueChange={(next) => tab.set(next)}`.

```tsx check
import { Tabs } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function Project() {
  const tab = signal("overview");
  return (
    <>
      <Tabs.Root class="lu-tabs" bind:value={tab}>
        <Tabs.List aria-label="Project" activateOnFocus>
          <Tabs.Tab value="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
          <Tabs.Tab value="settings">Settings</Tabs.Tab>
        </Tabs.List>
        <Tabs.Panel value="overview">The project at a glance.</Tabs.Panel>
        <Tabs.Panel value="settings">Name and members.</Tabs.Panel>
      </Tabs.Root>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => tab.set("settings")}>
        Open the settings
      </button>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-tabs` on `Root`: tabs in a row (or a column when vertical)
over a rule, the selected one underlined (beside it when vertical) in the foreground colour,
disabled ones faded, and focus rings on tabs and panels. The list wraps on narrow screens.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class` and their state: `[role="tab"]`,
`[aria-selected="true"]`, `[aria-disabled="true"]`, `[role="tablist"][aria-orientation="vertical"]`
and `[role="tabpanel"]`. Mark the selected tab with more than a colour (WCAG 1.4.1), such as a bar
or a weight, at 3:1 against its background (WCAG 1.4.11).

```css
.tabs [role="tab"] {
  padding: 0.5rem 1rem;
  border: 0;
  background: none;
  color: #52525b;
}
.tabs [role="tab"][aria-selected="true"] {
  color: #09090b;
  box-shadow: inset 0 -2px currentColor;
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/tabs.css` holds one rule, in the `lu.core` layer: `lu-tabs { display: block }`.

## Keyboard and focus

The [WAI-ARIA tabs pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/):

| Key                   | Does                                                                                               |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab                   | Into the list, onto the selected tab; out of it, onto the panel.                                   |
| ArrowRight, ArrowLeft | The next or previous tab (horizontal). Swapped in right-to-left. Loops unless `loopFocus={false}`. |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp    | The next or previous tab (vertical).                                                               |
| Home, End             | The first or last tab.                                                                             |
| Enter, Space          | Selects the focused tab (manual activation).                                                       |

- **Manual activation** (the default, as in Base UI): the arrows move focus and Enter, Space or a
  click selects. With `activateOnFocus`, moving focus selects too. Either way only the panels
  change: nothing navigates or submits.
- **Only the main button** selects: a right-click does not. Disabled tabs take focus but are
  never selected.
- The arrow keys do nothing while an input method is composing, or with Alt, Ctrl or Meta held.

## Without JavaScript, and the element's script

The server HTML is complete: the selected tab, its panel and the tab stop are right before any
script loads, and the panels of the other tabs are `hidden`. Selecting another tab needs
`<lu-tabs>`' script, a 0.8 kB (brotli) module that a page rendering `Tabs` loads once, without
the Lumiose runtime; islands bundle it. `value`, `onValueChange` and `bind:value` need the
component to run in an island.

## Browser support

- **Custom elements** (`<lu-tabs>`) and everything the element uses: every current browser.
- The default theme's vertical tabs follow the direction with `:dir()`: Chrome and Edge 120,
  Firefox 49, Safari 16.4.

## Related

- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling, the default theme and the other components.
- [Web components](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/guides/web-components/): custom elements, their properties and
  `bind:` on them.

<!-- source: toast.md -->

# Toast

> Short notices in a region of their own, after Base UI's toast: server HTML renders them (a form action's result), and islands add, update and close them through a toast manager. `<lu-toast-viewport>`, a 2.3 kB light-DOM element, puts them in the top layer, times them (pausing on hover and focus), limits how many show, closes them on a swipe, Escape or their close button, focuses the region on F6, and makes screen readers announce them.

```ts
import { Toast } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/toast"
import "@lumiose/ui/toast.css"; // the viewport's box, the limit, swipes on touch screens
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Toast.Provider>
  <Toast.Viewport>
    <Toast.Root>
      <Toast.Content>
        <Toast.Title />
        <Toast.Description />
      </Toast.Content>
      <Toast.Action />
      <Toast.Close />
    </Toast.Root>
  </Toast.Viewport>
</Toast.Provider>
```

| Part          | Renders                                                                                                          |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Provider`    | No element. Holds the toasts' defaults (`timeout`, `limit`) and a manager for `Toast.useToastManager()`.         |
| `Viewport`    | `<lu-toast-viewport role="region" aria-label="Notifications (F6)" tabindex="-1">`, the toasts' region.           |
| `Root`        | `<div role="status" aria-atomic="true">`, a toast: `role="alert"` for a high-priority one.                       |
| `Content`     | `<div>`, around the text.                                                                                        |
| `Title`       | `<h2>`: its children, or else the toast's `title`; nothing without either.                                       |
| `Description` | `<p>`: its children, or else the toast's `description`; nothing without either.                                  |
| `Action`      | `<button type="button">` with the toast's `actionProps`; nothing without them or children.                       |
| `Close`       | `<button type="button" command="--close-toast" commandfor="…">`: a custom invoker command that closes the toast. |

Each toast is a live region of its own, `role="status"` (announced when the reader is idle) or
`role="alert"` (announced at once), as in Zag; Base UI's are non-modal dialogs. The viewport is
a named region that F6 reaches.

## API

### Toast.createToastManager

`Toast.createToastManager()` returns a manager. Create one in a module and import it where toasts
are added and where they are shown: islands of a page share a module, so they share its manager.

| Method                      | Does                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toasts()`                  | The open toasts, newest first, read reactively: map them to `Toast.Root`s.                                                          |
| `add(options)`              | Adds a toast and returns its id. A toast with the `id` of an open one replaces it.                                                  |
| `update(id, options)`       | Changes an open toast in place: the same object, its fields read reactively, so its parts update without a new element.             |
| `close(id?)`                | Closes a toast, or every toast: it gets `transitionStatus: "ending"` and `data-ending-style`, then leaves after its exit animation. |
| `promise(promise, options)` | Shows a loading toast while `promise` runs (it stays), then turns it into a success or an error toast; returns `promise`.           |

The options of `add` and `update`:

| Option        | Type                              | Default |                                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | --------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | `string`                          | made up | An id of your own, to update or close the toast later.                                                          |
| `title`       | `string`                          |         | Shown by `Toast.Title`.                                                                                         |
| `description` | `string`                          |         | Shown by `Toast.Description`.                                                                                   |
| `type`        | `string`                          |         | A type of your own (`"success"`, `"error"`, `"loading"`): the toast's `data-type`, for styling.                 |
| `timeout`     | `number`                          | `5000`  | Milliseconds before it closes on its own; `0` keeps it until closed. The provider's `timeout` sets the default. |
| `priority`    | `"low" \| "high"`                 | `"low"` | `"high"` announces it at once (`role="alert"`), for errors that need attention.                                 |
| `actionProps` | `JSX.IntrinsicElements["button"]` |         | The props of its `Toast.Action`: `children` for the label, `onClick`.                                           |
| `onClose`     | `() => void`                      |         | Called when it starts closing.                                                                                  |
| `onRemove`    | `() => void`                      |         | Called once it is removed, after its exit animation.                                                            |

`promise`'s options are `loading`, `success` and `error`: options, a title, or (for `success` and
`error`) a function of the result. The loading toast has `type: "loading"` and `timeout: 0`; the
others `type: "success"` or `"error"` and the default timeout.

### Toast.Provider

| Prop           | Type           | Default   |                                                                                             |
| -------------- | -------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toastManager` | `ToastManager` | a new one | The manager its toasts come from, for `Toast.useToastManager()`.                            |
| `timeout`      | `number`       | `5000`    | Milliseconds before a toast closes on its own; `0` keeps toasts open.                       |
| `limit`        | `number`       | `3`       | How many toasts show at once; older ones wait, hidden and paused, until a newer one closes. |

`Toast.useToastManager()` returns the closest provider's manager.

### Toast.Root

| Prop             | Type                                      | Default             |                                                                  |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toast`          | `ToastObject \| ToastOptions`             |                     | The toast: one from a manager, or a plain object in server HTML. |
| `swipeDirection` | `("up" \| "down" \| "left" \| "right")[]` | `["down", "right"]` | The directions a swipe closes it in; `[]` turns swiping off.     |

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through. Your props override the defaults (`role`, `aria-label`,
`type`); `id`, `command` and `commandfor` stay the parts' own, since they connect them.

- **`Viewport`**: rename the region with `aria-label`; keep the hotkey in it.
- **`Root`**: the script fires a cancelable `close` event on it when a toast should close (a close
  button, Escape, a swipe, its timer); a managed toast handles it through its manager.
- **`Close`**: name it, with text or `aria-label`.

## Example

In an island, a button and the toasts it adds, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { Toast } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function SaveButton() {
  const toasts = Toast.createToastManager();
  return (
    <Toast.Provider toastManager={toasts}>
      <button
        type="button"
        class="lu-button"
        onClick={() => toasts.add({ title: "Saved", description: "Your changes are live." })}
      >
        Save
      </button>
      <Toast.Viewport class="lu-toast-viewport">
        {toasts.toasts().map((toast) => (
          <Toast.Root class="lu-toast" toast={toast}>
            <Toast.Title />
            <Toast.Description />
            <Toast.Close aria-label="Close">×</Toast.Close>
          </Toast.Root>
        ))}
      </Toast.Viewport>
    </Toast.Provider>
  );
}
```

A promise toast, and an error that stays (`timeout: 0`) with an action:

```tsx check
import { Toast } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function UploadButton() {
  const toasts = Toast.createToastManager();
  const upload = () =>
    toasts
      .promise(new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000)), {
        loading: "Uploading…",
        success: "Uploaded",
        error: "Upload failed",
      })
      .catch(() => undefined);
  const fail = () =>
    toasts.add({
      title: "Payment failed",
      description: "Check your card and try again.",
      type: "error",
      priority: "high",
      timeout: 0,
      actionProps: { children: "Retry", class: "lu-button", onClick: upload },
    });
  return (
    <Toast.Provider toastManager={toasts}>
      <button type="button" class="lu-button" onClick={upload}>
        Upload
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="lu-button" data-variant="destructive" onClick={fail}>
        Pay
      </button>
      <Toast.Viewport class="lu-toast-viewport">
        {toasts.toasts().map((toast) => (
          <Toast.Root class="lu-toast" toast={toast}>
            <Toast.Title />
            <Toast.Description />
            <Toast.Action />
            <Toast.Close aria-label="Close">×</Toast.Close>
          </Toast.Root>
        ))}
      </Toast.Viewport>
    </Toast.Provider>
  );
}
```

A form action's result in server HTML, with no island: the page renders the toast, and the
script times and closes it.

```tsx check
import { Toast } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function SaveResult(props: { saved: boolean }) {
  return (
    <Toast.Viewport class="lu-toast-viewport">
      {props.saved && (
        <Toast.Root class="lu-toast" toast={{ title: "Project saved" }}>
          <Toast.Title />
          <Toast.Close aria-label="Close">×</Toast.Close>
        </Toast.Root>
      )}
    </Toast.Viewport>
  );
}
```

To add toasts from several islands, create the manager in a module and import it in each: one
island renders the viewport from it, the others call `toasts.add()`.

```ts
// src/toasts.ts
import { Toast } from "@lumiose/ui";

export const toasts = Toast.createToastManager();
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-toast-viewport` on `Viewport` and `lu-toast` on each `Root`: a
column at the window's bottom end, popover surfaces with the title, description and a 28px close
button, a slide in, a fade out, and a swipe that leaves in its direction. `data-type="error"`
adds a red edge.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class` and the script's state:

- `[data-type]`, from the toast's `type`;
- `[data-starting-style]` on a new toast's first frame, and `[data-ending-style]` while it closes
  (the script, or the manager, waits for its animations before removing it);
- `[data-swiping]`, `[data-swipe-direction]` (`up`, `down`, `left`, `right`) and the
  `--toast-swipe-movement-x` and `--toast-swipe-movement-y` variables, in pixels, while a swipe
  runs; `[data-swipe-direction]` stays while a swiped toast leaves;
- `--toast-index` on each shown toast (0 for the first child), and `[data-limited]` on the ones
  past the limit;
- `[data-expanded]` on the viewport while the pointer or focus is in it.

```css
.toast {
  translate: var(--toast-swipe-movement-x, 0) var(--toast-swipe-movement-y, 0);
  transition:
    opacity 200ms,
    translate 200ms;
}
.toast:is([data-starting-style], [data-ending-style]) {
  opacity: 0;
}
.toast[data-swiping] {
  transition: none;
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/toast.css`, in the `lu.core` layer, makes the viewport a box fixed to the window's
bottom end, without a popover's default border, padding or centring; hides the toasts past the
limit whatever display your CSS gives them; and sets `touch-action` on swipeable toasts, so a
swipe does not scroll the page along its axes.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key       | Does                                                                 |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| F6        | Focuses the toasts' region, when a toast shows.                      |
| Tab       | Moves through the toasts' buttons.                                   |
| Escape    | In a toast: closes it. On the region: returns focus to where it was. |
| Shift+Tab | On the region: returns focus to where it was.                        |

- **When the focused toast closes**, focus moves to the next toast's first button, or back to
  where it was before it entered the region (F6, Tab or a click).
- **Timers pause** while the pointer is over the region, while focus is in it, while the window is
  in the background and while the page is hidden; they resume with the time that was left.
- **Swipes** have a single-pointer alternative, the close button, and a keyboard one, Escape
  (WCAG 2.5.1 and 2.5.7). A swipe never starts on a button, link or field.
- **Time limits** (WCAG 2.2.1): a toast that times out must hold nothing the reader needs to act
  on. Give a toast with an action, or with something to read twice, `timeout: 0`.
- **Over a modal dialog**: a modal dialog makes everything outside it inert, so while one is open
  the region moves into it, and back when it closes. Toasts stay usable and announced.
- **Persistent**: a press in a toast does not close an open menu, popover or combobox.
