## Without JavaScript, and the element's script

What is server-rendered and what needs the client:

| Server HTML                                                                   | The element's script (2.3 kB, loaded once per page)                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The region and the toasts a page renders, with their text, roles and buttons. | The top layer (a manual popover), so toasts sit above dialogs and survive other popovers' light dismiss. |
| Toasts show at the window's bottom end (`toast.css`).                         | Timers, pausing, the limit, closing (button, Escape, swipe), F6, focus when a toast goes.                |
|                                                                               | The announcement mutation, and following modal dialogs.                                                  |

Without JavaScript a server-rendered toast stays on the page until the next one, and its close
button does nothing. The manager needs an island.

**Announcements.** Each toast is a live region, so screen readers read it without moving focus
(WCAG 4.1.3). Safari's VoiceOver misses the text of a region inserted with it, so 250ms after a
toast appears the script adds an invisible word joiner to it, a change VoiceOver reads, as Base UI
does. A toast in the page's HTML is announced the same way once the script runs.

## Browser support

- **Popover**: every current browser. Without it, toasts stay out of the top layer.
- **Invoker commands** (`Toast.Close`): Chrome 135, Firefox 144, Safari 26.2; elsewhere the
  script handles the close button's click.

## Related

- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling and the other components.
- [Dialog](dialog.md): a modal popup, which the toasts' region follows.
- [Data and actions](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/data-and-actions/): a form action's result, for a server-rendered toast.

<!-- source: toggle.md -->

# Toggle

> A two-state button (bold, mute, pin), after Base UI's Toggle: a native `<button type="button" aria-pressed>`. Its label stays the same; `aria-pressed` tells pressed from not. On its own the component presses it, in an island, and `bind:pressed` keeps a signal in sync; inside a [Toggle Group](toggle-group.md) the group presses it, on server pages too.

```ts
import { Toggle } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/toggle"
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Toggle aria-label="Bold">B</Toggle>
```

| Part     | Renders                                                     |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Toggle` | `<button type="button" aria-pressed="true">` (or `"false"`) |

## API

### Toggle

| Prop              | Type                         | Default |                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pressed`         | `boolean`                    |         | Presses or releases it when it changes. Pair it with `onPressedChange`. |
| `defaultPressed`  | `boolean`                    | `false` | Whether it starts pressed.                                              |
| `onPressedChange` | `(pressed: boolean) => void` |         | Called after the user presses or releases it.                           |
| `bind:pressed`    | `Signal<boolean>`            |         | Stands in for `pressed` and `onPressedChange`.                          |
| `value`           | `string`                     |         | Its identity in a Toggle Group's `value`.                               |

Every other native button prop passes through: `disabled`, `id`, `class`, `aria-label`, `aria-*`,
`onClick` (`type` is always `"button"`).

**Differences from Base UI's Toggle.** No `nativeButton` or `render`. `onPressedChange` gets the new
state only; in a group, a `pressedchange` listener can cancel the press with
`event.preventDefault()`.

## Example

```tsx check
import { Toggle } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function PinToggle() {
  const pinned = signal(false);
  return (
    <p>
      <Toggle bind:pressed={pinned} class="lu-toggle">
        Pin
      </Toggle>{" "}
      {pinned() ? "Pinned to the top." : "Not pinned."}
    </p>
  );
}
```

Give an icon-only toggle an `aria-label` that names the action ("Bold"), not its state.

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-toggle` on it: a bordered 36px button that, pressed, takes a
filled surface and a bar along its bottom edge, so the state shows by shape and not by colour alone.

**With your own CSS**, style the button and its state: `[aria-pressed="true"]`, `:hover`,
`:focus-visible`, `:disabled`.

Toggle ships no stylesheet: it needs none to work.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key           | Does                         |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Enter / Space | Presses or releases it.      |
| Tab           | Moves on: one tab stop each. |

In a Toggle Group, the group's arrow keys move between the toggles instead.

## Without JavaScript

A native button with its state in `aria-pressed` from the server. On its own, a Toggle is pressed
by the component, so it needs an island (its state is for your code anyway); in a Toggle Group the
group's script presses it on server pages too. For a value a form submits, use a
[Checkbox](checkbox.md) or a [Switch](switch.md).

## Browser support

`aria-pressed` on a native button: every browser and screen reader.

## Related

- [Toggle Group](toggle-group.md): toggles that share one value, one or several pressed.
- [Switch](switch.md): an on/off setting submitted with a form.
- [Button](button.md): a plain button.

<!-- source: toggle-group.md -->

# Toggle Group

> A set of [Toggles](toggle.md) with one value, after Base UI's ToggleGroup: text alignment (one pressed at a time) or text style (several). `<lu-toggle-group role="group">` presses its toggles and gives the group one tab stop that the arrow keys, Home and End move, following the orientation and the direction, on server pages and in islands. `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync.

```ts
import { Toggle, ToggleGroup } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/toggle-group"
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<ToggleGroup aria-label="Alignment">
  <Toggle value="left">Left</Toggle>
  <Toggle value="center">Center</Toggle>
</ToggleGroup>
```

| Part          | Renders                                                                |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ToggleGroup` | `<lu-toggle-group role="group" data-orientation>`; `multiple` if set   |
| `Toggle`      | `<button aria-pressed value>`; the group's tab stop has `tabindex="0"` |

## API

### ToggleGroup

| Prop            | Type                           | Default        |                                                                            |
| --------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string[]`                     |                | Presses these toggles when it changes. Pair it with `onValueChange`.       |
| `defaultValue`  | `string[]`                     | `[]`           | The toggles pressed at first.                                              |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string[]) => void`    |                | Called after the user presses or releases a toggle.                        |
| `bind:value`    | `Signal<string[]>`             |                | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                 |
| `multiple`      | `boolean`                      | `false`        | Several toggles can be pressed; otherwise pressing one releases the other. |
| `orientation`   | `"horizontal"` \| `"vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Which arrow keys move focus.                                               |
| `loopFocus`     | `boolean`                      | `true`         | The arrow keys go from the last toggle to the first, and back.             |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`                      | `false`        | Disables every toggle.                                                     |

Every other prop passes through to `<lu-toggle-group>`: `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `id`,
`class`. Name the group with one of the first two.

Each toggle's `value` is its identity in the group; its `onPressedChange` still fires. A
`pressedchange` event (`detail.pressed`) bubbles from a toggle before it changes, and
`event.preventDefault()` cancels the change.

**Differences from Base UI's ToggleGroup.** No `render`. Focus follows `tabindex` on the toggles
(roving), as Base UI does; disabled toggles are natively `disabled`, so focus skips them.

## Example

```tsx check
import { Toggle, ToggleGroup } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function TextAlignment() {
  const align = signal<string[]>(["left"]);
  return (
    <p>
      <ToggleGroup aria-label="Text alignment" bind:value={align} class="lu-toggle-group">
        <Toggle value="left" class="lu-toggle">
          Left
        </Toggle>
        <Toggle value="center" class="lu-toggle">
          Center
        </Toggle>
        <Toggle value="right" class="lu-toggle">
          Right
        </Toggle>
      </ToggleGroup>{" "}
      Aligned: {align()[0] ?? "none"}.
    </p>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-toggle-group` on the group and `lu-toggle` on each toggle: the
toggles in a row with a small gap, in a column when `data-orientation="vertical"`.

**With your own CSS**, style the group by `[data-orientation]` and `[multiple]`, and the toggles by
`[aria-pressed="true"]`, `:focus-visible` and `:disabled`.

Toggle Group ships no stylesheet: it needs none to work.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key                      | Does                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab                      | Enters the group on the last focused toggle (at first, the first pressed or the first enabled), and leaves it. |
| Arrow Right / Arrow Left | Horizontal: the next or previous toggle (swapped right to left), looping.                                      |
| Arrow Down / Arrow Up    | Vertical: the next or previous toggle, looping.                                                                |
| Home / End               | The first or last enabled toggle.                                                                              |
| Enter / Space            | Presses or releases the focused toggle.                                                                        |

Arrows move focus without pressing, and skip disabled toggles. With `loopFocus={false}` they stop at
the ends.

Inside a [Toolbar](toolbar.md), the group still presses its toggles, but the toolbar's arrow keys
and single tab stop take over: the toggles are toolbar items.

## Without JavaScript, and the element's script

The server HTML has each toggle's `aria-pressed` and the tab stop. `<lu-toggle-group>`'s script
(0.8 kB brotli) presses the toggles and moves focus, on server pages and in islands; with no script
at all the toggles show their state but do not change. For values a form submits, use a
[Checkbox Group](checkbox-group.md) or a [Radio](radio-group.md) group.

## Browser support

Custom elements and `aria-pressed`: every supported browser.

## Related

- [Toggle](toggle.md): one toggle, on its own or in a group.
- [Radio](radio-group.md): one choice submitted with a form.
- [Tabs](tabs.md): toggles that switch panels.

<!-- source: toolbar.md -->

# Toolbar

> A set of controls with one tab stop, after Base UI's Toolbar and the APG toolbar pattern: `<lu-toolbar role="toolbar">` moves focus between its items with the arrow keys, Home and End, following the orientation and the text direction. Its items are native: buttons that stay focusable when disabled, links, inputs, and the toggles of a [Toggle Group](toggle-group.md) inside it. The server HTML has the single tab stop already; a 0.9 kB script moves it.

```ts
import { Toolbar } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/toolbar"
import "@lumiose/ui/toolbar.css"; // or "@lumiose/ui/styles.css" for every component
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Toolbar.Root>
  <Toolbar.Button />
  <Toolbar.Link />
  <Toolbar.Separator />
  <Toolbar.Group>
    <Toolbar.Button />
  </Toolbar.Group>
  <Toolbar.Input />
</Toolbar.Root>
```

| Part        | Renders                                                                                            |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`      | `<lu-toolbar role="toolbar" aria-orientation data-orientation>`                                    |
| `Button`    | A [Button](button.md): `<button type="button">`, `aria-disabled` when disabled (still focusable)   |
| `Link`      | `<a>`                                                                                              |
| `Input`     | `<input>`, `aria-disabled` and read-only when disabled (still focusable)                           |
| `Group`     | `<div role="group">`                                                                               |
| `Separator` | A [Separator](separator.md), `<hr>`, across the toolbar: vertical in a row, horizontal in a column |

Every item gets `tabindex="0"` (the first) or `"-1"` and `data-orientation`. Name the toolbar with
`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

## API

### Toolbar.Root

| Prop          | Type                         | Default        |                                                                        |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | A row moved through with Left and Right, or a column with Up and Down. |
| `loopFocus`   | `boolean`                    | `true`         | The arrow keys go from the last item to the first, and back.           |
| `disabled`    | `boolean`                    | `false`        | Disables every item; they stay focusable.                              |

### Toolbar.Button, Toolbar.Input and Toolbar.Group

| Prop                    | Type      | Default |                                                                    |
| ----------------------- | --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `disabled`              | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the item (a Group: its items).                            |
| `focusableWhenDisabled` | `boolean` | `true`  | Button and Input: disabled, they stay focusable (`aria-disabled`). |

Every other native prop passes through. A `ToggleGroup` inside a toolbar keeps pressing its
toggles but leaves the arrow keys and the tab stop to the toolbar; a Menu or Popover trigger inside
it is an item too (the script gives it its `tabindex`).

**Differences from Base UI's Toolbar.** No `render` or `nativeButton`: put other triggers
(`Menu.Trigger`, `Popover.Trigger`) in the toolbar directly. Disabled items are `aria-disabled`
rather than `data-disabled` and `data-focusable`.

## Example

```tsx check
import { Toggle, ToggleGroup, Toolbar } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function FormattingToolbar() {
  return (
    <Toolbar.Root aria-label="Formatting" class="lu-toolbar">
      <ToggleGroup aria-label="Text style" multiple class="lu-toggle-group">
        <Toggle value="bold" class="lu-toggle">
          Bold
        </Toggle>
        <Toggle value="italic" class="lu-toggle">
          Italic
        </Toggle>
      </ToggleGroup>
      <Toolbar.Separator />
      <Toolbar.Button class="lu-button">Undo</Toolbar.Button>
      <Toolbar.Button class="lu-button" disabled>
        Redo
      </Toolbar.Button>
      <Toolbar.Link href="/help">Help</Toolbar.Link>
    </Toolbar.Root>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-toolbar` on `Root`: a bordered row (a column when vertical)
that wraps on narrow screens, groups in rows, separators as 1px lines across it, links as tall as
the buttons. Style the items with their own classes (`lu-button`, `lu-toggle`, `lu-input`).

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class`, `[data-orientation]`, `[role="group"]`,
`hr` and the items' `[aria-disabled="true"]` and `:focus-visible`.

`@lumiose/ui/toolbar.css` makes `<lu-toolbar>` a block box, as Base UI's `<div>`.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key                      | Does                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab                      | Into the toolbar on the last focused item (at first, the first), and out of it. |
| Arrow Right / Arrow Left | In a row: the next or previous item (swapped right to left), looping.           |
| Arrow Down / Arrow Up    | In a column: the next or previous item, looping.                                |
| Home / End               | The first or last item.                                                         |
| Enter / Space            | Acts on the item: presses a button or a toggle, follows a link.                 |

Natively disabled controls are skipped. A control keeps the keys it needs: a text field its
caret's Left and Right (focus moves on at its start or end) and Home and End, a number field or a
slider its arrows, a select Up and Down. Base UI advises at most one input, last.

## Without JavaScript, and the element's script

The server HTML is a labelled toolbar with one tab stop, on its first item. `<lu-toolbar>`'s script
(0.9 kB brotli with Button's) moves focus with the keys and keeps the tab stop on the last focused
item.

## Browser support

Custom elements and `role="toolbar"`: every supported browser and screen reader.

<!-- source: tooltip.md -->

# Tooltip

> A short tip next to its trigger, on hover or keyboard focus: a native `popover="hint"` with `role="tooltip"`, placed with CSS anchor positioning. The trigger is described by the tip in server HTML, so screen readers announce it without hovering; a 1.5 kB script opens and closes it as Base UI's tooltip does. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.

```ts
import { Tooltip } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/tooltip"
import "@lumiose/ui/tooltip.css"; // places the tip next to its trigger
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Tooltip.Root>
  <Tooltip.Trigger />
  <Tooltip.Popup />
</Tooltip.Root>
```

| Part      | Renders                                                                                                     |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`    | No element. Holds the ids the parts share.                                                                  |
| `Trigger` | `<button type="button" aria-describedby="…">`, with an `anchor-name` in its `style`.                        |
| `Popup`   | `<span popover="hint" role="tooltip" data-side="…" data-align="…">`: a `<span>`, so it fits in a paragraph. |

**Accessibility model.** The tooltip follows the
[WAI-ARIA tooltip pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tooltip/): the tip is the
trigger's description, always, not only while it shows. It is not its name: give an icon-only
trigger an `aria-label` (Base UI asks the same).

## API

### Tooltip.Root

| Prop                    | Type                      | Default |                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`                  | `boolean`                 |         | Opens or closes the tip when it changes, in the browser.                                                                                                                                             |
| `onOpenChange`          | `(open: boolean) => void` |         | Called after the tip opens or closes, whatever did it: hover, focus, Escape, `open`.                                                                                                                 |
| `bind:open`             | `Signal<boolean>`         |         | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`.                                                                                                                                                             |
| `disabled`              | `boolean`                 | `false` | Hover and focus do not open the tip; `open` still does.                                                                                                                                              |
| `disableHoverablePopup` | `boolean`                 | `false` | Closes the tip as soon as the pointer leaves the trigger, instead of letting it move onto the tip. WCAG 1.4.13 asks for hoverable content: use it only for tips that cover something the user needs. |

### Tooltip.Trigger

| Prop           | Type      | Default |                                                                        |
| -------------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `delay`        | `number`  | `600`   | How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the tip opens, in ms. |
| `closeDelay`   | `number`  | `0`     | How long the tip stays after the pointer leaves, in ms.                |
| `closeOnClick` | `boolean` | `true`  | A click (or Enter, or Space) on the trigger closes the tip.            |

The trigger takes a `<button>`'s props too; an `aria-describedby` you pass is kept, after the tip.
These props reach the client script as attributes of the trigger: `data-delay`,
`data-close-delay`, `data-close-on-click="false"`, and `data-trigger-disabled` from `Root`'s
`disabled`.

### Tooltip.Popup

The placement props of [Popover.Popup](popover.md#popoverpopup): `side` (default `"top"`),
`align`, `sideOffset` and `alignOffset`.

## Example

```tsx check
import { Tooltip } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function BoldButton() {
  return (
    <Tooltip.Root>
      <Tooltip.Trigger class="lu-button" aria-label="Bold">
        B
      </Tooltip.Trigger>
      <Tooltip.Popup class="lu-tooltip">Bold (Ctrl+B)</Tooltip.Popup>
    </Tooltip.Root>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-tooltip` on `Popup`: inverted colours, a 6px gap and a fade.

**With your own CSS**, style the tip through `class`, `:popover-open`, `[data-side]` and
`[data-align]`, and the offsets through `--lu-side-offset` and `--lu-align-offset`, as for
[Popover](popover.md#styling). `@lumiose/ui/tooltip.css` holds the placement both share.

## Keyboard and focus

The [WAI-ARIA tooltip pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tooltip/), with Base UI's
and Zag's opening rules:

| Key          | Does                                                                             |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab          | Focusing the trigger from the keyboard opens the tip at once; leaving closes it. |
| Escape       | Closes the tip, and only the tip: a dialog or popover around it stays open.      |
| Enter, Space | Activate the trigger and close the tip, unless `closeOnClick={false}`.           |

- **Opens** after `delay` of hover with a mouse or a pen, or at once on keyboard focus
  (`:focus-visible`). A touch never opens it, and neither does the focus a mouse click gives.
- **One at a time.** Within 400 ms of another tooltip closing, or while one is open, the next one
  opens without delay, so moving along a toolbar reads each tip.
- **A press before the delay** cancels the opening.
- **Closes** on Escape (only the tip: a dialog or popover around it stays open), on a press, on a
  click of the trigger (unless `closeOnClick={false}`), on blur, and when something around the
  trigger scrolls.
- **Hoverable** (WCAG 1.4.13): the pointer can move from the trigger onto the tip, across the gap,
  and the tip stays; it closes `closeDelay` after the pointer leaves both.

A tooltip inside a popover keeps the popover open, and one inside a dialog belongs inside its
`Popup` (everything outside a modal dialog is inert).

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

Without JavaScript the tip never shows, but the trigger keeps its description: screen readers
announce it. A page that renders a `Tooltip` loads a 1.5 kB (brotli) module once, without the
Lumiose runtime; islands bundle it. It opens and closes every tooltip on the page, and places them
in browsers without CSS anchor positioning.

## Browser support

- **`popover="hint"`**: Chrome and Edge from 133 (complete in 151), Firefox from 149 (complete in
  153). Safari reads it as `popover="manual"`: the client script does the same work there.
- **CSS anchor positioning**: Chrome and Edge 125, Firefox 147, Safari 26. Elsewhere the client
  script places the tip.
